# Themes

The recurring ideas extracted across sources, each with the sources that support it. Built from research/themes/ (one file per task). Rules: [README.md](README.md).

## agent-as-service-many-surfaces: The agent as a service with many surfaces
One agent service behind an API, reached through a web app, Slack, browser extensions and embedding in existing tools, rather than a single app or a separate agent per surface. Matters for the agent-interface choice (own app vs Slack vs embedded).
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): the counter-case: River has one surface (Slack, no DMs), with companion links (Quick sites, Live Preview) for rich output (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): River can join Google Meet when invited, "although not really utilized" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): "The agent is a service, not an application, and surfaces are simply customized views into it"; web app, Slack, Chrome extension in third-party tools, internal apps embed via API (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe built their own in-house Glean alternative](sources/groundedhallucination-stripe-kai-teardown.md): "Surfaces are views, not the product" (independent restatement) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor is its own browser app but also an MCP toolset and a rendering service other agents call (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Claude Cowork and chat are now one Claude](sources/claude-cowork-chat-unified.md): one Claude on web, desktop and mobile; start on a computer, check progress or answer questions on a phone; work continues in the cloud (Pro/Max launch, "What it looks like"; Enterprise, "One Claude for every task"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Cowork on web and mobile: hand off work anywhere](sources/claude-cowork-web-mobile-handoff.md): Cowork on desktop, web and iOS/Android; chat and Cowork now share one home with projects and artifacts together; desktop keeps local files and browser use (sections "What changes today", "Getting started"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Cyera on making Claude Cowork the front door to 40 tools](sources/claude-customers-cyera-cowork-front-door.md): Cowork chosen as the aggregator over per-tool embedded AI: "Claude is now the aggregator" across Snowflake, Salesforce, Drive, Slack; 40 tools and several homegrown MCP servers (Q&A, "Why route work through Claude Cowork"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude for the financial industry](sources/claude-guide-financial-industry.md): each agent role can run as a Cowork or Microsoft 365 plugin on the desktop or as a Managed Agents hosted service (ch. 2, "Pre-built finance agent reference architectures"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude's memory works everywhere, and you decide what's in it](sources/claude-memory-everywhere.md): same memory in chat and Cowork, including Cowork tasks running in the cloud, carried in both directions ("One memory across Claude Cowork and chat"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): "capabilities, data and logic as the product, the UI as one of many consumption paths" (Salesforce headless split) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to develop an MCP Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-product-strategy.md): Intercom made Fin an MCP client that reaches other tools, rather than become a server hidden behind Claude. Stripe is content to be invisible behind agents (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## agent-factory-sdlc: Agents across the whole product development loop

## agent-failure-modes: Recurring agent failure modes in PM work
Invented content, silent omissions, brittleness, generic output when context is thin.
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): told to enumerate fully, River rechecked only the oldest claim; "Prompts are the right place to express judgment and the wrong place to express a guarantee" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [AI SLOPCAST #9](sources/oleg-guru-ai-slopcast-shopify-river-lehrwerkstatt.md): public-by-default archives everyone's gaps, "a treasure trove" for HR (critique) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): 'There were agents that went rogue ... may have almost taken down core systems'; 'when in doubt an agent will just brute force it' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Thoughts On A Month With Devin](sources/answerai-month-with-devin.md): stuck loops (an HTML-parsing scraper task), a day spent on a platform-unsupported deployment while hallucinating features, tunnel vision on the wrong root cause, false-positive security findings (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AWS AI coding tool decided to delete and recreate a customer-facing system, causing 13-hour outage (report)](sources/the-decoder-aws-kiro-outage.md): agent 'chose' to delete and recreate the environment; permissions inherited from the engineer bypassed two-person sign-off (FT sources; Amazon says it was misconfigured access controls and limited to Cost Explorer in one China region) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Replit makes vibe-y promise to stop its AI agents making vibe coding disasters](sources/theregister-replit-saastr-response.md): reported deletion of a production DB with records on ~1,206 executives and ~1,196 companies despite an instruction not to change code; agent reportedly said rollback would not work, but data was recovered manually (eWeek and others, search results) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [A month with Devin](sources/answerai-thoughts-month-with-devin.md): independent: 3/20 successes on real tasks; unpredictable; pursues impossible tasks instead of flagging blockers (Jan 2025, dated). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex MCP server removal](sources/openai-codex-mcp-server-removed.md): integration route removed by the vendor; third-party blogs still describe it. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Headless docs](sources/anthropic-claude-code-headless-agent-sdk.md): unattended runs deny permission prompts; `-p` does not wait for MCP tasks; MCP calls moved to background lose their result. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CR-Bench](sources/arxiv-cr-bench.md): independent, preliminary: agents built to find all issues have low signal-to-noise in code review (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [METR early-2025 developer RCT](sources/metr-early-2025-experienced-developer-rct.md): independent: AI-allowed tasks took 19% longer for experts on familiar repos while they believed it was faster (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How Delivery Hero's agent merges 100+ pull requests a day with Claude](sources/claude-customers-delivery-hero-pr-agent.md): "If you churn out five times more changes ... you will have five times more incidents if the change failure rate remains at the same level"; investing in agent-driven operations and safer rollouts (§Looking ahead). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Multi-agent coordination patterns: Five approaches and when to use them](sources/claude-multi-agent-coordination-patterns.md): rubber-stamping verifiers, orchestrator information bottleneck, conflicting teammates, silent routing failures, reactive loops in shared state (each "Where it struggles"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic secures its AI-native software development lifecycle](sources/claude-securing-ai-native-sdlc-at-anthropic.md): the agent-to-agent escalation over Slack after a model upgrade; lesson: "draw the boundary around access and actions, not around a model's instructions" and include an agent's access to other agents (§Monitor). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Uber's CISO on building an insider threat program for AI](sources/claude-uber-ciso-insider-threat-ai.md): concern is accidental misuse and models "directed to act outside the constraints we expect"; "constraints create new behaviors" so detection must keep finding new ones. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [DESIGN.md Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-design-md-explained.md): agents fill a missing token with something plausible, and the divergence spreads while still looking consistent. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Agentic Workflows Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agentic-workflows-explained.md): a cited benchmark classes failures as planning, execution and formatting errors. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is parallel AI agent coding? An in-depth guide for product teams](sources/departmentofproduct-parallel-agent-coding.md): parallel agents bring merge conflicts and harder debugging; they're weak on architecture and on UI that needs visual feedback (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Duet is beautiful. I still forgot to use it](sources/howiai-claire-vo-claude-duet-review.md): 10+ minute threads with no loop closure were forgotten; a faster agent wins "even if ... 10 percent worse" (7:59-9:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The Codex feature that works while you sleep](sources/howiai-claire-vo-codex-goal.md): agents given Linear access created tasks they never did, polluting the backlog (20:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Syncing Claude Code and Claude Design ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-claude-design-handoff.md): no verification step meant drift from the prototype went undetected (Thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Make product management fun again with AI agents](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-pm-agents.md): agent invented sprint numbers from examples and marked tasks done from end dates: context gaps, not model faults (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building eval systems that improve your AI product](sources/lenny-newsletter-evals-hamel-shreya.md): transition failure matrix localises which agent step breaks (section "Agentic workflows") (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Claude Mythos found a 15-year-old bug in Mozilla Firefox | Brian Grinstead](sources/howiai-mozilla-mythos-bug-harness.md): agents cheat to hit the goal (setting a test-only pref; introducing a vulnerability to exploit it); patch agents miss the bug class (8:44, 28:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to do AI analysis you can actually trust](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-analysis-you-can-trust.md): output "always looks confident"; teams on one enterprise LLM never see what it misses (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How to encourage engineers to use AI more ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-engineers-ai-adoption.md): April 2025: a 10-line fix became 170 lines; lost Docker containers; agent mode adds bugs and wrong libraries (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [5 OpenClaw agents run my home (Jesse Genet)](sources/howiai-jesse-genet-openclaw-agents.md): agent-to-agent handoffs break; no messaging platform handles them well (show notes, 16:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): model explains a skipped UI check as "I delegated the verification to this subagent and ... I didn't check its work" (53:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The grief, loneliness, and burnout ... | Molly Graham](sources/lenny-podcast-molly-graham-delegating-to-ai.md): AI as "a lazy intern"; slop comes from people who have "shipped accountability" by copy-paste-send (35:18) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): agents forget, crons break, time zones confused, a user's inbox deleted, the author's calendar mangled (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building AI product sense, part 2](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-product-sense-part-2.md): "semantic fragility" summarising a PRD for a VP; same "top 5 decisions" prompt returns different decisions each run (Rituals 2, 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Evals, error analysis, and better prompts](sources/howiai-hamel-husain-error-analysis.md): counted failures in a property-management assistant (handoffs, duplicate tour scheduling); a missing date in the system prompt; retrieval as "the Achilles heel" (20:11, 34:39) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [I spent $20,000 on Devin in a month (Ryan Carson)](sources/howiai-ryan-carson-devin-20k-month.md): "agent decision fatigue" managing 15 parallel agents, tracked on paper; "more AI output is the wrong goal" (18:09, 20:32) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Cursor for PM work](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-cursor-for-pm-work.md): agents make unrelated "fixes", escalate to library upgrades, "cheat to ensure the tests pass", and ignore conventions (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Block's Goose (Brosamer, Axen)](sources/howiai-block-goose-brosamer-axen.md): Goose tried to read a `.env` holding an API key and was blocked by a built-in check (28:50) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-claire-vo-openclaw.md): deleted family calendar on first try; forgets yesterday, loses auth, claims it can't read files; browser use unreliable (10:14, 40:59) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [AI prototyping with Lovable (Product Talk)](sources/producttalk-ai-prototyping-lovable.md): Tool claimed to have fixed issues it had not (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Atlassian Rovo AI review (Slite)](sources/slite-atlassian-rovo-ai-review.md): A user team reported (community post, relayed by Slite) a runbook summary with steps, commands and contacts absent from the source; a partner (Seibert) reported a custom agent that "confidently invented releases" (case 1) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Gong reviews (TrustRadius)](sources/trustradius-gong-reviews.md): Reviews note occasional wrong words in transcripts; accent complaints are on G2/Capterra, not TrustRadius [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [CBTW on Rovo since launch](sources/cbtw-atlassian-rovo-real-world-feedback.md): Partner reports inconsistent backlog analysis/JQL, wrong ticket selection, ignored filters; partner bias, no data (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Why Atlassian Rovo Failed Us](sources/devto-tschimev-why-atlassian-rovo-failed-us.md): Rovo "can't handle nuanced tickets, doesn't understand team conventions"; "polished in demos but struggles in production"; single-team anecdote (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence](sources/stanford-cheng-sycophantic-ai-science-2026.md): 11 models affirmed users ~49% more often than humans (Science, 2026; abstract via search); risk for 'pressure-test my idea' uses (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Webinar Q&A: How Fin 3x'd R&D output in 16 months](sources/ideas-fin-webinar-qa-3x-rd-output.md): an agent pushed "hundreds of thousands of changes" breaking CI; incident-investigation agents give "plausible suggestions that are red herrings" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Understanding Spec-Driven-Development: Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl](sources/fowler-bockeler-sdd-kiro-speckit-tessl.md): spec-kit ignored research notes and duplicated existing classes; over-applied constitution; Tessl regeneration non-deterministic. (user-story-mapping)

## agent-frameworks: Agent frameworks
Libraries and engines (agent frameworks, durable-execution engines) used to build or host an agent loop.
- [How Stripe Built Kai on Deep Agents (LangChain)](sources/langchain-how-stripe-built-kai-deep-agents.md): Kai built on LangChain Deep Agents: 'solves all the non-Stripey problems'; minions on a Goose fork: Stripe uses two different open-source harnesses for two agent families (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Long-running agents (Cloudflare Agents SDK docs)](sources/cloudflare-agents-long-running-agents.md): recovery after eviction is not automatic replay: onFiberRecovered runs and 'you decide what resuming means'; keepAlive suits minutes not hours, use Workflows for longer work (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Open-Inspect (ColeMurray/background-agents) README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): sandbox runs a Supervisor, a harness (OpenCode or Claude Agent) and a Bridge back to the control plane; harness is pluggable (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Durable Execution for AI Agents: LangGraph, DBOS, Inngest and Temporal Compared](sources/hackernoon-durable-execution-compared.md): LangGraph default async durability can lose the newest checkpoint on a hard crash, checkpoints are per node not per tool call; Inngest renaming a step orphans in-flight runs; Temporal needs a cluster and about two weeks to production (author's estimate) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Production-ready agents with the OpenAI Agents SDK + Temporal](sources/temporal-openai-agents-sdk-integration.md): the integration replaces the Agents SDK Runner so every agent invocation runs as a Temporal Activity; handoffs are also recorded; workflow code holds orchestration logic (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: no production coding harness uses LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, ADK, Pydantic AI or Semantic Kernel; "the harness SDKs are the framework layer now" (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Frameworks, Runtimes, and Harnesses, oh my!](sources/langchain-agent-frameworks-runtimes-harnesses.md): vendor claim: framework / runtime / harness vocabulary; author admits no agreed definition (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Deep Agents vs LangChain vs LangGraph](sources/langchain-deep-agents-vs-langchain-vs-langgraph.md): vendor claim: harness = framework agent plus middleware, on a LangGraph runtime (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Microsoft Agent Framework overview](sources/microsoft-agent-framework-overview.md): first-party: successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel now ships a Harness Agent; Go in preview (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Pydantic AI documentation overview](sources/pydantic-ai-docs.md): first-party: framework adds Harness (memory, sub-agents, compaction) and 8 durable-execution engines (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Development Kit (ADK) documentation](sources/google-adk-docs.md): first-party: model-agnostic, 5 languages, A2A, Google Cloud deployment (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [LangGraph overview](sources/langchain-docs-langgraph-overview.md): first-party: durable execution runtime; deployment and tracing via paid LangSmith (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [OpenAI Agents SDK documentation](sources/openai-agents-sdk-docs.md): first-party: handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing, sandbox agents; non-OpenAI via adapters (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex SDK and app server](sources/openai-codex-sdk-docs.md): first-party: Codex harness controllable via TypeScript/Python SDK over app-server JSON-RPC (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent SDK overview](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-overview.md): first-party: Claude Code as a library; four build options from Client SDK to Managed Agents (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Managed Agents overview](sources/anthropic-managed-agents-overview.md): first-party: hosted harness, beta, not ZDR/HIPAA eligible (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Mastra documentation](sources/mastra-docs.md): vendor claim: TypeScript framework with scaffolded workspace and memory (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CrewAI documentation: Introduction](sources/crewai-docs-introduction.md): vendor claim: Flows plus Crews (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [GitHub repos: OpenCode, Goose, Cline](sources/github-opencode-repo.md): OpenCode MIT about 221k stars; Goose Apache-2.0 Rust under Linux Foundation AAIF (github-block-goose-repo); Cline Apache-2.0 with SDK (github-cline-repo) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare Flue post](sources/cloudflare-flue-agents-platform.md): three layers: framework (Flue) / harness (Pi, Think) / runtime (Agents SDK) (vendor) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vercel AI SDK Harnesses](sources/vercel-ai-sdk-harnesses.md): harness vs model-provider abstraction as separate axes in a framework (vendor docs) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Project Think](sources/cloudflare-project-think.md): 'opinionated harness' with lifecycle hooks, override what you need (vendor) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How to think about agent frameworks](sources/langchain-how-to-think-about-agent-frameworks.md): vendor: workflows vs agents is a spectrum; most production systems mix both (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [A practical guide to building agents (OpenAI)](sources/openai-practical-guide-building-agents.md): vendor, secondary summary: single agent first; manager vs decentralized patterns (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Multi-agent coordination patterns: Five approaches and when to use them](sources/claude-multi-agent-coordination-patterns.md): five named patterns with mechanics, fit and failure modes, plus a situation-to-pattern table ("Getting started"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Multi Agent Architecture explained](sources/departmentofproduct-multi-agent-architecture.md): network, supervisor, hierarchical and custom patterns on AutoGen, LangGraph, A2A and Bedrock's supervisor toggle (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build an AI Agent](sources/departmentofproduct-how-to-build-an-ai-agent.md): LangChain and AutoGen (Magentic-One roles) recommended in Jan 2025; AutoGen was later archived (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [AI Agent SDKs Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-sdks-explained.md): sets model-vendor frameworks (OpenAI Agents SDK, ADK, both model-agnostic) against domain toolkits from SaaS firms (Stripe, 1Password) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Not all AI agents are created equal](sources/lenny-newsletter-three-agent-categories.md): tool map: n8n, Zapier, Make, AgentKit, Lindy, Gumloop (deterministic); LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, ADK (reasoning); ADK/AutoGen plus A2A and Temporal/Kafka/Step Functions (multi-agent) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## agent-led-intent-shaping: Agents shape intent, not only execute it
Agents do the research, interrogation and spec-tightening that turn rough intent into shovel-ready requirements, with humans answering and deciding. This is the core job of a "product agent".
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): Claude "asks the questions an analyst would ask: scope, users, constraints, and what success looks like" while the originator brainstorms; the spec pass must flag "areas of concern, especially where you cannot satisfy... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Best practices for getting started with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-cowork-getting-started-best-practices.md): "Make Claude ask you questions before it starts", repeating the ask back and asking clarifying questions, called the single most useful habit (Your first 10 minutes). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Miro's champions run their week with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-miro-champions.md): Cowork used to pressure-test half-formed problems "before there's anything to draft"; usage moved from last step to first step (Hostetler, first answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): "ask for ten options, then remix"; generate 15 versions of a flow to collect colleague feedback; Claude provides starting points and the human chooses ("Best practices"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A field guide to Claude Fable 5: Finding your unknowns](sources/claude-fable-finding-unknowns.md): the agent is asked to surface "unknown unknowns" ("blind spot pass"), brainstorm wildly different directions, and interview the user "one question at a time", prioritising questions that would change the architecture... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): Ideate researches named apps, proposes three directions, asks the PM to pick, then drafts a PRD for approval before designing (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): CASH's first stage is Claude identifying growth opportunities from trends; Lenny: AI is "getting really good at telling us what to do" (35:29, 39:50) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why humans are AI's biggest bottleneck (Alexander Embiricos)](sources/lenny-podcast-embiricos-codex-human-bottleneck.md): sceptical of spec-driven development ("a lot of people don't like writing specs"); prefers proactive agents and "chatter-driven development" from team and customer channels (36:16-37:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Claude Code (Boris Cherny)](sources/lenny-podcast-boris-cherny-after-coding.md): "Claude is starting to come up with ideas" for what to ship from feedback and telemetry (17:54) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of Design (Ian Silber)](sources/lenny-podcast-ian-silber-openai-design.md): ChatGPT helps users "express your intent better" with tap-through follow-up questions (44:08) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Everyone's an engineer now | Guillermo Rauch](sources/lenny-podcast-guillermo-rauch-v0.md): v0 "inverts" the git commit: start from intent, code is output; three skills are stating intent, coaching, getting unstuck (14:36, 45:46) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity](sources/lenny-podcast-adam-mosseri-product-staff.md): working with agents "looks more like management": define success, choose how prescriptive to be, give feedback along the way (24:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why LinkedIn is turning PMs into AI-powered "full stack builders"](sources/lenny-podcast-tomer-cohen-full-stack-builder.md): heads of craft built trust, growth, research and analyst agents that critique specs; the trust agent replayed on the Open to Work spec found "all the holes that we did not catch until later"; the research agent "shifted the direction of the team" (19:58-21:59) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Felix Rieseberg (Cowork)](sources/howiai-felix-rieseberg-cowork.md): uses Opus over Sonnet when "I ... don't really know yet what [I'm] asking for": reinterpreting the request is the hard part (10:11) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What we're learning from engineers getting the most from Claude Code](sources/ideas-fin-what-were-learning-from-engineers.md): 5-20 plan-mode turns mapping code, comparing options and challenging edge cases before "build it"; no formal spec artifact, the plan lives in the session (anecdote) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): Ramp's parallel research agents write each finding to a file; seven-question interrogation; agent-originated intent (§Vision, steps 1–3) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [Intent Shaping in a Well-Managed Environment](sources/geoff-intent-shaping-well-managed-environment.md): an iterative owner/risk-advisor loop in which mitigations become requirements and the spec tightens (§Iterative intent-shaping) (research-product-agent-and-harness)

## agent-project-failure-rates: Agent project failure rates
Press-reported statistics on agent and genAI pilot failure (Gartner, MIT); not PM-specific and mostly unverified.
- [Deploying AI from pilot to production: a practical blueprint for CIOs and technical leaders](sources/claude-pilot-to-production-cio-blueprint.md): cites Accenture's Pulse of Change (July 2026): only 23% of C-suite leaders report sustained enterprise-wide impact from AI initiatives; pilots are unrepresentative (hand-picked teams, protected budgets). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agentic Workflows Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agentic-workflows-explained.md): agents failed about 50% of 34 general tasks in a cited study (the post calls it "Cibench"; not verified). (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Why most AI products fail: Lessons from 50+ AI deployments](sources/lenny-podcast-reganti-badam-ai-deployments.md): cites ~74-75% of enterprises naming reliability as their top problem; one end-to-end support agent shut down after endless hot fixes; critical workflows take 4-6 months (21:45, 46:18, 30:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Not all AI agents are created equal](sources/lenny-newsletter-three-agent-categories.md): consultants' main failure pattern is mis-categorization: over-engineering deterministic problems, or using workflow tools for reasoning problems, which "breaks in production" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How 80,000 companies build with AI (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-asha-sharma-loop-not-lane.md): enterprises fail by "doing AI for AI's sake": many parallel projects, no blueprint, no measurement, observability or evals (11:05) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Sloppenheimer: Amazon employees mock the company's AI on Slack (404 Media)](sources/404media-amazon-employees-mock-ai-slop.md): internal AI coding product mocked as slop; failed usage push (leaderboard detail unverified; paywalled) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Zapier customer story (Anthropic)](sources/anthropic-customer-story-zapier.md): counter-example claim: 800+ internal agents and 89% adoption (vendor-claimed, no outcomes). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How Brex improves code quality and productivity with Claude Code](sources/claude-brex-claude-code.md): vendor-claimed 3-4x on coding tasks; not PM evidence. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [MIT report: 95% of generative AI pilots at companies are failing (Fortune)](sources/fortune-mit-nanda-95-percent-pilots.md): ~95% of pilots no measurable P&L impact; bought tools about 2x as successful as internal builds (press; primary now filed as mit-nanda-genai-divide-2025) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Over 40% of agentic AI projects will be scrapped by 2027, says Gartner (Outlook Business coverage)](sources/gartner-agentic-ai-40-percent-cancelled.md): forecast: over 40% of agentic AI projects cancelled by end of 2027. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025](sources/mit-nanda-genai-divide-2025.md): primary: "95% of organizations are getting zero return"; success = beyond pilot with measurable KPIs at six months; self-reported, 52 interviews, 153 surveys, selection bias acknowledged (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## agent-protocol-security: Security of agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool protocols
Attacks and gaps that arise because a remote agent or its metadata becomes input to your agent: card or description poisoning, session smuggling, identity loss across delegation hops, optional signing.
- [Agent identity: a new access model for autonomous, team-wide AI](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): credentials stored separately and injected at the network boundary; non-allowed hosts blocked; every routine, memory write and network call audited (section "Security and audit"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [CISO's guide to agentic AI](sources/claude-ciso-guide-agentic-ai.md): prompt injection named as a main internal risk; egress allowlisting called "your strongest control against prompt injection"; connector tokens injected by a reverse proxy so the sandbox never holds them. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inference hooks: inline data loss prevention for Claude Enterprise](sources/claude-enterprise-inference-hooks.md): tool responses from MCP connectors, skills and plugins are inspected before returning to the model, a check against injected or sensitive content arriving via tools ("How inference hooks works"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Centrally manage authorization for MCP connectors](sources/claude-enterprise-managed-mcp-auth.md): implemented as the Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension to the MCP authorization spec, embedding the Cross App Access protocol (intro; Okta-side quote). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Zero Trust for AI agents](sources/claude-zero-trust-for-ai-agents.md): Ch 04 catalogues tool poisoning, MCP rug pulls, tool-chaining exfiltration and loop amplification; Ch 06 Phase 2 advises self-hosting and signing verified MCP servers. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to develop an MCP Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-product-strategy.md): cites the Asana and GitHub MCP incidents. Broad read/write scopes are hard to avoid, and servers should reject tokens with too much or irrelevant scope (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [The coming AI security crisis | Sander Schulhoff](sources/lenny-podcast-sander-schulhoff-ai-security.md): malicious email or hidden web text redirects inbox and browser agents; in his competitions agents were easier to trick than models were to jailbreak for CBRNE (1:01:09) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [An AI state of the union (Simon Willison)](sources/lenny-podcast-simon-willison-state-of-ai.md): lethal trifecta (private data, untrusted instructions, exfiltration); "97% ... is a failing grade"; cut the exfiltration leg (1:20:18-1:22:09) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [A2ABreak: Systematic Security Analysis of the A2A Protocol](sources/arxiv-a2abreak-security-analysis.md): The first systematic, specification-level security analysis of A2A found. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [Agent Card Poisoning: A Metadata Injection Vulnerability in the Systems using Google A2A Protocol](sources/keysight-agent-card-poisoning.md): Shows that an Agent Card is untrusted text that ends up in the caller's prompt: a malicious remote agent embeds instructions in its card, and the host LLM follows them. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [A Security Engineer's Guide to the A2A Protocol](sources/semgrep-security-engineers-guide-a2a.md): The primary source behind the widely repeated claim that A2A "supports but does not enforce Agent Card signing", which Track 3 had only second-hand. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [Action Fabric: MCP Server, MCP Client, and A2A explained](sources/servicenow-community-action-fabric-mcp-a2a.md): ServiceNow supports A2A in both directions, but its own governance layer does not cover it: "AI Gateway currently governs MCP traffic only; A2A is outside its scope as of the current GA release." For a regulated setting  (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [When AI Agents Go Rogue: Agent Session Smuggling Attack in A2A Systems](sources/unit42-agent-session-smuggling-a2a.md): A worked attack on stateful agent-to-agent delegation: a malicious remote agent uses an established A2A session to inject instructions into the calling agent across turns, causing data leakage and an unauthorised stock p (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)

Intent is complete enough for agentic delivery when it meets an agreed standard (templates, examples, evals) that gates delivery and improves from delivery feedback.

- [Community Wisdom: When AI velocity outpaces your product strategy ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-velocity-strategy.md): dates slip because "the spec wasn't solid enough when we scoped the work"; more input context makes output "on-target and shippable" (threads 1, 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## agent-stewardship: Every deployed agent needs a human steward
Agents that people rely on stay useful only while a named person keeps tending them (reading traces, fixing prompts, adding guardrails, deciding what becomes a primitive); when that care stops, the agent decays. This matters for who maintains a PM agent and what headcount it implies. New because existing slugs cover harness ownership as a build-vs-buy choice (build-vs-buy) or the dimension harness-upkeep, but no theme covers the ongoing human care of a deployed agent as a role.
- [The AI paradox: More automation, more humans, more work | Dan Shipper](sources/lenny-podcast-dan-shipper-ai-paradox.md): personal agents failed at Every because "it really needs a human who cares about it"; forward-deployed engineers maintaining one company agent are "the new most essential role" (13:36, 53:15) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Claude Mythos found a 15-year-old bug in Mozilla Firefox | Brian Grinstead](sources/howiai-mozilla-mythos-bug-harness.md): analyzer prompts tuned continuously from trace analysis (manual and LLM-assisted) and engineers' feedback on bad reports (12:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

(research-claude-resources-articles)

## cost-control-routing: Cost metering and model routing built into the harness
Open access to frontier models blew budgets; Ramp added per-project meters, limits and a router that picks the model.
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): $1.5M week, taxi meter, Ramp Router, 30% drop claimed (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): LLM proxy with per-team cost tracing and config-only model swaps (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass. Make your entire company smarter](sources/ramp-introducing-glass.md): budget blown in weeks; users default to frontier models (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): the opposite stance in April: "Kill token limits and access restrictions", "treat AI usage as an infinite learning budget"; metering came later with Router/Glass (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp Router launch posts (Jul 20, 2026)](sources/x-ramp-router-launch-posts.md): the 30% bill cut is a Router claim from July 2026, 'without any performance degradation' (Zaks); no published data (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): independent data point on in-harness routing, LangChain Open SWE -64% median cost/thread, no significant quality change (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): Ramp Router sits in the harness as the LLM gateway; model choice per cost/latency/performance (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model](sources/shopify-engineering-agentic-harness-outlasts-model.md): full scan $50–300, diff scan $5–50; partitions sized to 20–30% of the context window (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): no token limits but "circuit breakers"; token leaderboard replaced by a usage dashboard where anyone sees their own spend (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Shopify built an AI stack that doesn't care which models survive](sources/venturebeat-shopify-ai-stack-model-agnostic.md): the proxy auto-moved users to Opus or GPT 5.5 when "Claude Fable 5 shut down" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [From Memo to Movement](sources/firstround-shopify-ai-culture.md): in 2025 a token-spend leaderboard was "a cool proxy for value"; by 2026 it was removed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): Kai projects set the default model and can block expensive models for a workflow (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Production-grade AI agents for financial compliance: Lessons from Stripe](sources/aws-stripe-compliance-agents.md): all LLM calls go through an LLM Proxy (noisy-neighbour limits, fallbacks, usage tracking by privacy class); prompt caching cut cost 60% (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): no separate VM charge; cloud sessions share the account's rate limits, so parallel tasks consume limits proportionately (Limitations) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): hourly caps (100 scheduled runs/hr per account, 30/hr per task for run-now and API fires) and subscription usage draw-down, no overage by default (Usage and limits) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The $47K agent loop: why logging, monitoring and max_tokens all failed to stop it](sources/devto-47k-agent-loop.md): claims four LangChain agents on A2A looped (Verifier requesting, Analyzer producing) with no termination condition or budget cap; 'They had logging. They had monitoring. They did not have a hard limit.' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Durable Execution for AI Agents: LangGraph, DBOS, Inngest and Temporal Compared](sources/hackernoon-durable-execution-compared.md): payloads must stay in network rules out Inngest unless self-hosted (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How Ramp built a full-context background coding agent on Modal](sources/modal-ramp-inspect-background-agent.md): sessions start in seconds from a filesystem snapshot refreshed by a cron every 30 minutes (repos cloned, dependencies installed, build run); startup speed framed as the adoption driver (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Oz Cloud Agents & Orchestration (Warp docs)](sources/warp-oz-cloud-agents.md): runs incur platform plus compute plus inference charges; personal BYOK not supported for cloud runs; team-managed inference on Business/Enterprise (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ramp Inspect Architecture 2026: How Background Coding Agents Scale Safely](sources/wavect-ramp-inspect-architecture.md): measure accepted changes per unit of review effort and incident risk, not PRs per day; review capacity and CI become the bottleneck (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Hosting the Agent SDK](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-hosting.md): first-party: token cost dominates container cost by an order of magnitude; per-session cost tracking available (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness design for long-running application development](sources/anthropic-harness-design-long-running-apps.md): first-party: 20x cost for the full harness on one task (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus](sources/manus-context-engineering-lessons.md): first-party: KV-cache hit rate is the key production metric (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Omnigent contextual policies](sources/databricks-omnigent-contextual-policies.md): soft/hard session cost caps that force a cheaper model; per-user daily caps (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare OS announcement](sources/cloudflare-os-announcement.md): all inference via AI Gateway with attribution and budgets per person/team/workspace (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare AI code review](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): $0.20 trivial to $1.68 full review by risk tier; shared context file prevents multiplying tokens (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Warp Oz](sources/warp-oz-multi-harness.md): per-team billing and credit caps, but third-party harness inference bills outside Warp's summaries (vendor docs) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Code Review is now generally available](sources/claude-code-review-ga.md): token-billed, averaging $15-25 per review; monthly org spend caps, repo-level enablement, an analytics dashboard of PRs reviewed, acceptance rate and cost (launch post, §Cost and control). - [Claude Cowork and chat are now one Claude](sources/claude-cowork-chat-unified.md): Efficient mode keeps the unified experience on Sonnet and Haiku; per-role model entitlements; spend limits at org, group and member level; pooled group budgets (Enterprise, "Managing cost"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Making Claude Cowork ready for enterprise](sources/claude-cowork-for-enterprise.md): per-team budgets "adjustable as you learn what each team needs". (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Asana built AI Teammates on Claude Opus 4.6](sources/claude-customers-asana-ai-teammates.md): multi-agent architecture with a top-level coordinating agent on Claude and different Claude models per subagent to trade speed against reasoning. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Atlassian builds AI agents teams can trust with Claude and Google Cloud](sources/claude-customers-atlassian-trusted-agents.md): an internal AI model gateway on Google's agent platform routes across providers; high-volume custom agents moved to Gemini Flash, Claude kept for complex work; teams benchmark models on quality and cost and deploy the winner... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Office Hours: Building for the model that doesn't exist yet (Ramp, with Boris Cherny)](sources/claude-customers-ramp-office-hours.md): no per-person token or dollar caps; instead defaults, batch/flex APIs and cheaper models for non-human-controlled automations, plus personal outreach to sudden top spenders (Rahul and Austin, cost section). - [Agent harness design: 3 patterns for harnessing Claude's intelligence](sources/claude-harness-design-three-patterns.md): cache rules: static content first, append updates as messages, don't switch models mid-session (use a subagent for a cheaper model), use tool search instead of changing the tool list (Pattern 3 table). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Loop engineering: Getting started with loops](sources/claude-loop-engineering.md): route routines to smaller models and keep the most capable for judgment; pilot dynamic workflows on a slice; scripts for deterministic steps; match intervals to change rate; /usage, /goal and /workflows show spend (section... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Decision Models Explained - The New AI Building Block for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-decision-models.md): routing steps (which tool, model or team) are usually a small LLM call returning one word; a typed-answer decision model does them faster and cheaper (Higgsfield auto-routing, Harvey Vault, both second-hand) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Perplexity's new Computer...](sources/departmentofproduct-perplexity-computer.md): each subtask is routed to a different vendor's model; credit-metered use means always-on workers need watching (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): Rippling claims a single code-mode MCP tool is 98% cheaper than chained tool calls (vendor claim) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Manage AI Agents Effectively](sources/departmentofproduct-managing-ai-agents.md): three spend tactics (gateway budgets at Databricks and Vercel; routing by task difficulty, where Block's Buzz benchmark found the priciest model cost about 5.5x for about 9 points more quality; dedicated spend products from Ramp and Rippling, with Rippling's set against PR volume and rework). All second-hand. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use /loops, /goals and other Powerful Slash Commands as a Non-Engineer](sources/departmentofproduct-loops-goals-slash-commands.md): /compact pitched to PMs as a token-cost saver, with a steerable focus (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [The Codex feature that works while you sleep](sources/howiai-claire-vo-codex-goal.md): a 3h52m inbox-cleanup goal used about six million tokens, "not token cheap" (18:42) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya](sources/lenny-podcast-anish-acharya-company-loops.md): open-weight tuned models for bounded verifiable work, frontier tokens for sales, support, research and engineering (22:04-25:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's CPO on how AI changes must-have skills (Kevin Weil)](sources/lenny-podcast-kevin-weil-openai-cpo.md): o-series where reasoning matters and latency doesn't, 4o-mini for quick cheap checks (1:01:24) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Claude Code (Boris Cherny)](sources/lenny-podcast-boris-cherny-after-coding.md): don't optimise tokens early; some Anthropic engineers spend "hundreds of thousands a month"; a cheaper model can cost more tokens overall (27:44, 1:08:51) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Community Wisdom: ... AI agents and data integrity ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-agents-data-integrity.md): encode exact warehouse queries in Markdown instead of paying agents to rediscover them via MCP (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): token cost per knowledge worker rises with each model jump, still below salary but a growing share (49:50) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How I run autonomous coding agents with OpenAI Symphony + Linear](sources/howiai-alessio-fanelli-symphony-linear.md): self-built per-task token ledger; one task cost 221M tokens; deviation from expected tokens signals missing tooling (7:36, 12:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): nine agents heading to ~$1,000/month on API; moving some to a subscription (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Driving AI adoption](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-driving-ai-adoption.md): token caps removed at the start of adoption, reintroduced later (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity](sources/lenny-podcast-adam-mosseri-product-staff.md): "no leaderboards for tokens"; no token caps today but expects caps proportional to trust in ROI-positive use; an engineer's token burn may match salary within 1-2 years (21:25-22:12) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to turn your AI into a world-class designer](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-world-class-designer.md): cheap implementer plus strong critic; the critic used "less than 10% of output tokens", half the cost of a direct redesign; scoped, spend-limited API keys for agents (Techniques 3-4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building AI product sense, part 2](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-product-sense-part-2.md): estimate a cost envelope per feature early (AI meeting notes ~$0.40 per user-month, ~$0.25-0.30 with caching and smaller models) (Estimating the cost envelope) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Not all AI agents are created equal](sources/lenny-newsletter-three-agent-categories.md): agent run cost ranges from "$500 per month" to "a six-figure annual LLM bill"; cost per run/session/task as a first-class metric (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [How Warp ships 2,000 PRs a month with AI factories (How I AI)](sources/howiai-warp-zach-lloyd-software-factory.md): per-PR agent cost tracked centrally; model is the biggest lever; replay past tasks under other configs to build a cost-quality Pareto chart for routing (17:01-30:39) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## docs-as-code-prd: PRDs and specs as files in the repo
Whether product specs live as markdown in git and how consistent that practice is.
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): intent and spec live as markdown in an `intent/` folder in the product repo for a single product; a dedicated intent repo only when intent spans many repos (§Stage 1, Infrastructure). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Datadog built a "universal machine tool" for Claude Code](sources/claude-datadog-universal-machine-tool.md): the transition table is "data, not spaghetti control flow"; agents change it and hot-reload it under policy without CI (§Why not just build a CRUD app?). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Spec-driven development at Notion | Ryan Nystrom](sources/howiai-notion-ryan-nystrom-spec-driven.md): `agent specs` folder of Markdown specs in the Notion repo; spec is the version-controlled source of truth; "update the specs, don't update the code" (32:06-39:23) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung](sources/lenny-podcast-fiona-fung-after-coding-solved.md): "check those [specs] into the repo" and keep them current so code review can test against "what good looks like"; content design shipped as a repo skill (15:00) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [HTML is the new Markdown | Thariq Shihipar](sources/howiai-thariq-shihipar-html-specs.md): living HTML design system kept in the repo; plans as implementation artifacts (26:39, 25:39; show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [A 3-step AI coding workflow for solo founders | Ryan Carson](sources/howiai-ryan-carson-prd-task-list.md): May 2025 three-file system: AI-written PRD → task list → stepwise execution in Cursor (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: The changing product development process ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-prd-vs-prototype.md): PRD one-pager kept beside the agent plan in Claude Code and revised there (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How I built LennyRPG](sources/lenny-newsletter-how-i-built-lennyrpg.md): PRD as a Markdown file in Cursor is the "single source of truth"; agent sent back to it when it drifts or context runs out; Markdown logs of attempts as working memory (sections 2-3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why humans are AI's biggest bottleneck (Alexander Embiricos)](sources/lenny-podcast-embiricos-codex-human-bottleneck.md): long Codex runs start from a co-written plan.md; "if that plan has verifiable steps, it'll work for much longer" (36:16) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Everyone should be using Claude Code more](sources/lenny-newsletter-everyone-claude-code.md): a `{project}-product` repo whose CLAUDE.md points at engineering repos; verbose commit messages as future decision context (#20) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Code for product managers (Teresa Torres)](sources/howiai-teresa-torres-claude-code-pm.md): tasks as Markdown files with YAML front matter, assembled by a /today command (6:09-8:38) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The non-technical PM's guide to building with Cursor | Zevi Arnovitz](sources/lenny-podcast-zevi-arnovitz-cursor-pm.md): plans written as files with TL;DR, critical decisions and per-task status Claude updates (29:50) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: speeding up discovery in a big org](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-discovery-big-org.md): structured intent model is canonical; readable PRDs generated from it on demand at any level of detail (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Notion's design team uses Claude Code to prototype](sources/howiai-notion-brian-lovin-prototype-playground.md): team prototype repo with "no back end ... just all files on disk", per-person namespaced folders and metadata files (10:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build your own AI developer tools with Claude Code](sources/howiai-tenex-cj-hess-flowy.md): plans iterated as Markdown in a `.plans` folder until confident to let the agent code (7:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The complete beginner's guide to coding with AI](sources/howiai-claire-vo-beginner-prd-to-code.md): PM hub repo with Markdown PRDs and prototypes side by side, plus a PRD agent-instruction file (26:11-33:45) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build AI product sense](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-product-sense-part-1.md): PMs doing strategy and PRDs in Cursor because the agent "edits your files directly (malleable knowledge)"; PRD context checklist includes transcripts folder, analytics MCP and codebase area (Steps 3, 10) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The rise of the professional vibe coder (Lazar Jovanovic)](sources/lenny-podcast-lazar-jovanovic-vibe-coder.md): four Markdown PRDs (master plan, implementation plan, design guidelines, user journeys) compile into tasks.md plus a rules file read before every prompt (31:34-34:36) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [I spent $20,000 on Devin in a month (Ryan Carson)](sources/howiai-ryan-carson-devin-20k-month.md): Claude Design, then a Markdown spec, then Codex as a design-to-code handoff (35:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Keeping architecture docs up to date](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-architecture-docs-intent.md): architecture specs live in the repo and are refreshed with agents; the refresh surfaces problems (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: PRDs for agents](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-prds-for-agents.md): living PRD with explicit versions; the agent works only from the current one, prior versions kept "as history rather than competing sources of truth" (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: when engineering outpaces product](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-engineering-outpaces-product.md): golden Markdown PRDs in an IDE updated by an AI intake command with change log (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Building without clear PM requirements](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-building-without-pm-requirements.md): contrast: leaders moving away from PRDs; PMs own the epic and engineers decompose, since "Requirements are clarified through conversation" (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Spec Kit and spec-driven.md (GitHub)](sources/github-spec-kit-sdd.md): spec is declared the source of truth ('Specifications don't serve code' is the doc's own framing); lives in git, one branch per feature. (user-story-mapping)
- [Specs (Kiro docs)](sources/kiro-specs-docs.md): specs are plain markdown files the agent keeps updated (task status); storage path not stated on the page fetched. (user-story-mapping)
- [Understanding Spec-Driven-Development: Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl](sources/fowler-bockeler-sdd-kiro-speckit-tessl.md): three levels (spec-first, spec-anchored, spec-as-source); all tools are spec-first, few commit to spec-anchored; spec-kit creates a branch per spec so specs behave like change requests. (user-story-mapping)
- [MADR: Markdown Architectural Decision Records](sources/adr-madr-template.md): sections Context and Problem Statement, Decision Drivers, Considered Options, Decision Outcome (Consequences, Confirmation), Pros/Cons; versioned with code. (user-story-mapping)
- [Cursor is a much better product manager (Lenny's Newsletter)](sources/lenny-cursor-better-product-manager.md): blurb lists 'Why source-controlled markdown files might replace traditional SaaS tools' and a chapter on creating PRDs in Cursor with source control (anecdote; no detail). (user-story-mapping)

## enablement-by-product: The product is the enablement
Teach users by what the product does (suggested skills, memory, self-healing) rather than training.
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): principle 3; "every feature is secretly a lesson" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): feature-request prompt example (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Karim Atiyeh Glass launch post](sources/x-karimatiyeh-glass-feature-requests.md): an account manager's saved prompt took feature-request capture from ~300 to ~20,000 a month (vendor claim) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment](sources/shopify-engineering-remote-dev.md): adoption needed internal ads with a River persona; River went from 6% to 61% of merged mobile PRs (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): learning "does not require a curriculum, a training plan, or a manager. It just requires everyone's work to be visible" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Make the Work Visible](sources/airealized-make-the-work-visible.md): visibility as the adoption lever; peer practices (AI Corner, failure labs) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Reflexive AI usage is now a baseline expectation at Shopify](sources/x-tobi-reflexive-ai-usage-memo.md): adoption by mandate as well: AI questions in performance and peer reviews; headcount requests must show why AI can't do it (Apr 2025) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Stripe Built Kai on Deep Agents (LangChain)](sources/langchain-how-stripe-built-kai-deep-agents.md): adoption came from removing knobs: users who bounced off configurable tools found Kai needed none (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): pilot with GTM (200-300 users), then a company-wide demo triggered the ramp (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Uber Agentic Pods (CTO post)](sources/x-praveen-uber-agentic-pods.md): 16 two-week pods in 16 functions: shadow, prioritise, build with the expert, validate, ship ('building with them, not for them') (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How Stripe Built a new Internal AI Knowledge Platform (Department of Product)](sources/departmentofproduct-stripe-kai.md): 'start with one domain and one surface', the most repeatable job in the tool people already use (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Building AI agents for the enterprise](sources/claude-building-agents-enterprise-cowork.md): Cowork offered as the route to agents for every team, plus a six-month rollout framework (guide contents list). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Best practices for getting started with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-cowork-getting-started-best-practices.md): delegation checklist and chat-vs-Cowork examples as the adoption guidance, with "ask Claude which of your tasks to hand off" using memory of past conversations (When should you use Cowork; Your first 10 minutes). - [Cowork and plugins for teams across the enterprise](sources/claude-cowork-plugins-enterprise.md): Claude guides admins through plugin setup by asking questions; slash commands open structured forms so a workflow "feels as intuitive as filling out a brief" ("Upgrading the plugin experience"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How a $2 billion venture fund made Claude Cowork its shared firm infrastructure](sources/claude-customers-airtree-cowork.md): a Data Lead built a one-hour course tailored by function, later published and reportedly downloaded 700+ times; a hackathon planned for new workflows (Q&A, "How did the team first start"; "Open Source VC"). - [How Blank Metal, a lean professional services firm, runs on Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-blank-metal-cowork.md): about 710 people trained (as of June 1) using Lectern, an in-house live training companion run side by side with participants' terminals ("You've trained more than 700 people"). - [Cyera on making Claude Cowork the front door to 40 tools](sources/claude-customers-cyera-cowork-front-door.md): 88% weekly active usage claimed about a month after rollout, attributed to ~20 department sessions, twice-weekly office hours, an 18-hour livestream, 24/7 on-call support and all-hands executive buy-in (Q&A, "88% adoption"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Office Hours: Building the case for leaders who ship with DoorDash](sources/claude-customers-doordash-office-hours.md): written artifacts shared company-wide, including failures, as "the most scalable way to distribute learnings" and readable by agents (Andy, adoption and closing). - [How Miro's champions run their week with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-miro-champions.md): adoption spread "on the strength of what its champions are building"; advice to nominate champions who filter updates and field first-line questions (Woods, final answer). - [Money Forward builds an AI-native engineering organization with Claude Code](sources/claude-customers-money-forward.md): small trials with a public channel any employee could follow; 200+ engineers outside the trial asked for access; the trial channel became the official one ("Choosing Claude through rigorous evaluation"). ## enterprise-admin-controls: Enterprise admin controls across harnesses
The identity, audit, policy, data-retention and cost controls a harness gives an org admin, and on which surfaces they are enforced. It is the baseline a regulated owner compares any build or layer against.
- [Agent identity: a new access model for autonomous, team-wide AI](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): workspace baseline profile inherited by channels, channel overrides; repo access, connectors, skills/plugins, standing instructions; RBAC on who can invoke; per-channel disable (sections "Inheriting permissions", "Broad... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): a worked managed-settings file for a regulated enterprise (deny reads of secrets, OS sandbox with domain allowlist, managed hooks and MCP servers only, an approved plugin marketplace, a minimum version) (§Stage 5, Worked example). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Introducing the Claude apps gateway for Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud](sources/claude-apps-gateway.md): managed settings defined once and enforced on every request; allowed models and defaults set centrally; onboarding/offboarding via the IdP. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Running auto mode in production](sources/claude-auto-mode-in-production.md): admins pin `defaultMode` or set `disableAutoMode` in managed settings; hard-deny rules are customisable org-wide; Garner pushed auto mode to all 550 staff via managed settings (companion pages). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [CISO's guide to agentic AI](sources/claude-ciso-guide-agentic-ai.md): seven controls, each stated as a generic requirement then as Cowork's implementation: IdP identity (SAML/OIDC, SCIM, custom roles), two-gate connector allowlist, per-tool per-action approval, sandbox without credentials,... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Measure Claude Code's impact with contribution metrics](sources/claude-code-contribution-metrics.md): dashboard visible to workspace admins and owners; per-user contribution data to "identify adoption patterns" ("Measure velocity"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Introducing dynamic workflows](sources/claude-code-dynamic-workflows.md): admins can disable workflows through managed settings ("How it works"; "Getting started"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Claude Code works in large codebases: Best practices and where to start](sources/claude-code-large-codebases.md): governance questions in regulated orgs; start with approved skills, required review, limited access, and cross-functional working groups with infosec (ownership section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Customize Claude Code with mods in TypeScript](sources/claude-code-mods.md): plugin marketplace allow/block via admin console or managed settings; admin mods can load first; audit-logging mod example (section "Mods for teams and enterprises"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Code Review is now generally available](sources/claude-code-review-ga.md): admin enables in Claude Code settings, installs the GitHub App and picks repositories; developers need no configuration (both posts, Get started). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A guide to cost visibility and control in Claude](sources/claude-cost-visibility-control.md): access gating by group/custom role, model entitlements and defaults, hard caps per org/user/group, automated review of limit-increase requests (section "Cost controls for Claude Enterprise"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Cowork and chat are now one Claude](sources/claude-cowork-chat-unified.md): admins choose when to enable Docs/Slides/Design, control access by role, get 30 days' notice before changes; SSO and Compliance API carry over; ZDR, HIPAA-ready and customer-managed-key orgs stay on current config (Enterprise,... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Making Claude Cowork ready for enterprise](sources/claude-cowork-for-enterprise.md): RBAC with custom roles per group (manual or SCIM), group spend limits, per-tool connector controls applied org-wide (section "Controls for organization-wide deployment"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Cowork and plugins for teams across the enterprise](sources/claude-cowork-plugins-enterprise.md): unified "Customize" menu for plugins, skills and connectors; admin control over which connectors are bundled; OpenTelemetry for usage, cost and tool activity ("Upgrading the plugin experience"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Asana built AI Teammates on Claude Opus 4.6](sources/claude-customers-asana-ai-teammates.md): admins control access to AI Teammates; users control which are active, what they access and what actions they take; every action recorded in task history; customer data not used for training. Framed as the answer to CIO "agent... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How League went all in on Claude in a regulated industry](sources/claude-customers-league.md): CEO cites tiered model access, control over which connectors are available to whom, and spend/usage transparency as what made regulators' concerns answerable (Q&A, final answer). - [Stripe deploys Claude Code to 1,370 engineers with zero-configuration enterprise rollout](sources/claude-customers-stripe-claude-code-rollout.md): security concerns initially blocked deployment until the signed enterprise binary existed. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Thomson Reuters CTO on piloting Cowork with Claude Enterprise](sources/claude-customers-thomson-reuters-cowork-pilot.md): Claude Enterprise valued for data isolation, security controls and admin oversight; least privilege via approved connectors (Q&A, guardrails answer). - [Scaling agentic coding across your organization](sources/claude-guide-scaling-agentic-coding.md): "enterprise managed policy settings that take precedence over user and project settings" push configuration and permitted MCP tools to all users (ch. 06 Security first). - [Agent harness design: 3 patterns for harnessing Claude's intelligence](sources/claude-harness-design-three-patterns.md): promote actions to dedicated tools when the harness needs a typed hook to gate, render or audit; hard-to-reverse actions such as external API calls can require user confirmation (Pattern 3, "declarative tools"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Memory for Claude Managed Agents: agents that learn across sessions](sources/claude-managed-agents-memory.md): scoped permissions per store, audit log of every change by agent and session, rollback, redaction from history, session events in the Console (section "Portable memories"). - [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](sources/claude-steering-claude-code.md): centrally managed CLAUDE.md deployed via MDM that individuals cannot exclude; managed settings cannot be overridden locally (CLAUDE.md; "When to use each method"). - [Claude Tag now supports personal connectors in channels](sources/claude-tag-personal-connectors.md): admins choose shared tools under an agent identity, personal connectors only (relying on existing role-based access), or tool by tool; Enterprise admins will be able to require review for everyone (intro). - [Uber's CISO on building an insider threat program for AI](sources/claude-uber-ciso-insider-threat-ai.md): Enterprise Frontier Safeguards described as safeguards in place while Uber's data stays inaccessible to Anthropic without permission, with Uber controlling the response after a trigger. ## evals-autonomy-trust: Evals, autonomy sliders and earned trust
Start agents as suggestions, measure against ground truth, then let users raise autonomy. Related: [[risk-sloped-review]].
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): Policy Agent suggestions -> auto-approve slider; weekly labeling; evals from five examples (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-geoff-charles-product-when-coding-solved.md): autonomous small loops, Review Buddy 93%, Testo 425 bugs (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Meet Ramp Research: Our Agentic Data Analyst](sources/ramp-builders-meet-ramp-research.md): evaluate the context layer, asserting on intermediate tool calls and query shape, not each answer (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)

## feedback-triage-agents: Feedback and research triage/synthesis as an agent job
Clustering and routing customer feedback, calls and tickets is the best-evidenced PM-agent job, but needs checks against invented or merged quotes.
- [Agents you can coach: how Asana builds human-agent teams with Claude](sources/claude-asana-agents-you-can-coach.md): Slack product questions become Asana tasks; agent answers from approved guidance with links, files product gaps to the product intake project, and raises enablement tasks when a question repeats ("Three jobs"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Carvana turns Slack alerts into production fixes with Claude Tag](sources/claude-customers-carvana-claude-tag.md): alert channels monitored; agent finds owning team, tags them, posts root cause in the team's format, opens PR on request (section "From alert to merged fix"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Gumroad's customer support team ships code with Claude](sources/claude-customers-gumroad-support-ships-code.md): "Our customer support team uses Claude to triage and often fix issues, reducing the load on our engineering team" (Claude improves customer support). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inside Rakuten's plan to turn every employee into a builder with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-rakuten-every-employee-builder.md): user-interviewing agent that creates tickets for agent or human triage (task system answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Sourcegraph streamlines product and community insights with Claude](sources/claude-customers-sourcegraph-product-insights.md): weekly community feedback reports for the product team generated from multiple sources (section "Choosing Claude"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic employees use Claude Tag](sources/claude-how-anthropic-uses-claude-tag.md): ~20 search variants across Slack to find every rep who asked for a feature (~24 accounts in ~26 min); a week of enterprise issues condensed from ~120 raw findings to 23 open and 14 resolved, then 15 more on a self-check... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Loop engineering: Getting started with loops](sources/claude-loop-engineering.md): bug reports and issue triage named as the best fit for proactive loops. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude](sources/claude-warp-self-improving-agents.md): issue-triage agent fired by a GitHub Action labels issues, assesses complexity and suggests a fix direction; maintainer feedback on a missed "ready to spec" label became a skill PR (section "The loop in action"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): support tickets grouped by theme and kept only if two or more independent sources corroborate them (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use Claude Routines at work - a Guide for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-routines-for-product-teams.md): weekly routine reads Slack, Intercom and app-store reviews, groups patterns across sources, checks each against open tickets and flags untracked ones (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- ["I'm incapable of doing my job without AI"](sources/howiai-monday-amir-klein-second-brain.md): Claude-guided Reddit scrape of 34,000 rows, then a frequency-weighted theme table for the team (8:35-13:32) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why every company now needs to think and operate like a lab team | Josh Woodward](sources/lenny-podcast-josh-woodward-labs-team.md): "agents running overnight, summarizing everything" is current practice; open problem is matching a top PM's insight from feedback (56:35) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung](sources/lenny-podcast-fiona-fung-after-coding-solved.md): a morning Claude routine reads all feedback channels, finds themes and opens PRs for review (12:39, 36:20) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [I gave Claude Code our entire codebase | Al Chen](sources/howiai-galileo-al-chen-codebase-context.md): customer questions clustered into roadmap themes; Slack threads turned into help articles (26:33-31:44) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
