## harness-over-model: The harness, not the model, limits real-world value
Ramp found models were good enough; the preconfigured environment (integrations, skills, memory, UX) decided whether non-experts got value. Central to what a "product agent and harness" is. Related: [[compounding-context-repo]].
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): "The Models are Good Enough, The Harness Isn't"; 99% adoption but most stuck (§intro) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): same finding framed as lesson 6, "the harness wasn't" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): the harness (sessions, sandboxes, connectors, observability, routing) is what Ramp chose to own; models stay swappable (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): the harness's 15 responsibilities listed; provider-agnostic; own trace-debug UI (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model](sources/shopify-engineering-agentic-harness-outlasts-model.md): better models gave more noise; all 30+ candidates in one audit were downgraded; the harness is the durable asset (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Introducing Roast](sources/shopify-engineering-introducing-roast.md): "Non-determinism is the enemy of reliability"; YAML + markdown steps interleaved with a Claude Code CodingAgent (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): 36%→77% merge rate "did not retrain a model... did not switch models" (self-reported) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Stripe's AI minions ship 1,300 PRs weekly from a Slack emoji (How I AI)](sources/howiai-stripe-minions-kaliski.md): minions succeed because of years of devex: hosted devboxes, CI, docs, a 'blessed path for 90% of the common activities' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): data-agent quality depends on pre-AI investments: tiered data catalog, blessed analytics layer, a warehouse hardened for agent query load (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Improving Deep Agents with harness engineering](sources/langchain-improving-deep-agents-harness-engineering.md): vendor claim: changing only prompt, tools and middleware moved the same model from 52.8% to 66.5% on Terminal Bench 2.0 (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): first-party: harness assumptions about model weakness go stale as models improve; harness components must be re-tested per model (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness design for long-running application development](sources/anthropic-harness-design-long-running-apps.md): first-party: planner/generator/evaluator harness cost $200 vs $9 solo on one task (20x) and a harness component was removed when the model improved (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Rebuilding Devin for Claude Sonnet 4.5](sources/cognition-devin-sonnet-45-rebuild.md): first-party: one model change forced harness changes (context anxiety, parallel tools); 2x faster, 12% better after rebuild (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [We removed 80% of our agent's tools](sources/vercel-we-removed-80-percent-of-our-agents-tools.md): first-party: simplifying to one bash tool raised success 80% to 100% on five queries, tokens down 37% (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: loop sophistication does not predict benchmark performance; production harnesses invest in scaffolding for safety, reliability and integration (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [OpenAI Introduces Harness Engineering (InfoQ)](sources/infoq-openai-harness-engineering.md): vendor claim: harness = repo docs, linters, layered architecture and observability; about a million lines with no hand-written code (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents](sources/anthropic-scaling-managed-agents.md): harness assumptions expire as models improve (context resets useful on Sonnet 4.5, dead weight on Opus 4.5) (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Meta-Harness paper](sources/arxiv-meta-harness-optimization.md): harness code is itself searchable/optimisable (independent paper) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Redesigning source control at Anthropic](sources/anthropic-redesigning-source-control-scion.md): an early internal Mythos Preview rewrote the hand-built ingestion pipeline at 20x less memory and 4x the speed with no further instructions (§What we learned). (research-claude-resources-articles)

(research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agent harness design: 3 patterns for harnessing Claude's intelligence](sources/claude-harness-design-three-patterns.md): "agent harnesses encode assumptions about what Claude can't do on its own, but those assumptions grow stale"; context resets added for Sonnet 4.5's "context anxiety" became "dead weight" with Opus 4.5 ("The future of agent... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Product management on the AI exponential](sources/claude-pm-on-the-ai-exponential.md): todo-list reminder hack removed when the next model did it unprompted; system prompt and tool descriptions trimmed with each model, including a 20% reduction for Opus 4.6 ("Do the simple thing"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Improving skill-creator: Test, measure, and refine Agent Skills](sources/claude-skill-creator-evals.md): if the base model passes a capability-uplift skill's evals without the skill, the skill may be retired. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](sources/claude-steering-claude-code.md): "two separate dials" (model and effort) control capability, while the seven methods control behaviour; each trades context cost against authority (intro; "The seven methods"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents Explained - a simple overview of the basics](sources/departmentofproduct-context-engineering-basics.md): agent failures "aren't necessarily model failures, but context failures" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): restates Anthropic's solo $9/20 min broken build vs harness $200/6 h working build; "the right harness for last year's model may be over-engineered for this year's" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [Inside Devin](sources/lenny-podcast-scott-wu-inside-devin.md): "in terms of base intelligence, we're honestly basically already there"; the work is teaching real-world idiosyncrasies (Datadog, PR flow) (1:02:20) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya](sources/lenny-podcast-anish-acharya-company-loops.md): host: across Cowork, ChatGPT Work, Cursor and Grok Bot "the underlying model is not that different ... most of it is the harness/UX" (58:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Why humans are AI's biggest bottleneck (Alexander Embiricos)](sources/lenny-podcast-embiricos-codex-human-bottleneck.md): Codex built as model + API + harness by one product-research team; compaction for 24-hour runs needed all three layers (21:38-24:45) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's CPO on how AI changes must-have skills (Kevin Weil)](sources/lenny-podcast-kevin-weil-openai-cpo.md): counterpoint, "model maximalism": avoid scaffolding around today's limits because a better model arrives in two months, except for errors you can't tolerate (30:03) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## harness-portability: Harness portability
Whether sessions, skills and context can move between harnesses and between local and cloud without losing history or behaviour.
- [How we built OCA, our AI on-call assistant](sources/ramp-builders-how-we-built-oca.md): OCA runs inside Claude Code or Codex depending on which models perform better; switched to GPT-6 Astra (first-party) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): harness outside the sandbox lets Shopify "swap models, runtimes, even languages on the harness side" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): "River ... switches between models"; "I don't care what harness you wanna use" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): a Kai project can be backed by a different API and harness while keeping Kai's features; Kai skills follow the open skill spec (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe Got 83% of Staff Using One AI Agent. Don't Copy Its Sales Numbers.](sources/aifounders-stripe-kai-dont-copy-sales-numbers.md): 'the skills are the durable asset'; keep them exportable from any vendor harness (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): handoff is deliberately asymmetric: cloud to terminal via --teleport (needs clean git state, same repo, same claude.ai account), terminal to cloud only as a new session or via the Desktop app; the terminal copy is a fork that does not sync back (Move tasks between terminal and cloud) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): credentials are never visible to the harness; git tokens used at sandbox init, MCP OAuth tokens held in a vault behind a proxy (Credential handling) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloud-origin agents have no 'Move to Machine' option (Cursor forum)](sources/cursor-forum-cloud-to-local-handoff.md): staff (2026-06-05) called cloud-to-local for cloud-origin sessions a 'known limitation', 'not being actively built out right now'; workaround is a local agent on the same repo or continuing in the cloud (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Code deletes conversation history after 30 days by default](sources/itdaily-claude-code-30-day-transcript-deletion.md): Anthropic's stated reason is that plain-text transcripts can hold code and credentials, i.e. retention conflicts with auditability (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Trace (Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 34)](sources/thoughtworks-radar-agent-trace.md): vendor-neutral JSON trace record linking code ranges to contributor type (human/AI/mixed/unknown) and, per the spec's draft, to the originating conversation; works with Git, Mercurial, Jujutsu (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [codex-plugin-cc](sources/openai-codex-plugin-for-claude-code.md): a competing vendor ships a plugin that runs inside Claude Code; shows plugins as a cross-harness delegation channel. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Run Claude Code programmatically](sources/anthropic-claude-code-headless-agent-sdk.md): `--bare` makes headless runs reproducible by skipping hooks, plugins, MCP and CLAUDE.md. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [MCP spec 2026-07-28](sources/mcp-spec-2026-07-28-key-changes.md): stateless transport and extension mechanism; Client ID Metadata Documents replace dynamic client registration. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Anthropic cracks down on unauthorized Claude usage by third-party harnesses](sources/venturebeat-anthropic-third-party-harness-crackdown.md): independent: Jan 2026 block of subscription OAuth outside official clients (OpenCode and others) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent SDK overview](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-overview.md): first-party: SDK runs the Claude Code binary; Claude models only; third-party products must use API keys, not claude.ai login (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: portability costs a maintained per-provider conditioning layer (cache breakpoints, thinking tiers); SKILL.md in 9 of 11 harnesses (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

## human-judgment-pm-jobs: PM jobs that stay human-led
Strategy, opportunity selection, interviewing, trade-offs and ratifying specs are where practitioners say human judgment stays central; agents prepare, humans decide.
- [Redesigning source control at Anthropic](sources/anthropic-redesigning-source-control-scion.md): engineers supplied system-level understanding and design trade-offs; "very often ... the role of the engineers was to tell Claude 'no'" when agents violated core constraints (§What we learned). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Product management on the AI exponential](sources/claude-pm-on-the-ai-exponential.md): PM's residual job is strategy clarity, pushing ambition, and choosing non-negotiables; letting go of control is "the first thing AI product management asks you to unlearn". (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): "AI led vs AI informed": human judgement keeps the final say (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use /loops, /goals and other Powerful Slash Commands as a Non-Engineer](sources/departmentofproduct-loops-goals-slash-commands.md): /goal is ruled out for strategic decisions and for security-sensitive or costly-to-get-wrong work (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Strategy Thought Partner](sources/departmentofproduct-strategy-thought-partner.md): framed as "cognitive expansion, not offloading": AI used "to think more clearly, not asking it to think for you" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): presents discovery ("what to build and why") as the skill that keeps its value as AI eats delivery (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): cross-functional stakeholder alignment is the stage CASH can't do: "we will have AGI and it will still be impossible to get six people in a room to get to align" (37:31-37:54) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [AI's third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers](sources/lenny-podcast-tara-seshan-persistent-coworkers.md): steering (opinionated direction) and accountability stay human, "especially in industries and places that are highly regulated"; writing-as-thinking is never automated (11:23, 46:19, 53:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why every company now needs to think and operate like a lab team | Josh Woodward](sources/lenny-podcast-josh-woodward-labs-team.md): dissent on role convergence: keep a "major"; APMs should prototype "in service of becoming an exceptional, extraordinary PM" (38:10) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya](sources/lenny-podcast-anish-acharya-company-loops.md): agents hill-climb to a local maximum then plateau; humans keep "sales, support, strategy and exceptions" and choosing the next hill (13:07-15:47) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Make product management fun again with AI agents](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-pm-agents.md): "AI isn't endangering your job, but letting AI read for you is"; insist on exact quotes and links to raw signals (item 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Product manager is an unfair role. So work unfairly.](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-unfair-role.md): let AI write the PRD from dictation but "avoid letting AI get between you and the raw data" (section 6) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's first technical PM ... | Dianne Penn](sources/lenny-podcast-dianne-penn-evals-prds.md): judgment is accumulated nuance models lack; choosing which buildable thing to build stays human; "we need more" user-centric PMs (1:12:09, 1:22:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino](sources/lenny-podcast-ambrosino-codex-product-work.md): with ~90 uncoordinated explorations of one feature, the expensive part is "the curation process", not implementation (3:09-4:50) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: The changing product development process ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-prd-vs-prototype.md): PRDs remain a forcing function for clear thinking and scope prioritization (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of ChatGPT ... | Tibo Sottiaux](sources/lenny-podcast-sottiaux-chatgpt-dots.md): typing fast trends down, taste and user understanding trend up (23:44) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why half of product managers are in trouble (Nikhyl Singhal)](sources/lenny-podcast-nikhyl-singhal-half-of-pms.md): judgment (is this change good, does it fit the system, is it worth releasing) becomes "paramount" as changes multiply 10-100x; "my job is not to move information. My job is to evaluate" (15:21-15:57, 51:08) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers (Elizabeth Stone)](sources/lenny-podcast-elizabeth-stone-netflix-systems-thinkers.md): PMs judge "have we really framed the what"; data scientists whether data can be trusted; engineers scale and quality (11:23) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's CPO on how AI changes must-have skills (Kevin Weil)](sources/lenny-podcast-kevin-weil-openai-cpo.md): the PM's distinctive job is to make sure a call gets made when ambiguity stalls a group (51:40) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [How OpenAI uses ChatGPT Sites (Kath Korevec)](sources/howiai-openai-korevec-chatgpt-sites.md): a hard line against the agent emailing or messaging in her name: "That's my voice" (32:35) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [OpenAI's Head of Design (Ian Silber)](sources/lenny-podcast-ian-silber-openai-design.md): humans keep understanding needs, watching use, inventing paradigms with no training data (24:05, 25:40) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Community Wisdom: How AI is changing product operating models](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-operating-models.md): "AI can accelerate delivery fast enough that the bottleneck moves ... The judgment gap got exposed" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Community Wisdom: when engineering outpaces product](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-engineering-outpaces-product.md): gate questions before adding a feature: does a way exist, useful to more than one customer, do we want to maintain it forever (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why your AI product needs a different development lifecycle (CC/CD)](sources/lenny-newsletter-cc-cd-ai-lifecycle.md): "At the heart of CC/CD is judgment": what to ship, when to hand control back, what "good enough" means (closing) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How AI is reshaping the product role (Udezue)](sources/lenny-podcast-udezue-ai-reshaping-pm-role.md): choosing "sharp problems"; support managers in design review; ethics guardrails owned by PMs (10:51, 14:33) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Warp ships 2,000 PRs a month with AI factories (How I AI)](sources/howiai-warp-zach-lloyd-software-factory.md): Warp keeps user interviews, watching users and design jams before building; "it still has to solve some user problem" (41:27-42:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Building without clear PM requirements](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-building-without-pm-requirements.md): in B2B2C healthcare, payer/patient/clinician experiences plus regulation and privacy mean PM and designer must hold context (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why AI evals are the hottest new skill (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-hamel-shreya-evals.md): the error-analysis "benevolent dictator" is the domain expert, "though oftentimes, it is the product manager" (27:42) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How 80,000 companies build with AI (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-asha-sharma-loop-not-lane.md): strategy needs "judgment and vision that could not be achieved without humans" (28:59) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Gumroad CEO's playbook to 40x his team's productivity (How I AI)](sources/howiai-gumroad-sahil-lavingia-v0-devin.md): humans still "go talk to people"; radical bets are not "in the next token prediction" (37:20) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How AI turns product managers back into builders](sources/atlassian-ai-turns-pms-into-builders.md): Likely automatable per Gupta's examples: email triage and drafting, Slack summarization, competitor launch tracking, feedback clustering, first-draft replies, research-note summaries, prototyping. Human-held (corrected in audit: 'deciding what to build' is not in this article; human-held are governance and review where judgment still matters): deciding what to build, governance and access, revi (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The bottleneck keeps shifting: what AI is changing about how we build (Gamma interview)](sources/atlassian-bottleneck-keeps-shifting-gamma.md): The author's narration calls 'discernment' the new PM superpower; bottleneck moves to deciding what to build, alignment, and documenting context for humans and agents; alignment on priorities remains a persistent challenge. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How to use AI to write a PRD from user research in 2026: a 4-step workflow (CleverX)](sources/cleverx-ai-prd-from-user-research.md): AI drafts problem statements, user stories, success metrics and edge cases but cannot make prioritization calls, define architecture, set engineering scope or choose trade-offs. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How can AI help me understand my customers? Interview analysis, synthesis and user research (echai.ventures)](sources/echai-torres-ai-interview-analysis.md): AI-moderated interviews and synthetic personas complement but do not replace real customers. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey](sources/lennys-newsletter-ai-tools-overdelivering-results.md): The write-up says AI helps PMs produce but lags in helping them think; strategic and discovery work near the bottom of use. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [What 638 practitioner voices reveal about PMs' AI transformation (Medium, Haberlah)](sources/medium-haberlah-638-practitioner-voices.md): Operational work automates while strategic judgment, stakeholder influence and user empathy appreciate (author's thesis, not survey data). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI in Product Management: What 379 Product Managers Revealed About the New Reality](sources/productboard-ai-in-product-management-report.md): Strategic and non-strategic PMs are diverging as AI takes over tactical work. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Focus Industry Survey Report 2026](sources/productfocus-industry-survey-2026.md): 85% of PMs use their expertise to validate AI output (PDF read in audit). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [More valuable, less protected](sources/reforge-more-valuable-less-protected.md): The map author's synthesis (the page gives no explicit lists; 'feature-level execution' is not on it). More valuable: problem definition, customer understanding, strategy, distributing context, holding project state, customer-validated prototyping. Less protected: default project captaincy, roadmap gatekeeping, feature-level execution, handoff-style prototyping (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The Era of the Product Creator](sources/svpg-era-of-the-product-creator.md): High-agency PMs 'that have understood that they are responsible for value and viability' are the ones Cagan praises (the phrase 'what survives' is not on the page). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The Four Big Risks](sources/svpg-four-big-risks.md): Engineering owns feasibility and delivery accountability, so an agent should not override engineering estimates (J6). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Manager Practices for Delegating Work to Generative AI](sources/arxiv-pm-delegating-work-to-genai.md): PMs hand off low-accountability work (formatting meeting notes) and keep specs and journey maps (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The AI Productivity Paradox](sources/svpg-ai-productivity-paradox.md): the constraint is knowing what is worth building, not build speed (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Experimentation, AI and the Product Model](sources/svpg-experimentation-ai-product-model.md): AI supports every discovery step but it "comes down to decisions and strategy"; eval quality judgments are subjective (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Don't Use Generative AI to Replace Discovery with Real Humans](sources/producttalk-generative-ai-discovery.md): one-click opportunity solution trees skip the team thinking that is the point (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Building My First AI Product: 6 Lessons from My 90-Day Deep Dive](sources/producttalk-ai-playbook-first-ai-product.md): "Claude is not ready to replace me" at synthesizing interviews (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How AI will impact product management](sources/lenny-how-ai-will-impact-product-management.md): roadmap trade-offs and design feedback rated least disrupted (2/5) but strategy/vision and goals rated most (4/5), against the map's J2 Low; interpersonal work gains value (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Management Theater](sources/svpg-product-management-theater.md): "Generative AI will only compound this": project-style PM work is the exposed part (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Customer Interview Analysis: Where AI Helps and Hurts](sources/producttalk-customer-interview-analysis-ai.md): "expert human synthesis aided by AI synthesis" is the sweet spot (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Customer Interview Analysis: All Things Product podcast with Teresa Torres and Petra Wille](sources/producttalk-torres-customer-interview-analysis-podcast.md): empathy comes from talking to customers; outsourcing customer understanding costs teams over time (show notes) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How we design when the code writes itself](sources/ideas-fin-how-we-design-when-code-writes-itself.md): agents "own the middle, the build" but "cannot decide which problems matter, set intent, resolve trade-offs, or hold the bar for quality" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Talk to the bot: When to use an AI interviewer](sources/ideas-fin-talk-to-the-bot-ai-interviewer.md): early-stage discovery, long interviews and synthesis kept human (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## human-review-gates: Human review gates on agent output
Where and how a human checks PM-agent output (quote checks, review before send, isolated repos). Related: [[risk-sloped-review]].
- [Why We Built Our Own Background Agent](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-background-agent.md): PRs open under the requesting user's GitHub identity so nobody approves their own agent's work (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How we built OCA, our AI on-call assistant](sources/ramp-builders-how-we-built-oca.md): nothing OCA triggers merges without a human; Slack buttons gate destructive actions (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How To Build Agents Users Can Trust](sources/ramp-builders-agents-users-can-trust.md): deterministic hard stops (dollar limits, blocklists) layered over the agent (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): draft-only, human merge authority; hand off "the smallest question that an owner has to answer"; River left a human-owned branch alone (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): "slop grenades", unread agent PRs that shift review load onto colleagues (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Inside Shopify's AI-first engineering playbook](sources/bvp-inside-shopifys-ai-first-engineering-playbook.md): "We still require a human PR reviewer, which is now becoming a big bottleneck" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Shopify builds product](sources/lenny-how-shopify-builds-product.md): every project passes GSD (Proposal, Prototype, Build, Release, Results), reviewed by directors (OK1) and senior leadership (OK2), mostly async (2023) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Production-grade AI agents for financial compliance: Lessons from Stripe](sources/aws-stripe-compliance-agents.md): compliance agents answer sub-questions as pre-fetched research; the human reviewer answers every sub-task; 26% faster median review, >96% helpfulness (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): per-project human-in-the-loop confirmation on sensitive tools, deliberately not for everyone, because prompting on every call makes people 'press the wrong button' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): deploys to 1% of boxes with automatic pause and rollback; mandated code review; review agent tested against past bad changes (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Thoughts On A Month With Devin](sources/answerai-month-with-devin.md): 'autonomy became a liability when Devin pursued dead ends instead of flagging blockers'; team found developer-driven tools like Cursor more effective for larger tasks because they allow incremental steering (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): a green run status 'does not mean the work your prompt describes succeeded'; runs start in auto mode with a classifier, and stop to wait if repeated blocks occur (View runs; Permission prompts) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Tag: agent identity (concepts)](sources/anthropic-claude-tag-agent-identity.md): audit attribution differs by context: channel actions appear under service accounts; DM actions under the user (PRs still authored by the GitHub App); personal-connector work in a channel is recorded under the approving user (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cursor Cloud Agent sessions are shared across users - act on behalf (forum bug report)](sources/cursor-forum-team-followups-act-on-behalf.md): reporter says the originating Slack prompt can be deleted, removing the audit trail while side effects remain (claim; staff reply did not address it) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent-risks.md): PRs are drafts a human must review and merge; the agent cannot mark them ready, approve or merge; the requester cannot approve their own agent-created PR; workflows do not run until a user with write access approves (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot, end-to-end coding agents - Part 2](sources/stripe-minions-part-2.md): every minion PR is human-reviewed; a minion gets one full CI iteration plus one retry, after which the branch goes back to a human (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Tag Slack access model (Tenable Research)](sources/tenable-claude-tag-slack-access-model.md): recommends auditing bundles, scoping to minimum, keeping elevated bundles in private channels, and logging/approving channel invites (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AWS AI coding tool decided to delete and recreate a customer-facing system, causing 13-hour outage (report)](sources/the-decoder-aws-kiro-outage.md): Amazon then added mandatory peer review for production access and says Kiro asks for authorisation by default (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Replit makes vibe-y promise to stop its AI agents making vibe coding disasters](sources/theregister-replit-saastr-response.md): Replit's fix is architectural (automatic dev/prod database separation, staging, planning/chat-only mode) not prompt-based; CEO called it 'Unacceptable and should never be possible' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Orchestrating AI Code Review at scale](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): first-party: AI review biased to approval, critical findings block, human 'break glass' used on 0.6% of MRs (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot coding agents](sources/stripe-minions-one-shot-coding-agents.md): first-party: every minion PR is human-reviewed; CI capped at two rounds (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Choose a design pattern for your agentic AI system](sources/google-cloud-choose-design-pattern-agentic-ai.md): vendor: HITL for high-stakes, safety-critical or subjective approvals (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How AI is transforming work at Anthropic](sources/anthropic-how-ai-is-transforming-work-at-anthropic.md): first-party self-report: more than half of engineers can fully delegate only 0-20% of work (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): humans gate each accepted artifact (product owner accepts intent and spec; engineer accepts plan; code owner approves PR via branch protection); higher-risk changes escalate to a tech lead or architect; human line review is... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Running auto mode in production](sources/claude-auto-mode-in-production.md): Anthropic reports users approve 97% of permission prompts but reject 39% of proposed plans, implying the review gate belongs at plan level, not per command (companion: "Comparing manual review to auto mode"). (research-claude-resources-articles)

- [Claude Cowork on web and mobile: hand off work anywhere](sources/claude-cowork-web-mobile-handoff.md): when Claude reaches "a call only you can make, it asks" via the phone; drafts can be redirected mid-run; "Nothing ships until you've reviewed and approved it" (section "What changes today"). - [How a $2 billion venture fund made Claude Cowork its shared firm infrastructure](sources/claude-customers-airtree-cowork.md): "All content generated by Claude Cowork must be verified and reviewed by a human before it's used for decision-making or published"; initial IT security, risk and compliance assessment and a usage record kept (Q&A, "sensitive... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Asana built AI Teammates on Claude Opus 4.6](sources/claude-customers-asana-ai-teammates.md): "autonomous on execution, but humans own the decisions"; drafting, triage and flagging compliance gaps are execution, judgement calls are surfaced to a human with context; autonomy adjustable by stakes. - [How Delivery Hero's agent merges 100+ pull requests a day with Claude](sources/claude-customers-delivery-hero-pr-agent.md): a "council of agents" of Claude and Gemini reviews from different perspectives "before a human does a final check"; multi-model by design (§The outcome). - [Office Hours: Building the case for leaders who ship with DoorDash](sources/claude-customers-doordash-office-hours.md): AI code review agents led to engineers "rubber stamping" reviews; more security issues surfacing industry-wide (Andy, early). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Miro's champions run their week with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-miro-champions.md): influencer reviewer handles brand/brief adherence while the manager keeps creative-judgment calls; "A human still owns the final call on anything external" (Judson; Hostetler). - [Office Hours: Asynchronous coding and the end of the IDE with Spotify](sources/claude-customers-spotify-office-hours.md): owning teams were told they may no longer see automated PRs, which are auto-merged; this forced stronger test automation, now reused as the agents' verification (Honk architecture segment). - [How the Claude Code team does code review](sources/claude-dev-claude-code-team-code-review.md): "an agent's approval never counts as a person's"; the person who directed the agent counts as one of the required reviewers; an approval covers one commit and is dismissed on new pushes (§5). - [A field guide to Claude Fable 5: Finding your unknowns](sources/claude-fable-finding-unknowns.md): the author merges only after passing a Claude-written quiz on the change; pitch/explainer artifacts package prototype, spec and notes for approvers ("Post implementation"). - [Claude for the financial industry](sources/claude-guide-financial-industry.md): the work brought first is "reviewed by a senior person before it ships"; for the ten agent roles "analysts stay in the loop, reviewing, iterating on, and approving the agent's outputs before anything moves downstream" (ch. 4... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic employees use Claude Tag](sources/claude-how-anthropic-uses-claude-tag.md): human time moves to challenging accuracy, supplying sources and deciding scope (thread-to-doc section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Loop engineering: Getting started with loops](sources/claude-loop-engineering.md): "Loops that write code need loops that check it"; use a second agent with fresh context for review (section "Maintaining code quality"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Deploying AI from pilot to production: a practical blueprint for CIOs and technical leaders](sources/claude-pilot-to-production-cio-blueprint.md): review is graded by output risk rather than applied uniformly. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic secures its AI-native software development lifecycle](sources/claude-securing-ai-native-sdlc-at-anthropic.md): shadow mode for every new AI reviewer (comments need human approval until trust is earned) and red-teaming of reviewers with inserted malicious changes (§Governance). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Turning conversation into knowledge: how Slack builds human-agent teams](sources/claude-slack-human-agent-teams.md): the human-agent rhythm is a cycle of handoffs: agents draft, summarise, monitor, prepare; a person reviews, decides and redirects (section "Learn when to handoff tasks"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Claude Tag serves as Anthropic's first responder for CI/CD failures](sources/claude-tag-ci-cd-first-responder.md): most frequent resolution is a PR "that the on-call can review, merge, and then deploy"; org-wide rule that every PR has a named human owner and every change needs approval to merge (sections "Resolution", "From monitoring... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building verification loops in Claude Code with skills](sources/claude-verification-loops-skills.md): in a chained loop "you only step in when something escalates back to you"; hold off on PR-wide gates while the chain is in flux ("Chained"; "On every PR"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude](sources/claude-warp-self-improving-agents.md): improver output goes through normal code review; "That final human step closes the loop and keeps a person in control of what actually changes." (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): Managerbot proposes every action (shift change, campaign, reorder) and the seller must approve it; approval is built into the loop, not bolted on, linked to Block's regulatory history (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Manage AI Agents Effectively](sources/departmentofproduct-managing-ai-agents.md): Intercom made agent knowledge-base readiness a mandatory launch sign-off; Vercel returns coding-agent work as Git patches that need human approval; the AARM proposal intercepts actions before they run. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use Claude Routines at work - a Guide for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-routines-for-product-teams.md): release notes drafted to Notion and linked in Slack for human review; the PM can open and steer a running routine (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is parallel AI agent coding? An in-depth guide for product teams](sources/departmentofproduct-parallel-agent-coding.md): each parallel agent's work lands as its own branch; a human compares the models' solutions and merges (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Claude Cowork as a Competitive Intelligence System](sources/departmentofproduct-cowork-competitive-intelligence.md): the author advises double-checking output before sharing. Browser automation was "a bit hit and miss" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): humans approve CASH experiments today; brand review could move into a brand-guidelines skill so human review "really decreases" (38:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The Codex feature that works while you sleep](sources/howiai-claire-vo-codex-goal.md): long-running goals end in PRs and a report of what needs human review; ambiguous items labelled "needs judgment" (14:02, 18:42) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Inside Devin](sources/lenny-podcast-scott-wu-inside-devin.md): humans step in for "the 10 or 20%" of a task on scoping, architecture or front-end checks; the human keeps "the full specification" (21:28, 25:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Advanced evals: How to find (and fix) hidden AI failures in your product](sources/lenny-newsletter-advanced-evals-error-discovery.md): the evals plugin forces a human to annotate 10 traces before the agent may propose labels, "a deliberate safeguard against automation bias"; aim for about 100 (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How tech workers are feeling in 2026](sources/lenny-newsletter-tech-workers-2026-survey.md): respondent: "I just follow Claude. I don't fully understand what I merge", a sign review is hollowing out under output pressure (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Devin replaces your junior engineers | Scott Wu](sources/howiai-scott-wu-devin-junior-engineer.md): every Devin change lands as a PR a human merges, with before/after screenshots and a stated confidence level (vendor demo) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The coming AI security crisis | Sander Schulhoff](sources/lenny-podcast-sander-schulhoff-ai-security.md): per-action human approval is good security but "what people want is AIs that just go and do stuff", so he expects it to fade (1:27:24) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung](sources/lenny-podcast-fiona-fung-after-coding-solved.md): human code review was "a really really big bottleneck" at 8x throughput until Claude code review; humans keep deep-expertise areas; "how far do you push fully automated reviews?" is open (14:54, 1:09:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Spec-driven development at Notion | Ryan Nystrom](sources/howiai-notion-ryan-nystrom-spec-driven.md): engineer still reviews agent PRs and prompts the agent to defend its change against pushback because models are sycophantic (29:59, 45:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Make product management fun again with AI agents](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-pm-agents.md): low-downside swaps for PM agents: DM me, draft not send, recommend not decide, append not modify (section "Can I keep the downside low?") (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building eval systems that improve your AI product](sources/lenny-newsletter-evals-hamel-shreya.md): one "benevolent dictator" domain expert, often the PM, labels pass/fail with critiques; LLM clustering must be human-validated (Phase 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Zapier's CEO shares his personal AI stack](sources/howiai-zapier-wade-foster-ai-stack.md): interview agent gives yes/no/maybe plus reasoning as a second opinion and "bias check", not the decision (14:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## identity-delegation: Identity and delegation (on-behalf-of)
Who an agent acts as when one agent or harness calls another: user tokens, service accounts, delegation chains, revocation and audit. Cuts across remote agents, MCP/A2A and shared sessions.
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): "River can see Slack messages ... data warehouse ... product management system"; "you can't go into a private channel" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Inside Shopify's AI-first engineering playbook](sources/bvp-inside-shopifys-ai-first-engineering-playbook.md): MCP servers go "through the same auth flow that you have", so AI sees only what you can see (assistant tools, not River) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River at Shopify (Internal Agents Map)](sources/internal-agents-shopify-river.md): credentials and sandbox marked "Not reported" in public sources (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's Aquifer, in the Open (Lobu)](sources/lobu-shopifys-aquifer-in-the-open.md): a proxy swaps placeholder tokens for real ones at egress, so the worker never holds secrets (vendor's own design, contrasted with Aquifer) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Create information barriers in Slack](sources/slack-information-barriers-docs.md): barriers block DMs and huddles between IdP groups, but members "will still be able to interact in public and private channels" they share (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): 'agentic identity ... we haven't solved this yet'; agent identity tags the use case an agent serves, used for priority and load shedding after agents nearly took down core systems (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [MCP Authorization spec](sources/mcp-authorization-spec-draft.md): OAuth 2.1 resource-server model; servers must not accept or pass through tokens issued for other audiences; so on-behalf-of access downstream needs token exchange or a vault (first-party spec). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare remote MCP](sources/cloudflare-remote-mcp-servers.md): the MCP server acts as OAuth provider to clients and OAuth client to GitHub/Google, issuing narrower tokens of its own (vendor). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Sentry MCP + Seer](sources/sentry-mcp-server-seer.md): OAuth consent with selectable permission sets for a vendor agent (vendor docs; partly unverified). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Copilot Studio A2A](sources/microsoft-copilot-studio-a2a.md): per-connection None/API key/OAuth; no user-identity propagation described. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Code cloud sessions](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): credentials kept outside the VM behind a proxy; auto-fix replies post under the user's GitHub account (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ask HN A2A](sources/hn-ask-is-anyone-using-a2a.md): commenters: the open problems are who delegated authority, revocation and trusting claimed capability (anecdote). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare OS announcement](sources/cloudflare-os-announcement.md): agents start with zero access; typed bindings; Gatekeepers hold credentials; shared agents reflect the viewer's permissions via an observation log (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Omnigent repo issue #11413](sources/github-omnigent-repo.md): session sharing did not separate chat access from host access to terminals and files (open P1 issue, 2026-10-23) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent identity: a new access model for autonomous, team-wide AI](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): two reasons act-as-user breaks: autonomy (tasks run after the requester logs off) and multiple people steering a channel (section "Why 'act as the user' breaks down"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Introducing the Claude apps gateway for Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud](sources/claude-apps-gateway.md): OIDC relying party (Google Workspace, Entra ID, Okta); short-lived sessions, no long-lived secrets on laptops. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agents you can coach: how Asana builds human-agent teams with Claude](sources/claude-asana-agents-you-can-coach.md): agents have their own profile (users, admins, instructions, skills, integrations, permissions) and access scoped to projects/documents/apps; Asana says an agent's effective access is bounded by the permissions of the person... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [CISO's guide to agentic AI](sources/claude-ciso-guide-agentic-ai.md): "agentic identity spectrum": service account (single-purpose, no human identity, e.g. incident agent, Claude Tag) vs human credential (Cowork on a laptop); the middle, delegated identity in systems the person isn't watching,... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Asana built AI Teammates on Claude Opus 4.6](sources/claude-customers-asana-ai-teammates.md): an AI Teammate has its own Asana account like any colleague; invoked by assignment, @mention or workflow rule. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Carvana turns Slack alerts into production fixes with Claude Tag](sources/claude-customers-carvana-claude-tag.md): one warehouse connection plus separate scoped identities per team (section "Managed agents with per-team identities"). (research-claude-resources-articles)

- [Building agents that reach production systems with MCP](sources/claude-mcp-production-patterns.md): CIMD client registration; vaults hold users' OAuth tokens and inject them per MCP connection (section "Lean on standardized auth"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic secures its AI-native software development lifecycle](sources/claude-securing-ai-native-sdlc-at-anthropic.md): the alert-triage agent is "a single-purpose system account agent with three permissions" (write docs, post in company channels, read production logs) and cannot deploy; fixes go through a separate agent-human reviewer system... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How healthcare organizations use Claude Tag](sources/claude-tag-healthcare-human-agent-teams.md): Insight Health pairs Tag (sees codebase and Linear) with its own Agent SDK agent Zeus on a BAA-covered API org that queries production data and masks PHI before Slack; deliberately different access per agent (Insight Health... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Tag now supports personal connectors in channels](sources/claude-tag-personal-connectors.md): Claude reads the channel's GitHub through the channel connector and Priya's private doc "through Priya's Google Drive connector, separately from the channel's work"; actions via a personal connector appear in that tool's log... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Self-service data analytics in Slack: how Anthropic deploys Claude Tag for ad-hoc questions](sources/claude-tag-self-service-analytics.md): queries run as a service account, not the asker; "everyone who can mention the bot has the bot's data access", no per-user row-level security (section "Permission the service account deliberately"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Zero Trust for AI agents](sources/claude-zero-trust-for-ai-agents.md): Ch 04 names "unscoped privilege inheritance" (manager agent passes full access to workers) and the confused-deputy problem; Ch 06 Phase 6 requires per-agent credentials and authorization checks at each hop of a multi-agent... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): WorkOS Agent Auth caps delegated sessions at user permissions ∩ agent ceiling, with step-up auth on sensitive calls (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Manage AI Agents Effectively](sources/departmentofproduct-managing-ai-agents.md): Uber gives each agent its own cryptographic identity because "who authorised what" was lost across agent hops; Block's User Identity Delegation carries the human and the agent as two identities through every call. Second-hand. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use Claude Routines at work - a Guide for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-routines-for-product-teams.md): attached connectors are used, writes included, with no per-action approval, so the connector list is the run's permission boundary (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [Community Wisdom: Evaluating startup equity ... MCPs vs. CLIs ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-knowledge-graph-mcp-cli.md): agent-built API skills pass credentials through inference; CLIs and MCP OAuth keep them out of model context (Thread 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The coming AI security crisis | Sander Schulhoff](sources/lenny-podcast-sander-schulhoff-ai-security.md): "any data that AI has access to, the user can make it leak it. Any actions that it can possibly take, the user can make it take" (48:49) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte](sources/lenny-podcast-roman-ugarte-grok-bot.md): each bot gets its own computer and credentials; sharing the user's machine is like sharing a laptop and credentials with a new hire forever (31:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How OpenAI uses ChatGPT Sites (Kath Korevec)](sources/howiai-openai-korevec-chatgpt-sites.md): a shared site renders each viewer's own data through their own connector grants: "you see only your data on that site" (1:32, 8:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): agent gets its own email and read-only calendar; with external channels it "might even impersonate you" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Webflow's CPO built an AI chief of staff](sources/howiai-webflow-rachel-wolan-chief-of-staff.md): personal agent on the CPO's own Google API tokens with per-scope limits; "too much authority to act on my behalf" trimmed back by hand (11:26-12:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-claire-vo-openclaw.md): progressive trust like an EA: calendar, then read email, draft, send; agent listens only to one person on one channel (22:20-23:51) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Amplitude MCP in Claude Code (Amplitude docs)](sources/amplitude-mcp-claude-code-docs.md): server inherits the authenticating user's Amplitude permissions and grants nothing extra. (user-story-mapping)
- [Dovetail MCP (Dovetail developer docs)](sources/dovetail-mcp-server-docs.md): access matches the user's own account/role (from search summary of the main Dovetail help page). (user-story-mapping)
- [Snowflake-managed MCP server (Snowflake docs)](sources/snowflake-managed-mcp-server-docs.md): 'Access to the MCP Server does not give access to the tools'; each tool needs its own grant; users sign in with own credentials. (user-story-mapping)
- [Notion MCP (Notion developer docs)](sources/notion-mcp-developer-docs.md): workspace owners manage allowed MCP clients in Settings; restricting clients requires Enterprise; org owners can list/revoke members' connections via Admin API. (user-story-mapping)
- [Getting started with the Atlassian Rovo MCP server](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-getting-started.md): OAuth 2.1 primary; actions respect each user's existing access controls; API token optional. (user-story-mapping)
- [Linear for Agents (developer docs)](sources/linear-developers-agents.md): assigning an issue to an agent sets it as delegate; the human stays assignee. (user-story-mapping)
- [What are Confluence's roles?](sources/atlassian-confluence-roles-space-permissions.md): role-based space access (Admin, Manager, Collaborator, Viewer, custom); public links, guest access and anonymous access are separate admin grants; 'you can't assign or remove roles that include permissions you don't have.' (user-story-mapping)
- [Add or remove page restrictions (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-page-restrictions.md): per-item states open / edit-restricted / restricted / restricted-by-parent; view restrictions inherit to children, edit restrictions do not; the Rovo MCP server can read and set these states. (user-story-mapping)

## intent-factory-before-discovery: Accelerate the intent factory before discovery
Automating intent refinement and delivery has to come before using AI for higher-order discovery, or more ideas just swell the backlog. This sets the order of priorities for what a product agent should do first.
- [A field guide to Claude Fable 5: Finding your unknowns](sources/claude-fable-finding-unknowns.md): four-quadrant framing (known knowns, known unknowns, unknown knowns, unknown unknowns) as the start of every task ("Knowing your unknowns"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): with 20 engineers per PM, the PM adds more by improving "the why and the what ... by 5%" than by shipping features (47:52-49:30) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Quarterly planning and AI ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-quarterly-planning.md): with day-long builds, planning "moved downstream of the evidence instead of upstream of it"; counterpoint: large-org planning is coordination and customer change-absorption (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino](sources/lenny-podcast-ambrosino-codex-product-work.md): plan detail inversely proportional to horizon; prototype every idea and re-test each at every model leap; the Codex app would have failed three months earlier with the same shape (32:00, 33:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why humans are AI's biggest bottleneck (Alexander Embiricos)](sources/lenny-podcast-embiricos-codex-human-bottleneck.md): with building easy, the scarce competency is "really meaningful understanding of the problems that a certain customer has" (54:18) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How PMs are using AI coding tools](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-pms-ai-coding-tools.md): a "project manager" agent with its own context checks the requirements "for dependencies and unanswered questions" before build agents start (thread 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: When AI velocity outpaces your product strategy ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-velocity-strategy.md): "building got cheap, but confusion didn't ... slow down on decisions, not on execution"; "what to ship" and "whether to ship" converging (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: speeding up discovery in a big org](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-discovery-big-org.md): once designs change in an afternoon, "the constraint becomes how fast someone can decide"; a one-line decisions log (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why LinkedIn is turning PMs into AI-powered "full stack builders"](sources/lenny-podcast-tomer-cohen-full-stack-builder.md): research meant "10 to 15 sources of information" and stacked reviews (design, privacy, security) made small features take six months; "the work itself is not complex, but the process we made very complex" (7:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): with ~90% of code AI-written, "there's an upstream bottleneck, which is decision making and alignment"; Krieger seeks a "minimum viable strategy" and hasn't got it right (14:25) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [An AI state of the union (Simon Willison)](sources/lenny-podcast-simon-willison-state-of-ai.md): spec-to-implementation went from "three weeks" to "maybe ... three hours"; "Now the bottlenecks are everywhere else" (21:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From Figma to Claude Code and back](sources/howiai-figma-design-code-loop.md): Figma's design role "really moved upstream" to planning and "what should we be building", because building is faster (19:11) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [AI is critical for humanity's survival (Jeetu Patel)](sources/lenny-podcast-jeetu-patel-cisco-ai.md): Cisco: coding is the clear win, but other functions are "not as easy" (6:47) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: when engineering outpaces product](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-engineering-outpaces-product.md): a fully AI-enabled team's engineers ship so fast "the bottleneck becomes writing specs/stories fast enough"; one engineer shipped every feature from a call transcript to staging before scoping, half judged bloat; "decision-making velocity" now hurts more than delivery velocity (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How AI is reshaping the product role (Udezue)](sources/lenny-podcast-udezue-ai-reshaping-pm-role.md): fixed PM-to-engineering time ratios are "exploding"; a client goes from pitch call to prototype in four hours; "PRD writing is insufficient at the moment" (8:37) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Shape Up (Ryan Singer)](sources/lenny-podcast-ryan-singer-shape-up.md): projects fail to ship because "the input at the very beginning of the process is too unclear"; the dominant failure is "not enough detail" (47:26, 1:38:37) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): the core thesis and order of operations (§Introduction) (research-product-agent-and-harness)

## leadership-permission-mandate: Leadership permission and mandates drive AI-native ways of working
New ways of working with agents (no specs, prototypes before meetings, PMs and designers shipping code) spread only when leaders explicitly permit or mandate them, and change hiring, reviews and rituals to match; tools alone get the top ~5%. No existing slug fits: enablement-by-product is about the product teaching its own use, and org-learning-loop is about sharing wins, not authority and incentives. Bears on the adoption-model dimension.
- [No Figma. No Jira. No docs. How Gusto built a new product line with Claude Code](sources/howiai-gusto-eddie-kim-cofounder.md): Gusto's CTO says teams that skip specs "might get a slap on the wrist"; to scale he'd forbid docs and Figma outright because teams "don't feel like they're allowed to" (41:12) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why LinkedIn is turning PMs into AI-powered "full stack builders"](sources/lenny-podcast-tomer-cohen-full-stack-builder.md): 20% tech, 80% change management; only the "cutting edge 5%" adopt unaided; AI agency and fluency added to hiring and biannual reviews; cross-functional 360s for directs (38:24-44:45) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Webflow's CPO built an AI chief of staff](sources/howiai-webflow-rachel-wolan-chief-of-staff.md): "you can't get into a meeting with me without a prototype"; mandate plus bottom-up early adopters; career ladder being rewritten (32:34, 40:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why cultivating agency matters more than cultivating skills](sources/lenny-podcast-max-schoening-agency.md): Notion's head of product is surprised "how much prodding" it takes for people to enlist agents in the outer loop of their work; sympathetic to leaderboards at large scale (36:52) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [2× – nine months later: We did it](sources/ideas-fin-2x-nine-months-later.md): CTO goal to 2x R&D productivity in 12 months; "All technical work is becoming agent-first. This is the top priority for R&D."; adoption targets with short deadlines (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## legible-org-for-agents: Make the organisation legible to agents
Roadmaps, specs, tickets and tools must be agent-readable so agents can answer and act. Related: [[compounding-context-repo]].
- [What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-geoff-charles-product-when-coding-solved.md): "the organization needs to be legible to your agents"; Gadget (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): shared internal tool catalog of hundreds of tools (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Meet Ramp Research: Our Agentic Data Analyst](sources/ramp-builders-meet-ramp-research.md): domain owners wrote docs as a file system the data agent reads; dbt/Looker/Snowflake metadata indexed (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): 2024 monorepo + Nix bets; "agent-friendly ≈ human-friendly"; "The work to make a codebase legible to an agent is simply the debt you owe to your human engineers" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Shopify powers "World" (Flagship)](sources/flagship-ai-first-series-2-shopify-tectonix-nix.md): Nix reproducibility narrows agent build errors to pure code errors (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): org chart, projects/OKRs and a tiered data catalog are what let Kai 'do the right thing' without users explaining their job (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): Orbit plans by 'reading files in our code base, it's reading Trailhead' (internal docs); Compass tracks projects (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Inside Stripe's Engineering Culture: Part 2](sources/pragmaticengineer-inside-stripe-engineering-culture-part-2.md): pre-AI internal tools: Trailhead (docs structured like the external docs), Compass (project status, linked docs, standups), Home intranet search (2024) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Lessons from Anthropic on building effective human-agent teams](sources/claude-building-effective-human-agent-teams.md): write artifacts and meeting notes "so that agents can find them, since agents are now a primary consumer of team documentation" (Lesson 1 list). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Claude Code works in large codebases: Best practices and where to start](sources/claude-code-large-codebases.md): upfront investment in making the codebase legible; path-scoped skills; committed permissions.deny rules (navigability section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Atlassian builds AI agents teams can trust with Claude and Google Cloud](sources/claude-customers-atlassian-trusted-agents.md): "How do I make sure agents are an equivalent customer of our software?" (Sherif Mansour, "The challenge"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Office Hours: Asynchronous coding and the end of the IDE with Spotify](sources/claude-customers-spotify-office-hours.md): standardisation of codebases, tools and frameworks, done for humans, makes agents work better; "if they look ten different ways, Claude is going to be more confused" (advice segment). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Turning conversation into knowledge: how Slack builds human-agent teams](sources/claude-slack-human-agent-teams.md): ask agents to reconstruct why a decision was made, not just what; widen connected surfaces (meetings, email, calendars, docs) so the team repeats itself less (section "Treat your conversation history"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [What is a Command Line Interface and why do they suddenly matter to product teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-cli-for-product-teams.md): an API leaves conventions to the caller, while a CLI exposes the vendor's recommended patterns as commands; "a distribution channel for the agent economy" (Stripe Projects, Save to Spotify, Ramp CLI) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Why Semantic Data Layers matter](sources/departmentofproduct-semantic-data-layers.md): the semantic layer turns company vocabulary (activation, new user, PII) into versioned, owned definitions that agents and BI tools query alike. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): personal "notebook channels" feed Claude; HR onboarding docs carry an owner-check warning because Claude references them (1:28:22-1:29:52) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Evaluating startup equity ... MCPs vs. CLIs ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-knowledge-graph-mcp-cli.md): build "a living product/org memory for onboarding and AI agents" from a small entity set, not an ontology-first graph (Thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Successfully coding with AI in large enterprises (LaunchDarkly)](sources/howiai-launchdarkly-zach-davis-enterprise-coding.md): "what's good for humans is also good for LLMs" as documentation principle (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers (Elizabeth Stone)](sources/lenny-podcast-elizabeth-stone-netflix-systems-thinkers.md): shift from local stacks to "preferred paved paths" so agents across systems get source-of-truth data; "can no longer rely on tribal knowledge" (13:43-17:38) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why half of product managers are in trouble (Nikhyl Singhal)](sources/lenny-podcast-nikhyl-singhal-half-of-pms.md): alignment with "less theatrics" because "the CEO can literally ask their agent" for ground truth (1:13:25) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How I built LennyRPG](sources/lenny-newsletter-how-i-built-lennyrpg.md): Lenny released ~350 posts and ~300 transcripts as Markdown plus an MCP server for agents (intro) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [This CPO regrets that product management exists (Tom Verrilli)](sources/lenny-podcast-tom-verrilli-whatnot-pm.md): firms underinvested in data engineering and labelling; data scientists now fix tracking and taxonomy so self-serve AI analysis is less misread (41:49) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Zapier's EA built an army of AI interns](sources/howiai-zapier-ea-cortney-hickey.md): a NotebookLM "strategy companion" makes company strategy "accessible and interactive for all employees" (33:15, show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How AI is changing product operating models](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-operating-models.md): interest in systems that keep shared organisational context ("same understanding of what's important and why") rather than standalone assistants (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-claire-vo-openclaw.md): agent failure is visible in its files ("Does it have this information?"); if an agent can't tell which projects are doing well, neither can a new hire (1:27:32) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How eight people hold the bar for 200+ builders](sources/ideas-fin-eight-people-hold-the-bar.md): with the design-system knowledge layer, agent use of existing components went 7% → 96% and typecheck pass 0% → 74% (self-reported) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How we design when the code writes itself](sources/ideas-fin-how-we-design-when-code-writes-itself.md): "Design system as agentic infrastructure"; the Surge playground lets designers prototype with production components (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
