- [Teamwork Graph glossary (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-glossary.md): the graph is explicitly the layer that links work data across Atlassian apps and connected external tools (Core concepts, 'Teamwork Graph'). (user-story-mapping)
- [Teamwork Graph object types (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-object-types.md): a fixed set of connector object types lets Rovo Search/Chat treat Asana tasks, Figma files and Google events uniformly. (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian Rovo MCP server: supported tools](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-supported-tools.md): agents can read work items, projects, boards, sprints, pages, whiteboards, databases, goals and projects. (user-story-mapping)
- [What is a Jira space (formerly project)](sources/atlassian-jira-space-definition.md): 'A Jira space is a collection of related work items' for a product, team, service or project; items carry a space key prefix (e.g. GDT-1). (user-story-mapping)
- [Working with databases (Notion API docs)](sources/notion-api-databases-data-sources.md): schema lives on the data source so an agent can read property types. (user-story-mapping)
- [Projects (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-projects.md): Project = 'a grouping of issues that have a clear outcome or planned completion date'. (user-story-mapping)
- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-initiatives.md): Initiatives are workspace-level containers for projects tied to a shared objective; IDs like I-<n>. (user-story-mapping)
- [Documents (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-documents.md): Documents attach to projects, initiatives, teams, issues or cycles; same editor as issues; realtime collaboration; version history including agent edits; templates at workspace/team level. (user-story-mapping)
- [About Projects (GitHub Docs)](sources/github-docs-about-projects.md): Project = adaptable table, board and roadmap integrating issues and PRs, at user or organisation level; two-way sync with issues. (user-story-mapping)
- [Glean Enterprise Graph (product page)](sources/glean-enterprise-graph-product-page.md): entities are inferred automatically by machine learning rather than declared. (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian Rovo MCP server: supported tools](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-supported-tools.md): verbatim re-read: getTeamworkGraphContext returns 'all relationships and linked objects in one traversal' from Jira, Confluence, Goals/Projects/Focus Areas, people, DevOps, Loom, Compass entry points; Confluence spaces carry agent-readable 'space instructions' (getConfluenceSpaceInstructions / setConfluenceSpaceInstructions). (user-story-mapping)
- [Scopes (Teamwork Graph API)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-scopes.md): 'All Teamwork Graph API scopes are read-only'; a missing scope returns success and empty rows ('fails closed rather than leaking data'), so an agent cannot tell 'no data' from 'no permission'. (user-story-mapping)

## memory-architecture: Memory as inspectable files from an offline pipeline
Agent memory built on first connection, refreshed by a periodic pipeline, read-only during sessions.
- [How We Built Glass: Vibe Coding a Product Used by 700 People](sources/x-shanebuchan-how-we-built-glass.md): 24h pipeline, write-once-read-many memory files (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): memory built from authenticated connections, 24h synthesis and cleanup (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): River "dreams" off-hours over the day's threads and rewrites skill files; per-person and per-channel memory injected at session start (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): the work ledger is "useful memory, but it isn't the operational truth"; each entry a claim to re-check (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Stripe Built Kai on Deep Agents (LangChain)](sources/langchain-how-stripe-built-kai-deep-agents.md): Kai keeps session state in an S3-backed virtual filesystem; sandbox calls sync files in and out so the agent sees one persistent file environment per session (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): only the conversation history is restored when an expired environment is reopened; running shell commands, subagents and session-scoped scheduled tasks are not (Environment expired) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): the session log is the durable store outside the context window; getEvents() allows positional slices and rewind; irreversible compaction is avoided in the store (Session as durable event store) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Long-running agents (Cloudflare Agents SDK docs)](sources/cloudflare-agents-long-running-agents.md): state survives via setState/this.sql/scheduled tasks/fiber stash; lost: in-memory fields, timers, in-flight fetches, closures (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Code deletes conversation history after 30 days by default](sources/itdaily-claude-code-30-day-transcript-deletion.md): cleanupPeriodDays defaults to 30, run on each startup; users say there is no warning or recovery; deletion keys on file modification time so backups or sync can trigger removal of active files (per GitHub discussions cited) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [LangGraph persistence (checkpointers, threads, stores)](sources/langchain-langgraph-persistence.md): checkpointers keep thread-scoped state keyed by thread_id; stores hold cross-thread data (preferences, facts); a parent graph may not see subgraph state immediately because of checkpoint namespaces (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The AI Agent Doom Loop: Why Your Agent Keeps Making the Same Mistake](sources/unblocked-agent-doom-loop.md): claims shared team context must be automatic, reasoned (the why), current and cross-source; CLAUDE.md-style files 'help only partly' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Effective harnesses for long-running agents](sources/anthropic-effective-harnesses-long-running-agents.md): first-party: feature list, progress file, git history and init script as cross-session handoff memory (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus](sources/manus-context-engineering-lessons.md): first-party: filesystem as external context, todo recitation (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Hosting the Agent SDK](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-hosting.md): first-party: SessionStore mirrors transcripts only; CLAUDE.md memory and working-dir artifacts need separate storage and leak across tenants by default (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): every thread adds to and draws from a shared project memory (e.g. release moved to Friday, why the export was dropped, who to check with before touching billing); also remembers working and communication style. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agent harness design: 3 patterns for harnessing Claude's intelligence](sources/claude-harness-design-three-patterns.md): prefers model-chosen persistence (compaction, a memory folder of files) over retrieval infrastructure; Opus 4.6 Pokémon memory: 10 organised files and a learnings file versus Sonnet 3.5's 31 transcript-like files (Pattern 2,... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [New in Claude Managed Agents: dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration](sources/claude-managed-agents-dreaming-outcomes.md): memory captures learnings per agent; dreaming "refines that memory between sessions, pulling shared learnings across agents"; can update automatically or have changes reviewed first (§Build self-improving agents with dreaming). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Memory for Claude Managed Agents: agents that learn across sessions](sources/claude-managed-agents-memory.md): memory mounts onto a filesystem so the agent uses bash and code execution on it; memories are files exportable and manageable by API (sections "How memory works", "Portable memories"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude's memory works everywhere, and you decide what's in it](sources/claude-memory-everywhere.md): memory updates "as you chat" rather than by post-conversation summary; stored as a list of short files under Topics that the user can read, edit, delete, pause or reset ("Memory updates as you chat"; "See and edit"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](sources/claude-steering-claude-code.md): per-method compaction behaviour (root CLAUDE.md re-read after compaction; invoked skills re-injected up to a shared budget, oldest dropped first; hooks bypass compaction) (summary table). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude](sources/claude-warp-self-improving-agents.md): sidebar distinguishes skills (procedural, stable, changed deliberately) from memory (auto-written at inference time, always changing). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Zero Trust for AI agents](sources/claude-zero-trust-for-ai-agents.md): Ch 06 Phase 7 memory isolation, hash-based context integrity checks at every retrieval, source tagging, TTLs and versioned memory rollback. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): a reflection agent rewrites one markdown memory file per product area each cycle (worked, didn't, what the team keeps rejecting) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use Claude Routines at work - a Guide for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-routines-for-product-teams.md): the competitor tracker keeps state between runs as a snapshot file in the repo and diffs against it each run (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use /loops, /goals and other Powerful Slash Commands as a Non-Engineer](sources/departmentofproduct-loops-goals-slash-commands.md): /init writes CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as a standing project briefing read at the start of every session (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Community Wisdom: Evaluating startup equity ... MCPs vs. CLIs ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-knowledge-graph-mcp-cli.md): plain markdown vault as agent memory; members warn it turns to noise within weeks without a trusted vs captured split (Thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino](sources/lenny-podcast-ambrosino-codex-product-work.md): users build Obsidian/Notion "mind palaces" for agents; "You shouldn't have to do that. There should be a memory feature" (47:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of ChatGPT ... | Tibo Sottiaux](sources/lenny-podcast-sottiaux-chatgpt-dots.md): Dots combines two-plus years of coherent-memory research with the Codex harness and 24/7 running (15:14) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Code for product managers (Teresa Torres)](sources/howiai-teresa-torres-claude-code-pm.md): small topic context files behind index files, routed from a global CLAUDE.md; project-level CLAUDE.md holds the tag taxonomy (11:29, 28:42-30:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Community Wisdom: ... AI agents and data integrity ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-agents-data-integrity.md): inspectable semantic layer that the agent may update when prompted, as it learns in conversation (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Grok Bot designers use AI agents ...](sources/howiai-grok-bot-designers-agents.md): after a failure, tell the bot to "memorize this" so it follows the learned script next time (39:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Code with Claude: The 5 biggest updates explained](sources/howiai-code-with-claude-updates.md): Anthropic's "Dreams" memory system pitched for long-term agent behaviour (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-memory-docs.md): CLAUDE.md (human-written instructions) vs auto memory (Claude-written learnings; first 200 lines or 25KB loaded each session). (user-story-mapping)

## meta-harness: Meta harness
A layer that runs, governs or abstracts over several harnesses.
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): harness is explicitly treated as replaceable behind stable interfaces ('brains' stateless, 'hands' = execute(name,input)->string); cited example: context resets needed for Sonnet 4.5 became unnecessary with Opus 4.5 (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CData on Managed Agents](sources/cdata-claude-managed-agents-meta-harness.md): independent-ish: frames Managed Agents as a meta-harness and lists lock-in, memory/trace portability and reliability as trade-offs. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: Omnigent analysed as the first meta-harness; claims harnesses are becoming importable SDKs while framework vendors ship harnesses (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AI SDK: Agents overview](sources/vercel-ai-sdk-agents-docs.md): first-party: a general SDK adding a HarnessAgent adapter for Claude Code, Codex, Pi (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Introducing Omnigent](sources/databricks-omnigent-meta-harness-launch.md): defines the horizontal sense: a layer 'above the agents you already use' with composition, control, collaboration (vendor claim, 2026-06-13, Apache-2.0 alpha) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [omnigent-ai/omnigent repo](sources/github-omnigent-repo.md): runner + server, 13+ harnesses, 12 sandbox providers, ~11k stars; open issues include sharing not separating chat from host access (#11413) and OIDC/Entra login failing (first-party repo, 2026-10-24) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Contextual Policies in Omnigent](sources/databricks-omnigent-contextual-policies.md): stateful allow/deny/ask policies applied across every wrapped agent (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Atlan Omnigent explainer](sources/atlan-omnigent-explainer.md): alpha OSS, Beta on Databricks; harness support tiers; advises a pilot, not a standard (vendor-biased) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [HN Omnigent thread](sources/hn-omnigent-launch-thread.md): 15 points, 4 comments; little organic discussion found (anecdote) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents](sources/anthropic-scaling-managed-agents.md): Anthropic's own text calls Managed Agents 'a meta-harness' (2026-04-08), so the term predates Omnigent in first-party use (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CodePick buyer's guide](sources/codepick-meta-harness-guide.md): term is NOT settled; horizontal (compose harnesses) vs vertical (optimise one harness's code) senses; no standard yet (independent) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Meta-Harness paper](sources/arxiv-meta-harness-optimization.md): the vertical sense: an outer-loop optimiser over harness code (arXiv 2026-03-30) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Daniel Vaughan: Pi as coordinator](sources/danielvaughan-meta-harness-pattern-pi.md): DIY meta-harness via `codex exec`/`claude -p`; cost fan-out ~23-25 sessions, debugging opacity, approvals bypassed in shared CI (independent practitioner) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Garrit Franke](sources/garrit-meta-harness-parallel-agents.md), [Claude Squad](sources/github-claude-squad.md), [Conductor](sources/conductor-build-homepage.md): 'meta harness' in practice often means a local parallel-session manager (worktrees, notifications), with no governance layer (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vibe Kanban shutdown](sources/vibekanban-shutdown.md): orchestrator UI company shut down 2026-04-10 for lack of a business model; local app continues community-maintained (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Nx Polygraph](sources/nx-polygraph-meta-harness.md): another vendor use: agent-agnostic, repository graph + session graph (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Warp Oz multi-harness](sources/warp-oz-multi-harness.md): hosted/self-hostable control plane running Claude Code, Codex and Warp Agent with shared audit and credit caps (vendor claim, 2026-05-20) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare Flue / Agents SDK](sources/cloudflare-flue-agents-platform.md): platform-level layering (framework / harness / runtime); does not wrap Claude Code or Codex (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Customize Claude Code with mods in TypeScript](sources/claude-code-mods.md): harness behaviour itself is replaceable; built-in features shipping as mods; plan to "pare Claude Code down to a small core" (section "Swap built-in features"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Cresta turned CX expertise into an agent builder on the Claude Agent SDK](sources/claude-cresta-agent-builder-evals.md): Conductor is "a self-improving meta-agent" that helps developers build and improve other agents (§A meta-agent that helps build the next agent). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): presents the Stanford Meta-Harness optimiser to PMs as "self-improving harnesses" (the optimiser sense of the term); calls it not production-ready (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [Community Wisdom: sharing Claude Code skills across the org](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-sharing-skills.md): a member's company distributes a Go "meta-harness" orchestrating dozens of opencode sessions with plan/implement/review/QA roles, file-based handoff, TUI and headless CI modes (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## one-job-per-agent: One job per agent
Scoping an agent to one defined job (with human in the loop) for consistency and evals. In tension with [[single-agent-many-skills]].
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Stripe: 'keep agents specialized (on research, coding, or browser-native tools) while exposing them to capabilities in other systems' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [12-Factor Agents, factor 10](sources/humanlayer-12-factor-agents-small-focused-agents.md): first-party: small focused agents (about 3-10 steps) because LLMs lose focus as context grows; scope grows only as quality holds (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Measuring Agents in Production](sources/arxiv-measuring-agents-in-production.md): independent: 68% of deployed agents execute at most 10 steps before human intervention; reliability is the top challenge (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Orchestrating AI Code Review at scale](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): first-party: seven narrow specialist reviewers plus a coordinator beat one big prompt; 'what not to flag' per specialist (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Don't Build Multi-Agents](sources/cognition-dont-build-multi-agents.md): reconciliation note: its objection is to splitting interdependent work across parallel agents, not to bounded single-job agents (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How ABC Legal turned every employee into a builder with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-abc-legal-managed-agents-builders.md): "Each agent has a name, an owner, and a single job"; most of the fleet are single-task runners ("Bridging the technical divide"; "harvest, tune, repeat"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Lessons from Anthropic on building effective human-agent teams](sources/claude-building-effective-human-agent-teams.md): Lesson 2: separate agents own data analysis, design-standard enforcement, research synthesis, release management; roles defined in skill files so others can stand up the same agent type. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Notion ships and scales agents with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-notion-managed-agents.md): "a Claude agent for each stage: one that investigates, one that plans, and one that builds", each with own permissions, context and automations (Q&A, "army of agents"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop](sources/claude-fold-subagents-into-main-loop.md): sharpens the counter-case: subagents kept only for measurable context bloat, parallel discardable work, or tool-selection or instruction conflicts; split by context, not by problem type, to avoid a "telephone game" (intro;... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Multi-agent coordination patterns: Five approaches and when to use them](sources/claude-multi-agent-coordination-patterns.md): orchestrator-subagent dispatches distinct checks (security, test coverage, style, architecture) to specialised subagents in a code-review example (Pattern 2). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How a non-technical project manager built and shipped a stress management app with Claude Code in six weeks](sources/claude-nontechnical-pm-ships-app.md): a self-built set of 15+ specialised subagents (TCA architect, Swift developer, Metal specialist, code reviewer and more) running in parallel across modules ("Managing agents like people"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Multi Agent Architecture explained](sources/departmentofproduct-multi-agent-architecture.md): the 2025 case for multi-agent: a single agent is "overwhelmed" by too many tools and too much context (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte](sources/lenny-podcast-roman-ugarte-grok-bot.md): users ran 5-10 lane-scoped bots, then promoted one to "chief of staff" that fans tasks out; the vendor encouraged it only after users found it unprompted (12:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Communication architectures ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-communication-architectures.md): call-transcript pipeline runs one LLM call per analysis job ("separation of concerns") for more consistent results at higher token cost (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## opportunity-to-code-chain: Opportunity → problem → goal → intent → plan → code
A stage chain for product work, drawn by a Stripe engineer, in which agents today own the lower stages (intent research, plan, code, review) and people own the upper ones (opportunity, problem, goal) through customer conversations. It gives the strategy a spine: where each agent sits, where hand-offs and artifacts are, and where captured context must feed in.
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): whiteboard at ~12:24 reads Opportunity → Problem → Goal → Intent → Plan, with a brace over Problem and Goal labelled (partly legible) "Customer conv…"; "This is the part that today is happening a lot more in Orbit now"; the plan is then handed to a minion to code (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): Geoff's eight-step Stripe/Ramp loop starts at informal intent and runs to staged release; Stripe's chain adds the three human stages above intent (opportunity, problem, goal) that the loop leaves implicit (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's Internal Agent Ecosystem for Product Development](sources/claude-doc-geoff-stripe-internal-agent-ecosystem.md): Geoff's flow maps Kai (research), Harbor/Protodash (prototype), Orbit (plan), Minions (build), review agent plus human onto the same chain (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [AI didn't write our SDK. It changed how we built it.](sources/stripe-ai-didnt-write-our-sdk.md): between intent and code, agents draft specs that humans review as GitHub issues before implementation (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Intercom Fin NPI](sources/intercom-fin-npi-agent-readiness.md): adds a step after code: shipped work is written back into the agent's knowledge, tested, and monitored for 2-4 weeks (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Eight trends defining how software gets built in 2026](sources/claude-2026-agentic-coding-trends.md): the agentic SDLC starts at "express intent" and ends with humans "defining the problems worth solving"; problem selection stays human, but the report says nothing on how intent is shaped (Foreword; Trend 1). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): the chain is intent.md → spec.md → plan.md → diff and tests → PR with findings → incident record → new intent.md; "each stage ends by writing one to version control ... and the next stage begins by reading it" (§What is an... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How CodeRabbit used Claude to build an agent orchestration system](sources/claude-coderabbit-plan-orchestration.md): a planning phase before code generation; the plan "becomes a quality gate" (sections "An orchestration layer", "Catching errors before any code gets written"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inside Rakuten's plan to turn every employee into a builder with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-rakuten-every-employee-builder.md): feedback agent chats with users and creates tickets; another agent or humans triage; if accepted, agents help finalise the PRD, wireframe or prototype, iterating to success criteria (task system answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Sentry built end-to-end bug fixing with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-sentry-bug-fixing-agents.md): covers the tail of the chain for bugs: telemetry to root cause to plan to code to PR, with the handoff between diagnosis and coding agent as Sentry's differentiating design work (section "How the Seer-to-PR workflow runs"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The founder's playbook: Building an AI-native startup](sources/claude-founders-playbook.md): Idea stage is an explicit ordered chain (is the problem real, who has it, who else solves it, what must a solution do) before Claude Code is used; the prototype comes last and is a "pressure-testing prop" for user... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [What are Claude Skills and how can you use them for product-related work?](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-skills-for-product-work.md): Notion's Spec to Implementation skill goes spec, plan page, 42 tracked tasks, then Claude Code status updates, but assumes the whole cycle lives in Notion (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): signal → judge → spec (codebase-checked, complexity-tagged) → routed to Claude Code or Linear → review agent checks the PR against the spec's acceptance criteria and instrumentation (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): research → shortlist → PRD → screens → stakeholder PowerPoint, all in one Claude Code session over the Stitch MCP (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical Agent Skills for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-practical-agent-skills.md): compound-engineering splits brainstorm (what), plan (how) and work, with an artifact between each stage. Atlassian's official skill turns a Confluence spec into a Jira epic plus tickets and shows the breakdown for approval first (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [The non-technical PM's guide to building with Cursor | Zevi Arnovitz](sources/lenny-podcast-zevi-arnovitz-cursor-pm.md): slash-command chain create issue → exploration (clarifying questions only) → plan (TL;DR, decisions, tasks) → execute → review → peer review → update docs (15:00-48:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): Krieger's chain: model reads Discord, forums and X for "what's emergent", proposes fixes, opens a PR, spins up an A/B test; limited by context flow, not reasoning (19:20-20:51) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: What to do when non-PMs start shipping](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-non-pms-shipping.md): canonical chain (goal, opportunity, selection, solution, design, build, release) still holds; "prototyping is just solution identification"; what changes is who's involved at each stage (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Shape Up (Ryan Singer)](sources/lenny-podcast-ryan-singer-shape-up.md): demand-side JTBD research, then framing ("calendar" becomes "see empty spaces"), then shaping within an appetite, then a whole idea to a team that writes its own tasks (40:36, 1:38:37) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## org-context-grounding: Agents work when grounded in organisation context
Successful PM agents read the organisation's own data (docs, tickets, calls, code); thin context yields generic output. Related: [[compounding-context-repo]], [[harness-over-model]].
- [Meet Ramp Research: Our Agentic Data Analyst](sources/ramp-builders-meet-ramp-research.md): grounding in dbt, Looker and Snowflake metadata plus domain-owner docs (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How To Build Agents Users Can Trust](sources/ramp-builders-agents-users-can-trust.md): customer's expense policy brought in as editable context the agent cites (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): Kai knows the user and org chart by default, reads the project-management system, and connects Drive, Slack and DMs only if the user opts in (toggleable per session) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Emily Glassberg Sands on Latent Space](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): Hubert (text-to-SQL) failed most at data discovery; fixed by deprecating low-quality tables, owner-written docs, and org-position persona context (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How can we help everyone become a 10x engineer? (Stripe Sessions 2024)](sources/stripe-sessions-2024-10x-engineer-panel.md): Stripe put an LLM bot over Trailhead only after owners verified docs and the hierarchy was trusted, so answers 'were going to be accurate' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [The 2026 State of AI Agents Report](sources/claude-2026-state-of-ai-agents.md): Economic Index section says each 1% more input context is associated with 0.38% higher output quality/length, and calls data accessibility and context aggregation the main barrier (ch. 6, "Context is the real bottleneck"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic enables self-service data analytics with Claude](sources/claude-anthropic-self-service-analytics.md): four "sources of truth" in descending trust (semantic layer, lineage, query corpus, business context via a company knowledge graph of docs, roadmaps, decision logs and org structure) (Sources of truth). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How a $2 billion venture fund made Claude Cowork its shared firm infrastructure](sources/claude-customers-airtree-cowork.md): value "scales with the number of systems you connect it to": Notion, Slack, Drive, Affinity, Gmail, Granola, Harmonic, Canva, Webflow, plus a partner's personal CRM exposed to colleagues via a custom MCP (Q&A, "biggest win"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Atlassian builds AI agents teams can trust with Claude and Google Cloud](sources/claude-customers-atlassian-trusted-agents.md): Rovo Max draws on Teamwork Graph's map of billions of objects; demo agent followed Jira links to Figma and Google Docs to build a release reel ("The outcome"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Cyera on making Claude Cowork the front door to 40 tools](sources/claude-customers-cyera-cowork-front-door.md): a semantic layer of 30-40 documented Snowflake tables, one schema per department, role-level security by region, and a shared metric-definitions skill that fires in every team plugin before any query (Q&A, "keep it... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude's memory works everywhere, and you decide what's in it](sources/claude-memory-everywhere.md): examples include team metric definitions explained once in chat and reused in every QBR deck Cowork builds, and knowing the user's manager and their update preferences (same section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Self-service data analytics in Slack: how Anthropic deploys Claude Tag for ad-hoc questions](sources/claude-tag-self-service-analytics.md): wiring Claude Tag to an internal knowledge index (incidents, flags, release notes) to explain why a metric moved (section "Connect to business context"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Uber's CISO on building an insider threat program for AI](sources/claude-uber-ciso-insider-threat-ai.md): threat modelling improved as models gather context themselves from code, design docs and Jira history; vision of one agent per service that knows its threat model and talks to other services' agents. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Decision Models Explained - The New AI Building Block for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-decision-models.md): in Rippling's GrowthOS test a classifier won on email triage (90% vs 50%) but failed as a text-to-SQL control step because it couldn't read business definitions like "qualified pipeline"; hybrid recommended (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents Explained - a simple overview of the basics](sources/departmentofproduct-context-engineering-basics.md): calendar-agent example; a rich reply needs contacts, calendar, past threads and send tools (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Claude Cowork as a Competitive Intelligence System](sources/departmentofproduct-cowork-competitive-intelligence.md): recommends a "my-company" folder of strategy decks and OKRs and a competitor list kept as a file so the agent can judge strategic gaps (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Design is here](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-design.md): setup starts with a design system imported from a repo, code folder or .fig file. Claude extracts the components into an editable library (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Strategy Thought Partner](sources/departmentofproduct-strategy-thought-partner.md): a company-context settings page whose text feeds every analysis (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [AI's third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers](sources/lenny-podcast-tara-seshan-persistent-coworkers.md): a cloud agent without Docs, Slack and database access is like a hire "locked into a room"; data access and cloud infra matter as much as intelligence (18:47) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): weekly Cowork runs over Slack find cross-team misalignment that would have caused overlapping work (55:35, 1:03:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- ["Vibe analysis": How Faire's data team uses AI](sources/howiai-faire-vibe-analysis.md): a semantic layer so AI understands business data; Cursor as context engine over code (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya](sources/lenny-podcast-anish-acharya-company-loops.md): "anytime the model's making a mistake ... what do you know that it doesn't know?" Give the loop more context where it blocks (18:50-19:42) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Vibe coding as a team sport](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-vibe-coding-team-sport.md): all conversations transcribed and made available to agents, plus a shared agent-accessible context space; it "gets noisy fast, just like a codebase" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [I gave Claude Code our entire codebase | Al Chen](sources/howiai-galileo-al-chen-codebase-context.md): 15 repos opened at parent level plus Confluence and Slack MCPs; code as current source of truth beats docs (4:23-8:17) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Communication architectures ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-communication-architectures.md): off-the-shelf call recaps are "lackluster" without business context; custom prompts per business need (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Make product management fun again with AI agents](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-pm-agents.md): agents need where data lives, decision guidance and who is on which team, not the three-year vision (checklist item 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Quarterly planning and AI ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-quarterly-planning.md): "the prompt is rarely the hard part. Context governance is."; agents fail when they can't tell current vs stale, canonical vs discussed, decided vs open (thread 6) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to do AI analysis you can actually trust](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-analysis-you-can-trust.md): generic insights come from missing context; four parts needed: decision, business goal, product context, participant overview; more unstructured context doesn't help (Failure mode #2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's CPO on how AI changes must-have skills (Kevin Weil)](sources/lenny-podcast-kevin-weil-openai-cpo.md): "most of the world's data, knowledge, process is not public"; models need company data like a new hire's onboarding (22:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers (Elizabeth Stone)](sources/lenny-podcast-elizabeth-stone-netflix-systems-thinkers.md): encode source-of-truth data, how to interpret and access it, and what not to do with it (17:38) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build your PM second brain](sources/lenny-newsletter-pm-second-brain-chatgpt.md): context scattered across Slack, Notion, Monday boards, decks, Docs; "everything is essentially text" (Step 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Code for product managers (Teresa Torres)](sources/howiai-teresa-torres-claude-code-pm.md): "if we give it too much irrelevant context it's still going to not be very good at its job" (31:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How PMs are using AI coding tools](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-pms-ai-coding-tools.md): a 400+ line project file (data model, team contacts, release schedule, SQL conventions) loaded every session: "The agents aren't guessing" (thread 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Using AI to accelerate a team's velocity](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-team-velocity.md): shared team projects are valuable once you learn "how to build and maintain the right context" (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): Cowork step one is connecting Calendar, Slack, Gmail, Drive; design fidelity from the standard deck template's ~20 example slides (36:08-41:15) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Five proven prompt engineering techniques](sources/lenny-newsletter-prompt-engineering-techniques.md): retrieval of relevant documents into the prompt as a basic grounding tactic (Tactic 7) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why most AI products fail: Lessons from 50+ AI deployments](sources/lenny-podcast-reganti-badam-ai-deployments.md): messy enterprise taxonomies and "really weird rules ... not documented anywhere" block routing agents (52:46) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Build your personal AI copilot](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-ai-copilot.md): generic output came from missing context; onboard the copilot with strategy, research, org chart, retros, performance review (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Becoming an AI PM: Aman Khan](sources/lenny-podcast-aman-khan-becoming-ai-pm.md): on-call routing Slackbot failed because current project ownership context was missing (38:05) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: building a PM copilot](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-pm-copilot-context.md): "Maintaining context is constant manual work, and it's difficult or impossible to share context across your org" (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why LinkedIn is turning PMs into AI-powered "full stack builders"](sources/lenny-podcast-tomer-cohen-full-stack-builder.md): drive-wide access "failed miserably and hallucinates like crazy"; curated "gold examples" linking specs to outcomes worked (28:54, 48:21) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why cultivating agency matters more than cultivating skills](sources/lenny-podcast-max-schoening-agency.md): "agents need context to operate in" and "don't really like walls"; a connected workspace resembles a coding agent's Unix environment (vendor view, 49:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Amplitude built an internal AI tool](sources/howiai-amplitude-wade-chambers-moda.md): internal tool Moda searches Slack, Confluence, Jira, Salesforce, Zendesk, Drive, Productboard, Zoom, GitHub and more (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Webflow's CPO built an AI chief of staff](sources/howiai-webflow-rachel-wolan-chief-of-staff.md): Slack triage is "almost too much data to triage" even for current models (19:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): "The difference between the right context and not ... is entirely the difference between a good answer and a bad answer"; utility = intelligence × context/memory × apps/UI (54:45) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Zapier's EA built an army of AI interns](sources/howiai-zapier-ea-cortney-hickey.md): meeting-prep agent researches participants and checks HubSpot CRM before meetings (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Community Wisdom: How AI is changing product operating models](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-operating-models.md): without explicit goals, priorities, decisions and ownership "AI basically accelerates confusion" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Felix Rieseberg (Cowork)](sources/howiai-felix-rieseberg-cowork.md): a useful daily brief researches who you're meeting and what co-workers did on Slack, not a calendar summary (32:34) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Cursor for PM work](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-cursor-for-pm-work.md): the friction "isn't the change itself, it's the surrounding knowledge"; design systems and headless CMS lower agent risk (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How this PM uses MCPs to automate (How I AI)](sources/howiai-zapier-reid-robinson-mcp-pm-workflows.md): Claude Projects hold per-workflow tool order and CRM field meanings; meeting prep pulls product usage, sales history and Glean results (9:08-14:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to use AI to generate product requirements documents (Atticus Li)](sources/atticusli-ai-prd-generation.md): AI PRDs lack specificity; blamed mainly on missing context, partly on model habits (anecdotal) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [ChatPRD AI review (Banani)](sources/banani-chatprd-ai-review.md): Competitor BuildBetter: ChatPRD has no customer-evidence layer; output depends on the context the PM supplies [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

- [Ramp's AI build factory: 75% of pull requests now written by agents (Dealroom summary of Geoff Charles talk)](sources/dealroom-ramp-ai-build-factory-summary.md): Glass value rests on a written spec format, principles and connected systems. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [We gave Claude Code to everyone at Intercom](sources/intercom-we-gave-claude-code-to-everyone.md): 'guidance skills' teach Claude company metrics and table mappings. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Cursor is a much better product manager (Lenny's Newsletter)](sources/lenny-cursor-better-product-manager.md): Codebase grounding of PRDs (Builder.io); 'prototypes generic/disconnected' claim unverified [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Meta VP's personal agents (Lenny's Newsletter write-up of The Skip Podcast)](sources/lenny-newsletter-meta-chawla-pm-leader-agents.md): analytics agent answers data questions in about five minutes using queries the data scientist already wrote; depends on Meta's habit of documenting experiments. - [The bottleneck keeps shifting: what AI is changing about how we build (Gamma interview)](sources/atlassian-bottleneck-keeps-shifting-gamma.md): Documenting context for humans and agents is part of the PM's new bottleneck. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

Everybody changed their job.](sources/ideas-fin-nobody-changed-their-title.md): shared semantic layer being built so AI skills define metrics consistently; "shared, verified infrastructure for our AI tools is essential to their accuracy" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Teamwork Graph glossary (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-glossary.md): ACLs are specified per object that a connector adds, so permissions travel with the object. (user-story-mapping)

## org-learning-loop: One person's win becomes everyone's baseline
Skills, prompts and corrections made by one employee propagate to the team so the organisation learns once. Overlaps with [[compounding-context-repo]] (product context) but is about workflow/skills and shared sessions.
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): principle 2 and Dojo, 350+ skills (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): 323 employees, 6,500+ edits to what Glass knows; Finance taught it the UK-customer rule (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass. Make your entire company smarter](sources/ramp-introducing-glass.md): shareable sessions, 0:48-1:01 (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): L0-L3 ladder, leaderboards, center + spokes (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Inside Ramp's Custom Agent Operating System](sources/notion-inside-ramps-custom-agent-os.md): pre-Glass layer; sales feedback piped into Notion and triaged to the roadmap by agents (0:40-1:20) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Eric Glyman April 2026 posts on Glass and AI adoption](sources/x-eglyman-april-glass-posts.md): "when one person on a team figures out a better workflow, everyone on that team gets it" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Today, we're launching Glass (Geoff Charles X post)](sources/x-geoffintech-glass-launch.md): "Adoption, it turns out, is the easy part. The hard part is making AI work compound." (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass (Ramp X post)](sources/x-tryramp-introducing-glass.md): tagline contrasts individual speed with company-level learning (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Other Ramp (@tryramp) posts about Glass, Apr-May 2026](sources/x-tryramp-other-glass-posts.md): company-account amplification; Ramptables episode on the Glass builders (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): River refuses DMs so others learn by watching (Lehrwerkstatt); a checkout-warehouse skill reused by 12 teams; merge rate 36%→77% credited to people writing down what River should have known (self-reported) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi's replies about River](sources/x-tobi-river-replies-may-2026.md): "It's not about the transcript of the work. It's about seeing how other people begin the work with the ai" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): the public transcript corpus is mined and fed back into skills, prompts and defaults; "the privacy of an agent thread is a disadvantage" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): open channels only, to recreate office "osmosis learning"; "a late choice ... one of my favorite calls" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment](sources/shopify-engineering-remote-dev.md): the cheap "Jev" classifier tags every mobile River thread, scores outcomes, and failures feed an LLM to improve River (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Learning on the Shop floor (Simon Willison)](sources/simonwillison-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): compares River to Midjourney's public-Discord interface as a way to learn a finicky new skill (independent opinion) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [The Transparency Paradox (Bernstein)](sources/asq-bernstein-transparency-paradox.md): counter-evidence: broad visibility bred hiding; curtained lines +10–15% output; learning shared upward once there was data (independent, factory 2009) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify River (Ashgaliyev wiki)](sources/ashgaliyev-wiki-shopify-river.md): River as "organizational apprenticeship" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River: Shopify's Slack-native AI agent (video)](sources/youtube-shopify-river-slack-native-agent.md): official one-line positioning is the public-only constraint (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)

- [Stripe's payment method factory](sources/stripe-payment-method-factory.md): learning logs, decision logs, transcripts and PR comments from each run feed an agent that proposes updates to 100+ reusable prompts; an observer agent hardens prompts (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
