## product-artifact-primitives: Native PM artifact objects and project containers across platforms
What each platform treats as its first-class product-work objects (idea, initiative, project, space, spec, insight, document, skill) and how a 'project' is bounded. Matters for deciding whether a product meta-harness defines its own primitives or maps onto existing ones.
- [Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): project library collects files you add and artifacts Claude produces. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Cowork and chat are now one Claude](sources/claude-cowork-chat-unified.md): Claude Docs and Claude Slides launched (beta, paid plans), Claude Design available inside conversations; artifacts live at one shareable link, editable directly or by commenting to Claude, exportable to PowerPoint or PDF... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): HTML as the universal medium for decks, one-pagers, emails, animations, and "designs that are also their own editors" ("Make it alive"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Claude Projects and Skills to Monitor your Product's Health](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-projects-product-health.md): a Project (instructions, knowledge files, history) is the PM's standing container; filename prefixes stand in for structure (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Duet is beautiful. I still forgot to use it](sources/howiai-claire-vo-claude-duet-review.md): Duet's primitives are task lists (user's and agent's), first-class artifacts carried over from the Claude account, and Slack-style channels; "we're all trying to decide what the primitives are for agents" (3:07-4:38) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- ["I'm incapable of doing my job without AI"](sources/howiai-monday-amir-klein-second-brain.md): a Monday.com PM keeps one chat-app project per workstream as a "second brain", seeded with kickoff decks and PRDs and fed back its own outputs (0:14, 17:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [HTML is the new Markdown | Thariq Shihipar](sources/howiai-thariq-shihipar-html-specs.md): throwaway micro-UIs to edit parts of a plan; comments and annotations on HTML plans (18:16, 30:16; show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build your PM second brain](sources/lenny-newsletter-pm-second-brain-chatgpt.md): one ChatGPT/Claude Project or Gemini Gem per initiative, instructions plus files, as the PM's working container (Step 1, Appendix) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How OpenAI uses ChatGPT Sites (Kath Korevec)](sources/howiai-openai-korevec-chatgpt-sites.md): Sites hosts Codex-built web artifacts with storage, co-editors and deploy; used for DevDay keynote slides and throwaway personal tools (1:32, 9:46) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Cowork 101](sources/howiai-jj-englert-cowork-101.md): Cowork project = folder plus shared memory across chats, project instructions and a context panel (15:35-17:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build your own AI developer tools with Claude Code](sources/howiai-tenex-cj-hess-flowy.md): Flowy renders agent-written JSON as editable flowcharts and mockups; edits save back for the agent to read (10:44, 30:26) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): Claude.ai primitives (projects, Artifacts, styles, conversations) "should all just be exposed to an MCP" so the agent can write back to project knowledge (56:25-58:00) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Felix Rieseberg (Cowork)](sources/howiai-felix-rieseberg-cowork.md): "live artifacts" refresh from connectors and reuse connector OAuth; target pain is re-updating a deck weekly per audience (23:46-25:51, 33:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Teamwork Graph glossary (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-glossary.md): Object = single item of data (Jira work item, Confluence page, Google Drive file); each belongs to an object type that defines structure, properties and possible relationships. (user-story-mapping)
- [Teamwork Graph object types (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-object-types.md): Queryable API object types named on the page: Jira work items and Users. (user-story-mapping)
- [Getting started with the Atlassian Rovo MCP server](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-getting-started.md): Server URL https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp; v1 usage moves to v2 tools on 2027-03-01 (per the page). (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian Rovo MCP server: supported tools](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-supported-tools.md): Jira read: work items, projects, boards, sprints, filters, dashboards, comments, changelogs, worklogs, statuses, versions, components. Write: create/edit/transition work items, comments, links, versio (user-story-mapping)
- [What is a Jira space (formerly project)](sources/atlassian-jira-space-definition.md): 'A Jira space is a collection of related work items' for a product, team, service or project; items carry a space key prefix (e.g. GDT-1). (user-story-mapping)
- [What is a Confluence space](sources/atlassian-confluence-space-definition.md): A space is a container for creating, storing and collaborating on work tied to a team, shared project or initiative; examples: a knowledge base, or a space per launch or campaign. (user-story-mapping)
- [What is an idea (Jira Product Discovery docs)](sources/atlassian-jira-product-discovery-ideas.md): Idea = basic unit of work in a JPD space; fields such as goals, team, priority score, impact. (user-story-mapping)
- [Working with databases (Notion API docs)](sources/notion-api-databases-data-sources.md): Database = container holding data sources and views; does not carry the schema in current API versions. (user-story-mapping)
- [Notion MCP supported tools](sources/notion-mcp-supported-tools.md): Search (up to 50 results), connector search across Slack/Drive/GitHub, memory search over saved agent memories. (user-story-mapping)
- [Projects (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-projects.md): Project = 'a grouping of issues that have a clear outcome or planned completion date'. (user-story-mapping)
- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-initiatives.md): Initiatives are workspace-level containers for projects tied to a shared objective; IDs like I-<n>. (user-story-mapping)
- [Documents (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-documents.md): Documents attach to projects, initiatives, teams, issues or cycles; same editor as issues; realtime collaboration; version history including agent edits; templates at workspace/team level. (user-story-mapping)
- [Linear for Agents (developer docs)](sources/linear-developers-agents.md): Agents can be @mentioned, assigned issues, comment, and collaborate on projects and documents; installed agents are not billable users. (user-story-mapping)
- [Connect a coding agent to Spark via MCP (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-mcp-server-spark.md): Beta, included with Spark-enabled workspaces at no extra cost; admins enable it under Settings > MCP Server and choose roles. (user-story-mapping)
- [Add features to your hierarchy (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-product-hierarchy.md): Hierarchy: Product > Component > Feature > Subfeature. Features can be imported from spreadsheet, Jira or Zapier. (user-story-mapping)
- [Build on Dovetail (docs)](sources/dovetail-build-on-dovetail.md): Three options: MCP server, REST API (default 200 requests/min per workspace), CLI 'dt' for bulk import from Notion, Confluence, Google Drive and files (no sync after import). (user-story-mapping)
- [github/spec-kit (README)](sources/github-spec-kit-readme.md): Workflow: /speckit-constitution (once per project), then per feature /speckit-specify, -plan, -tasks, -implement, -converge. Runs as skills in the agent's chat. (user-story-mapping)
- [Spec-Driven Development (spec-kit spec-driven.md)](sources/github-spec-kit-spec-driven.md): Each feature lives in specs/<NNN-branch-name>/ with spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md, tasks.md ([P] marks parallel tasks). (user-story-mapping)
- [About Projects (GitHub Docs)](sources/github-docs-about-projects.md): Project = adaptable table, board and roadmap integrating issues and PRs, at user or organisation level; two-way sync with issues. (user-story-mapping)
- [What are projects? (Claude Help Center)](sources/anthropic-claude-projects-support.md): Project = self-contained workspace: knowledge base (documents, text, code), custom instructions, own chat history; memory mentioned only for a beta version. (user-story-mapping)
- [How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-memory-docs.md): Locations: managed policy (e.g. /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md), user, project (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md), local (CLAUDE.local.md). (user-story-mapping)
- [Organize work with projects (Claude Cowork docs)](sources/anthropic-cowork-projects-docs.md): Project holds: description (Dispatch reads it to choose a project for a task), folders (one or more local), instructions, links, linked Chat projects, memory. (user-story-mapping)
- [Glean Enterprise Graph (product page)](sources/glean-enterprise-graph-product-page.md): Enterprise Graph = relationships among people, projects, teams, products and processes, plus indexed content metadata; personal graphs infer the tasks and projects behind a person's activity. (user-story-mapping)
- [Scopes (Teamwork Graph API)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-scopes.md): the full API object-type list (one read scope each) covers Jira, Confluence (page, blogpost, comment, database, folder, space, whiteboard), Atlassian Home (goal, goal update, project, project update, tag, comment), Loom, Compass, Focus, Talent and 29 External* connector types; still no idea, PRD, spec, insight or decision type. (user-story-mapping)
- [Relationships (Teamwork Graph)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-relationships.md): four relationship kinds (canonical, activity, logical, inferred); logical ones like AtlassianUserCreatedDocuments unify Confluence pages and external documents under one edge. (user-story-mapping)
- [PRD template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-prd-template.md): Atlassian's PRD is a page template whose Options table holds user story, importance and 'Jira issues' as embedded links via /jira; no typed PRD-to-work-item relationship, no JPD or Home link. (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian MCP enhancements blog](sources/atlassian-blog-mcp-enhancements-jpd.md): July 2026 blog claims agents can find a JPD idea and link it to a delivery issue, but the supported-tools page names no JPD tool. (user-story-mapping)
- [Open-Inspect README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): the session is 'the core unit of work'; it stores messages, events, 'Artifacts | PRs created, screenshots captured', participants and sandbox state; no project object, grouping is by repository, environment and team; Linear holds the project mapping. (user-story-mapping)
- [Why We Built Our Own Background Agent (Ramp Builders)](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-our-own-background-agent.md): Inspect's unit is the session (own SQLite DB, shareable by URL) and its output is the PR with before/after screenshots; no spec, PRD, project or folder concept described. (user-story-mapping)

## product-coherence-over-automation: Product coherence can suffer from over-automation
Warnings that agent-driven shipping produces incoherent 'additive' products without a human holding the whole.
- [Office Hours: Building the case for leaders who ship with DoorDash](sources/claude-customers-doordash-office-hours.md): user-facing features need cross-functional buy-in; product/ship/design review now friction; Andy asks "do we even need to have product review?" (learnings answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): metric-chasing agents risk wins that harm the experience (Netflix autoplay), "AI optimized product slop" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [DESIGN.md Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-design-md-explained.md): "consistency gets easier but coherence gets harder"; finished-looking AI output suppresses critique. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How do AI coding agents work?](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-coding-agents-explained.md): once engineering capacity stops being the constraint, the risk is "feature slop" and feature discovery becomes the bottleneck. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How tech workers are feeling in 2026](sources/lenny-newsletter-tech-workers-2026-survey.md): "I can do more, faster, but not better"; respondents report focus and judgment suffering (Takeaway 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte](sources/lenny-podcast-roman-ugarte-grok-bot.md): built a separate app rather than a tab in Cursor to avoid "shipping your org chart"; "unshipped" thinking traces, memory views and debug tools before launch (9:20, 19:21) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino](sources/lenny-podcast-ambrosino-codex-product-work.md): product people play "zone defense" so a full team doesn't have to review code for product coherence; models "usually increase complexity" and should get better at deleting code (29:00, 40:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The AI paradox | Dan Shipper](sources/lenny-podcast-dan-shipper-ai-paradox.md): non-technical staff now open PRs, moving pressure to whoever merges: keep "a coherent whole" and decide "what do we delete?" (50:25-51:55) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers (Elizabeth Stone)](sources/lenny-podcast-elizabeth-stone-netflix-systems-thinkers.md): designers build templates and design systems so non-designers don't ship "Frankensteins"; deep design still gets time for top priorities (15:14, 20:51) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of Design (Ian Silber)](sources/lenny-podcast-ian-silber-openai-design.md): "Just do less"; build composable primitives so the product stays "one cohesive, simple thing" when engineers ship thousands of PRs (29:32-32:08) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): "We're sacrificing product consistency": overlapping features, confused new users, users on a treadmill; /powerup onboarding added against prior principle (25:42-27:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: When AI velocity outpaces your product strategy ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-velocity-strategy.md): legal-tech founder-PM slows to protect discovery and avoid a "Frankenstein product" (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The design process is dead: Jenny Wen](sources/lenny-podcast-jenny-wen-design-process-dead.md): when anyone can build anything, "you need to point them towards something"; Claude misses the design system (8:02, 23:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Becoming an AI PM: Aman Khan](sources/lenny-podcast-aman-khan-becoming-ai-pm.md): Betty Crocker "add an egg": leave users knobs rather than automate the job away (39:37) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why cultivating agency matters more than cultivating skills](sources/lenny-podcast-max-schoening-agency.md): the amount of software rose in 12 months but not its quality; merged roles risk losing specialists (6:42, 14:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [All of the Lenny & Friends Summit talks are now online!](sources/lenny-newsletter-summit-talks-online.md): "It's never been easier to build something nobody wants"; "The output is not the product" (Saarinen) (trend 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [No Figma. No Jira. No docs. How Gusto built a new product line with Claude Code](sources/howiai-gusto-eddie-kim-cofounder.md): "at any given time there was always something wrong with it in production" while the team chipped away behind a flag (21:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): downstream bottleneck: "how do we make sure that we're still building something coherent and packaging it up" (15:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Microsoft CPO (Aparna Chennapragada)](sources/lenny-podcast-aparna-chennapragada-microsoft.md): more ideas and prototypes need editorial taste "otherwise you just have Frankenstein product" (24:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: What to do when non-PMs start shipping](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-non-pms-shipping.md): even with unlimited engineering "you still need some discipline to create coherent products" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: when engineering outpaces product](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-engineering-outpaces-product.md): transcript-driven features judged half bloat; risk of "3 slightly different versions of the same feature because it was easier to build a new one" (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Someone Behind the Software (Karri Saarinen, Linear)](sources/linear-saarinen-someone-behind-the-software.md): changes are mostly additive and agent-made changes average the product (essay, read); losing learning from struggle is from his summit talk (PMS write-up, secondhand) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Marty Cagan interview (Modern CTO)](sources/moderncto-marty-cagan-2026.md): "product management theater" (title without control over what is built); one-click AI PRDs speed up a bad process; the avoid-thinking remark is from the PMS write-up [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Mike Krieger remarks at Lenny and Friends Summit (note.com write-up)](sources/note-krieger-pm-summit-remarks.md): Krieger told a PM "You were 100% right" after the PM covered enterprise customers, customer success and safety; Dill: LLMs give the most likely answer. (Single decision owner and editing-as-a-job are in the PMS write-up, not here) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Ten things I brought back from the Lenny & Friends Summit 2026](sources/productmanagementsociety-ten-things-lenny-summit.md): Saarinen, Krieger, Dill and Cagan remarks on judgment, single decision owner and avoiding thinking (secondhand). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## project-taxonomy: How 'project' is defined
Initiative/project/epic/space taxonomies across tools and conventions.
- [Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): a project = goal + repo or context + configured environment, connectors, plugins, instructions and model; work is "longer than one reply and has more than one part" (sections "Threads do the work", "Context builds over time"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Claude Projects and Skills to Monitor your Product's Health](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-projects-product-health.md): either one Project, or five function-owned sub-Projects plus a master; the master is fed by pasting each sub-Project's summary by hand (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Cowork 101](sources/howiai-jj-englert-cowork-101.md): "a project is a folder on your computer"; "a skill is literally like a file" (6:20, 9:23) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-initiatives-docs.md): Initiatives are curated groups of projects tied to a company objective; sub-initiatives allowed; projects can be collected by filters; initiative health on track/at risk/off track from updates; documents attach via a Resources pro (user-story-mapping)
- [Create a space (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-create-a-space.md): a space is 'a container ... for work related to a shared project or initiative' with a purpose of Collaboration, Knowledge base or Custom, one owner and a permissions scheme; it is a third 'project'-like container beside Jira spaces and Atlassian Home projects. (user-story-mapping)

## prototyping-agents-limits: Prototyping agents and their limits
Prompt-to-prototype tools let PMs build quickly but break down as complexity grows and need engineering handoff.
- [Reflexive AI usage is now a baseline expectation at Shopify](sources/x-tobi-reflexive-ai-usage-memo.md): "AI must be part of your GSD Prototype phase"; the prototype phase "should be dominated by AI exploration" (Apr 2025) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor prototype animation shipped 'nearly one-for-one'; prototypes became inputs to reviews; next step is live data and prototype-scoped databases (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Protodash (How I AI, Owen Williams)](sources/howiai-stripe-protodash-owen-williams.md): gets '90% of the way most of the time ... it will make slop'; taste and craft stay with designers (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Office Hours: Asynchronous coding and the end of the IDE with Spotify](sources/claude-customers-spotify-office-hours.md): prototypes run in real apps with real users and data within an hour or two, but "not every idea ships in an hour"; many need lots of exploration (deployments segment; closing segment). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): not for production software (use Claude Code), no image model so poor for logos; left undirected Claude falls back to recognisable house aesthetics ("What Claude Design is not meant to do", "Tell Claude what it should look like"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The founder's playbook: Building an AI-native startup](sources/claude-founders-playbook.md): prototype existence is not evidence; zero-cost building drives scope creep and "insecure by inexperience" code (Idea and MVP stage challenges). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build AI Assistant Prototypes](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-assistant-prototypes.md): five vibe-coded clones built from chatbot ideas, then PRD, then a Lovable prompt, with no eval or user test; the author admits the inputs were illustrative (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to "vibe code"](sources/departmentofproduct-vibe-coding.md): Replit couldn't fix a padding bug even from a screenshot; chat-only Lovable leaves non-coders stuck: "works well - until it doesn't" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): Stitch output is "by no means production-ready"; for discussion only; beta, free with limits (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Persona Feature Tester with Claude Code and ElevenLabs](sources/departmentofproduct-persona-feature-tester.md): Claude Design's first pass looked like a brochure until the author redirected it (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Design is here](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-design.md): onboarding, landing page and 3D component were strong from short prompts. The stakeholder deck was "passable" but full of AI clichés, and PPT export failed (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): Alloy builds features on a screenshot of the live product and pulls specs from Jira, Linear or Notion (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Community Wisdom: Syncing Claude Code and Claude Design ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-claude-design-handoff.md): Claude Design export README told Claude Code to "interpret" designs; invisible states (empty, loading, error) were lost in handoff; several members use Claude Design only as a directional scratchpad (Thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build prototypes that actually look like your product | Colin Matthews](sources/howiai-colin-matthews-brand-prototypes.md): AI prototypes don't look like your product by default; fix with a component library generated from screenshots or extracted from a live site (show notes) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [A guide to AI prototyping for product managers](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-prototyping-guide-pms.md): 2025 limits: prompt-only editing, browser-run servers without auth or persistence, tools rewriting whole sections when instructions are vague; tactics: plan first, small batches, be specific (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Yelp AI PM works backward from golden conversations (Priya Badger)](sources/howiai-yelp-priya-badger-golden-conversations.md): live-model Artifact prototypes reveal that replies fine in a doc feel long in a chat bubble; the Magic Patterns demo failed on a React version error (19:19, 30:42) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Turn meeting notes into prototypes (Acolyte Health)](sources/howiai-acolyte-health-meeting-notes-prototypes.md): "at least three demos that did not work" per one shown; iterating inside Lovable/v0 wasted time (45:51) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: AM calls, MCP server](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-am-calls-mcp-server.md): fast AI prototyping tempts teams to jump to solutions before understanding the problem (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of Design (Ian Silber)](sources/lenny-podcast-ian-silber-openai-design.md): design isn't "binary" like a coding task; agents compress the try-fail-feedback loop but don't remove it (4:56) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [A designer's guide to AI (Joel Unger, Atlassian)](sources/howiai-atlassian-joel-unger-cursor-design.md): Figma's limits for interactive panels pushed prototyping into Cursor (show notes, 4:24-5:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Grok Bot designers use AI agents ...](sources/howiai-grok-bot-designers-agents.md): "trash can method": prototypes built assuming they will be thrown away; both variants of one idea rejected (27:30-28:49) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Everyone's an engineer now | Guillermo Rauch](sources/lenny-podcast-guillermo-rauch-v0.md): weak on massive codebases; scope to a component; escape hatches (edit code, hand to another model after ~120 iterations) (47:45, 1:15:39) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: ... AI agents and data integrity ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-agents-data-integrity.md): vibe-coded app with weak retention; "build is the easiest part of starting a business" (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The design process is dead: Jenny Wen](sources/lenny-podcast-jenny-wen-design-process-dead.md): coding tools are "super linear" and bias to one direction; Figma still better for exploring 8-10 options (20:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Guillermo Rauch: v0 Git workflow](sources/howiai-guillermo-rauch-v0-git-workflow.md): zero to one is easy, iterating at scale and deploying safely is hard; prototypes without a PR path were "La La Land" (4:51, 18:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Notion's design team uses Claude Code to prototype](sources/howiai-notion-brian-lovin-prototype-playground.md): Figma MCP alone ~60%; with a slash command and browser verification loop ~80% right 80% of the time; agent hallucinated passing CI (24:42, 40:29) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to get your entire team prototyping with AI](sources/lenny-newsletter-colin-matthews-team-prototyping.md): AI prototype code "mostly useless to your engineering team" unless built on real components; delivery still 2-6 weeks (Step 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The complete beginner's guide to coding with AI](sources/howiai-claire-vo-beginner-prd-to-code.md): v0 overbuilt from a deliberately simple PRD ("scope creep" built into agentic builders) and was abandoned for Cursor (12:25-15:29) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Identify your bullseye customer in one day](sources/lenny-podcast-michael-margolis-bullseye.md): GV researcher keeps discovery prototypes flat; "Build only as much as you actually need to answer the question" (59:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why cultivating agency matters more than cultivating skills](sources/lenny-podcast-max-schoening-agency.md): the first 10% is free but the last 10% is 90% of the work; software prototypes hide their "layer lines" (14:22, 29:19) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to turn your AI into a world-class designer](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-world-class-designer.md): models default to predictable, committee-like design and "love to add more, but rarely take away"; seed strings and critics push past it (Techniques 1, 6) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How top PMs increase their leverage with AI](sources/lenny-newsletter-pm-leverage-ladders.md): web prototyping tools are "removed from reality" without real components and data models (product ladder) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The secret to better AI prototypes (Ravi Mehta)](sources/howiai-ravi-mehta-data-driven-prototyping.md): prompt-only prototypes hallucinated image URLs and showed a French Polynesia hotel for Paris; real data needed for credible feedback (10:13-11:08, 23:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From Figma to Claude Code and back](sources/howiai-figma-design-code-loop.md): code tools still lack "precision editing"; direct manipulation remains the gold standard (13:05) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What Claude Design is actually good for](sources/howiai-claude-design-hands-on.md): good for landing pages and decks, weak at app UX components; 5-10 minutes per generation; she hit the plan limit and paid $200 more; Figma wins on loop speed (10:20-15:21) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The rise of the professional vibe coder (Lazar Jovanovic)](sources/lenny-podcast-lazar-jovanovic-vibe-coder.md): 4-5 parallel prototypes of rising specificity to find clarity; regulated firms (healthcare, finance) prototype but can't push to production (27:21, 51:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How AI is changing product operating models](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-operating-models.md): vibe deployments to production handed back to developers because someone must own maintenance (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: What to do when non-PMs start shipping](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-non-pms-shipping.md): "treat these prototypes like PRDs"; "clickable PRDs really, too immature to take seriously" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Cursor for PM work](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-cursor-for-pm-work.md): "the best use case for PMs today is in prototyping" on a branch deployed to test, then handed to engineering to merge or reimplement (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to ship like a startup (Figma Slides)](sources/lenny-newsletter-figma-slides-ship-like-startup.md): eight people built a working product prototype in a three-day hackathon; "Throwaway code is a superpower" (lessons 2, 6) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Marily Nika: new PM toolkit](sources/howiai-marily-nika-pm-toolkit.md): v0 prototype from a full PRD added unrequested features; "at least five to ten follow-ups"; used mainly for influence in product review (17:00, 21:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Pivoting to AI PM, how AI changed our product development cycles](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-product-dev-cycles.md): prototyping-tool vendor: no tool makes production-ready code outside small/new projects; PMs rarely hand off generated code (thread 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Prototyping vs. writing PRDs](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-prototyping-vs-prds.md): choose the prototype by the risk to reduce; it can be a one-pager, role-play or concierge test (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Choosing your AI prototyping stack (Anna Arteeva)](sources/annaarteeva-choosing-ai-prototyping-stack.md): Practitioner migration Bolt -> v0 -> Lovable, prefers Lovable (case 17) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Figma Make vs Lovable (Playcode)](sources/playcode-figma-make-vs-lovable.md): Competitor (Playcode) comparison, reportedly without hands-on testing; original page now redirects, unverified (case 16) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI prototyping with Lovable (Product Talk)](sources/producttalk-ai-prototyping-lovable.md): Visual/brand inconsistency, breakage with complexity, Supabase login ~0.5s to 25s (TimelyCare), tool claiming unmade fixes, prototype looking too real; about half (5 of 11) moved design work to Figma/Stitch/a design system; Cursor only suggested (case 18) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Figma Make review (Salesdorado)](sources/salesdorado-figma-make-review.md): Edge is reading existing Figma files; prototype-only, figma.site hosting, credit quotas strictly enforced per licence since 18 March 2026; no documented test (case 16) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Lovable raises $330M at $6.6B valuation (tech.eu)](sources/techeu-lovable-330m-raise.md): Unnamed ride-sharing and delivery platform: design concept testing "six weeks to five days" (vendor-supplied speed claim, not a limit) (case 18) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Vercel case studies (Avalara)](sources/vercel-case-studies-avalara.md): Avalara "two patent-pending products created in roughly 60 days" (vendor-claim) (case 17) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Prototypes vs Products](sources/svpg-prototypes-vs-products.md): prototypes show nothing about reliability, scale, security, compliance or full business logic; vendor claims are "buyer beware" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Agentic Software Development Takes The Lead (Forrester)](sources/forrester-agentic-software-development-sdlc-agents.md): PM prototypes are handed "to the rest of the team to productize" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [To Vibe Code, or Not to Vibe Code?](sources/ideas-fin-to-vibe-code-or-not.md): Fin designer: "Vibe coding doesn't replace structured design work—it precedes it"; five guardrails; replace a prototype treated as a commitment with "something explicitly finalized" (2026-01-23) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## public-by-default-agent-work: Public-by-default agent work and its costs
Agent sessions that are visible to the whole organisation by default (no DMs, no private mode), so others learn by watching and the transcripts can be mined; and the costs of that default: questions not asked, sensitive data in open threads, channel membership as access control, regulated walls. Matters for the trust-privacy-defaults and agent-interface choices.
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): River "does not respond to direct messages"; "Asking for help feels different when the whole company can see the question" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): "Every conversation with River becomes a public Slack transcript, open by default to other Shopify employees" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River's reaction to the Shop floor post](sources/x-tobi-river-reaction-to-shop-floor-post.md): "Some questions that would have been asked in a DM just don't get asked"; also an "honesty pressure" on agent and user (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): River refuses private channels too: "you can't go into a private channel and say, 'Hey, River, help me build'" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Quick](sources/shopify-engineering-quick.md): the same default for artifacts: all sites open to all employees, no owners (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's River shows why agent context costs more (Magica)](sources/magica-shopify-river-agent-context-cost.md): Slack's CPO: a boundary for "genuinely sensitive work"; "psychological safety should determine where openness stops" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify Just Showed the Agent Stack](sources/adaptordie-shopify-river-agent-stack.md): "A pricing conversation may need a tighter audience" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Hacker News: River submissions and comments](sources/hn-shopify-river-discussion.md): one-line anecdote: the way people speak to agents wouldn't be "kosher in a company slack" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [The Transparency Paradox (Bernstein)](sources/asq-bernstein-transparency-paradox.md): broad visibility can breed hiding; privacy zones raised output 10–15% (independent; factory setting) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Create information barriers in Slack](sources/slack-information-barriers-docs.md): chat-tool walls don't stop interaction in shared channels, so a channel-native agent inherits that gap (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tenable on Claude Tag](sources/tenable-claude-tag-slack-access-model.md): in channel agents, public-channel join policy effectively governs access to the agent's credentials; new members see scrollback (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Agents you can coach: how Asana builds human-agent teams with Claude](sources/claude-asana-agents-you-can-coach.md): Bose argues one-on-one agent use hides the prompt and back-and-forth from reviewers, so they cannot align on or revise the instructions. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Lessons from Anthropic on building effective human-agent teams](sources/claude-building-effective-human-agent-teams.md): Lesson 1: "if it's not written down and accessible, it doesn't exist" for agents; channels default public within the org; a handful of workspace-level boundaries instead of per-item sharing; private DMs and personal-connector... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the Claude Code team does code review](sources/claude-dev-claude-code-team-code-review.md): review's second job, building shared understanding, is now covered by Claude-written explainers on demand and by "our culture of defaulting to working on open Slack channels" (§Sharing context across the team). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Turning conversation into knowledge: how Slack builds human-agent teams](sources/claude-slack-human-agent-teams.md): "Agents can only learn from what they can see"; default channels to public and go private on purpose; "A private channel is a blind spot for every agent that reports on it" (sections "Treat your conversation history", "Default... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Tag now supports personal connectors in channels](sources/claude-tag-personal-connectors.md): "Anything Claude posts is visible to everyone in the channel"; the requester chooses review mode (see the reply before it posts) or auto mode (posts unless Claude judges content sensitive) (intro, §Using personal connectors). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Self-service data analytics in Slack: how Anthropic deploys Claude Tag for ad-hoc questions](sources/claude-tag-self-service-analytics.md): keep the agent in shared channels and work in threads, not DMs, so threads are a reviewable record (section "Claude Tag threads become the new meeting"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Devin replaces your junior engineers | Scott Wu](sources/howiai-scott-wu-devin-junior-engineer.md): host: "hiding your AI use is kind of the worst thing you can do"; Wu: public use transfers knowledge to the agent and educates the humans (24:01-24:56) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Warp ships 2,000 PRs a month with AI factories (How I AI)](sources/howiai-warp-zach-lloyd-software-factory.md): factory work starts in public Slack threads others can join; Lloyd credits this with spreading power-user habits across a power-law team (41:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## remote-agent-invocation: Remote agent invocation
Starting and steering agents that run elsewhere: cloud tasks, scheduled or API/webhook-triggered runs, Slack mentions.
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): one stack, three modes: interactive (River), automation (PR review, woken by external systems), job (CI/batch, log optional) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): River opens one Slack thread per finding from a ledger; 4 threads / 35 findings in a minute, each progressing independently (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): River is pull-only: "you can talk to it, but it doesn't talk to you" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Stripe's AI minions ship 1,300 PRs weekly from a Slack emoji (How I AI)](sources/howiai-stripe-minions-kaliski.md): minions start from a Slack emoji reaction (message = prompt, emoji picks the repo), also from Docs and tickets, and from a phone (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor's toolset is exposed on Stripe's internal MCP so Kai and devbox coding agents can create, read, update and publish prototypes; its renderer is a separate service (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): an API trigger gives a task a /fire HTTP endpoint with a per-task bearer token that returns a session URL; fire text is wrapped as untrusted data (Add an API trigger) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex cloud and the Slack integration (OpenAI docs)](sources/openai-codex-cloud-slack.md): Codex cloud tasks run in published environments, in parallel, 'while your computer is asleep'; internet access and secrets configured per environment (cloud docs, learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud.md) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Oz Cloud Agents & Orchestration (Warp docs)](sources/warp-oz-cloud-agents.md): triggers from Slack, Linear, schedules, CLI, API/SDK; self-host via managed Docker worker or unmanaged `oz agent run` in CI/Kubernetes (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification](sources/a2a-project-specification-v1.md): v1.0.0; Agent Card discovery, task lifecycle incl. INPUT_REQUIRED/AUTH_REQUIRED, streaming and push webhooks; identity/credential issuance left to implementers (first-party spec). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [LF A2A one-year release](sources/linuxfoundation-a2a-one-year-press-release.md): 150+ supporting orgs, v1.0, Azure Foundry/Copilot Studio and Bedrock AgentCore integrations; no named end-user production deployment (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [A2A adoption, hype and reality](sources/glukhov-a2a-adoption-hype-reality.md): independent: no named production deployments; 'supported by' is not 'used in production'; proposes four adoption tiers. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ask HN: Is anyone using A2A?](sources/hn-ask-is-anyone-using-a2a.md): anecdote: some enterprise/Google-ecosystem use, many reports of returning to MCP or plain HTTP; 'no A2A in any final product' at one large company. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Copilot Studio A2A](sources/microsoft-copilot-studio-a2a.md): a shipping enterprise orchestrator consumes external A2A agents with API key/OAuth; customer responsible for permissions and oversight (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AgentCore Runtime A2A](sources/aws-bedrock-agentcore-runtime-a2a.md): managed hosting of A2A servers with SigV4/JWT auth (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [MCP Tasks extension](sources/mcp-ext-tasks-long-running-operations.md): durable task handle, polling, input_required; the MCP-native answer to host timeouts for agent-like tools (first-party spec). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

## risk-review-as-classification: Risk review as a specification and classification problem
Risk advisory works as classification against a known taxonomy, with a curation path for novel risks. That makes a risk agent tractable to build and straightforward to evaluate with SME labels.
- [How Anthropic employees use Claude Tag](sources/claude-how-anthropic-uses-claude-tag.md): claims sorted into "verified against public documentation" vs "its own framing" flagged for product-lead sign-off (section "Turning a Slack thread"); legal channel flags issues and tags counsel only for what needs sign-off... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic secures its AI-native software development lifecycle](sources/claude-securing-ai-native-sdlc-at-anthropic.md): an Opus-powered project security review (PSR) app reads a design doc against MITRE ATT&CK plus an internal knowledge index; once trusted, teams "approve their own project, if Claude deemed the launch low enough risk" (§Plan). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Decision Models Explained - The New AI Building Block for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-decision-models.md): the same "is this safe to run?" check before every agent action, where speed matters; Vercel's CEO is relayed as claiming 18x faster safety checks (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## risk-sloped-review: Human review sloped to risk
How much human review agent output gets depends on how risky it is. Where that line sits is a key harness and governance design choice, especially in regulated organisations.

- [Why your AI product needs a different development lifecycle (CC/CD)](sources/lenny-newsletter-cc-cd-ai-lifecycle.md): start with "simple decisions that are easy to verify and easy for humans to override"; three-rung ladders for support, marketing and coding (CD 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Warp ships 2,000 PRs a month with AI factories (How I AI)](sources/howiai-warp-zach-lloyd-software-factory.md): Vo risk-scores every PR and auto-stamps low-risk ones; Lloyd: "code review becomes an exercise in risk management" (16:18-17:01) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [AI is approving our pull requests (Intercom)](sources/intercom-ai-approving-pull-requests.md): sub-agents check problem description, diff-vs-intent, safety, logic and anti-patterns; ~19% of PRs auto-approved; large or broad PRs refused and split (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [2× – nine months later: We did it](sources/ideas-fin-2x-nine-months-later.md): auto-approval began with feature-flag cleanups and small bug fixes; 86% of auto-approved PRs are 20 lines or fewer (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Webinar Q&A: How Fin 3x'd R&D output in 16 months](sources/ideas-fin-webinar-qa-3x-rd-output.md): "Shrek" reviewer triggered by GitHub webhooks in short-lived AWS containers (Claude and Codex); per-repo safety criteria; repo owners add review requirements (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): Ramp auto-approves low-complexity PRs; Stripe requires human review on every change (§Vision, step 7) (research-product-agent-and-harness)

## scoped-governance-containers: Governance scoped to a project or workspace
Policy (default model, allowed tools, human-in-the-loop rules, data back end, even which harness) set once by a project owner and applied to everyone working in that project, rather than per user or org-wide. Matters for governance and trust defaults.
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): "projects are primarily a governance mechanism"; owners set default model, tool policies, HITL; HR has a separately backed secure project; projects of 5 to 500 people (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): domain-owned custom Kai agents load a team's skills and data sources by default (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Agent identity: a new access model for autonomous, team-wide AI](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): distinct identity per private channel, shared workspace identity for public channels; memory and access stay inside boundaries (section "How identity boundaries work"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Notion ships and scales agents with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-notion-managed-agents.md): every agent starts private and must be shared explicitly, with chat-only, trigger and edit permission levels; the review agent is managed by a few people, the investigator by many (same answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How healthcare organizations use Claude Tag](sources/claude-tag-healthcare-human-agent-teams.md): Tag can be off by default, enabled only in approved channels, DMs disabled, connectors scoped per channel; "access bundles" give a channel its codebase and tracker while EHR and clinical systems stay unreachable (intro bullets). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Community Wisdom: Using AI to accelerate a team's velocity](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-team-velocity.md): one Claude Project per larger feature initiative, shared with CS, PMM and marketing for handoffs (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What a harness is and how to build one with Claude Agent SDK](sources/howiai-claire-vo-agent-sdk-harness.md): "How to encode specific permissions into a harness" (show notes; details not available) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: ... sharing Claude Code context across a team](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-claude-context-sharing.md): Obsidian dropped for "too little governance around what agents can do to the data (without a human in the loop)" (thread 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Quests, token leaderboards, and a skills marketplace (How I AI)](sources/howiai-sendbird-john-kim-adoption-playbook.md): pre-vetted app template with auth and environments, "fully compliant", plus a weekly CTO/engineering/Infosec task force; quests show a risk rating (9:51-14:56) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## shared-persistent-sessions: Shared, persistent, multi-user agent sessions
Agent sessions that outlive one person's laptop: shared with teammates, running in a deployed runtime, resumable or event-driven. Raises identity (who is the agent acting as), permission-leakage, durability and cost questions that local sessions avoid.
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): async-by-default, always-open sessions with HITL approvals, steering and multiplayer; session state in Postgres decoupled from sandboxes; cloud workers so 'laptop goes to sleep' no longer matters (first-party) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Why We Built Our Own Background Agent](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-background-agent.md): every Inspect session is multiplayer, prompts attributed per person, state synced across Slack, web, extension, PR and hosted VS Code (first-party) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): Aquifer session = append-only Postgres event log; harness and sandbox disposable; idle "session cells" rehydrate on any host; "Cells die, sandboxes die, machines die. The conversation doesn't." (Part III) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River floods Shopify chart](sources/x-tobi-river-floods-shopify-chart.md): "wrote in the same thread" links 61,680 (Mar) → 171,853 (Sep 2026), the only published multiplayer metric (self-reported) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment](sources/shopify-engineering-remote-dev.md): each River session claims a warm Mac plus Android VM, destroyed after use; tasks start from Slack or run overnight; Live Preview links shareable (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify: Building River (ZenML)](sources/zenml-llmops-shopify-river-durable-infrastructure.md): Postgres event-log session, harness outside the sandbox, idle "session cells" restart anywhere (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Case Study: Shopify River (Wallfacer)](sources/wallfacer-case-study-shopify-river.md): "the resume mechanism and the audit record are the same artifact" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Hacker News: River submissions and comments](sources/hn-shopify-river-discussion.md): practitioners compare River to Managed Agents and say "we built something similar" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): Kai sessions are cloud-hosted and long (one hit 932 turns) but single-user; context is 'locked in'; sharing and multi-person artifacts are on the roadmap (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's AI minions ship 1,300 PRs weekly from a Slack emoji (How I AI)](sources/howiai-stripe-minions-kaliski.md): minions run in a public Slack 'robots' channel watched by 76 people: open-by-default observation and 'pair prompting' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor shares artifacts, not sessions: one published snapshot per URL, anchored comments that re-resolve after agent rewrites, remix into a copy (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Thoughts On A Month With Devin](sources/answerai-month-with-devin.md): the Slack-based chat and visible environment setup were polished; the unreliability was in the agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): cloud sessions keep running after the laptop closes and can be steered from mobile; sharing is Private or Team visibility, and 'recipients see the latest state when they open the link, but their view doesn't update in real time' (Share sessions) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): scheduled tasks 'belong to your individual claude.ai account. They are not shared with teammates'; everything they do through GitHub/connectors 'appears as you' (Create a scheduled task) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Tag: agent identity (concepts)](sources/anthropic-claude-tag-agent-identity.md): channel sessions use connectors, repos and plugins an admin applied to the channel/workspace/org, and 'everyone in the channel gets the same capability, regardless of who asks' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): first design ran session, harness and sandbox in one container, making it a 'pet'; decoupling into session (durable log), harness (loop) and sandbox (hands) lets any piece fail or be replaced (Decoupling) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Self-hosted environments (Claude Code cloud sessions on your infrastructure)](sources/anthropic-self-hosted-environments.md): control plane (queue, session stream, claude.ai UI) stays Anthropic-hosted; runners execute sessions; 'Anthropic stores the session transcript so you can resume the session from another supported surface' (What stays on your infrastructure) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Self-hosted environments (Claude Code cloud sessions on your infrastructure)](sources/anthropic-self-hosted-environments.md): a runner locks to one owner (a user account or a Claude Tag agent) at a time so checked-out code never mixes between owners; minimum fleet size equals active owners (Runner lifecycle) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Long-running agents (Cloudflare Agents SDK docs)](sources/cloudflare-agents-long-running-agents.md): agents are 'durable identities, not always-on processes': wake on HTTP, WebSocket, RPC, alarm or inbound email, hibernate after about 2 minutes idle; eviction can occur at any point (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloud-origin agents have no 'Move to Machine' option (Cursor forum)](sources/cursor-forum-cloud-to-local-handoff.md): related thread reports local to cloud handoff failing for GitLab repos with 'Background composer not found' (search snippet only) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cursor Cloud Agent sessions are shared across users - act on behalf (forum bug report)](sources/cursor-forum-team-followups-act-on-behalf.md): the reporter claims a session runs with the initiating user's OAuth identity for Jira, GitHub and Slack while its prompt surface is not bound to that user; follow-ups via Slack thread or the shared web URL run as the initiator (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The $47K agent loop: why logging, monitoring and max_tokens all failed to stop it](sources/devto-47k-agent-loop.md): argues enforcement should be deterministic, pre-call and per-run (cost, iterations, wall clock) with an external kill switch, separate from the agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent-risks.md): identity: commits are authored by Copilot with the requesting developer as co-author, signed ('Verified'), each linked to its session log; logs and audit events available to admins (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent-risks.md): only users with write access can trigger the agent and comments from others never reach it; pushes confined to one branch (the PR branch or a new copilot/ branch) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Open-Inspect (ColeMurray/background-agents) README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): a Durable Object per session holds SQLite, a WebSocket hub and event stream; clients are web, Slack, GitHub, Linear, webhooks; presence indicators and prompts attributed to authors in git commits (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Open-Inspect (ColeMurray/background-agents) README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): access model has Workspace/Team/Private visibility separate from ownership, break-glass audited read for workspace owners, but 'Team-visibility read restrictions only apply when TEAMS_ENFORCEMENT=on. The default is shadow' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Durable Execution for AI Agents: LangGraph, DBOS, Inngest and Temporal Compared](sources/hackernoon-durable-execution-compared.md): 'None of the four saves a model call made outside a step boundary' so retries pay again; durability does not guarantee idempotency (a step that charged a card and timed out still needs handling) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [LangGraph persistence (checkpointers, threads, stores)](sources/langchain-langgraph-persistence.md): InMemory saver is for dev only; production uses Postgres/Sqlite savers; Agent Server handles persistence automatically; checkpoints accumulate over long conversations and need pruning (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How Ramp built a full-context background coding agent on Modal](sources/modal-ramp-inspect-background-agent.md): each session gets its own Modal sandbox; Modal Dicts hold session locks, Modal Queues route prompts from any client into the right session so several clients feed one session without conflict (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex cloud and the Slack integration (OpenAI docs)](sources/openai-codex-cloud-slack.md): repository work 'runs as a separate task under the requester's account'; a different account may start a new task instead of continuing; sharing an environment does not grant repo access or share credential values (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex cloud and the Slack integration (OpenAI docs)](sources/openai-codex-cloud-slack.md): approval requests go to the requester as a private card, but the response 'can be read by people with access to that channel'; following the channel reply does not give access to the task (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot, end-to-end coding agents - Part 2](sources/stripe-minions-part-2.md): blast radius bounded by environment not by prompts: devboxes (EC2, pre-warmed, ~10 s) run in QA with no real user data, production services or arbitrary egress; engineers run about half a dozen at once (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Claude Tag Slack access model (Tenable Research)](sources/tenable-claude-tag-slack-access-model.md): service-identity pattern means 'anyone in a channel with the bundle can direct Claude within its scope'; public-channel join policy effectively governs access to bundle credentials; new members also see prior scrollback (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

## single-agent-many-skills: One agent with many skills, not many agents
Consolidate to one agent and one conversational surface, extended by skills and tools.
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): "single agent with a thousand skills"; OmniChat (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass. Make your entire company smarter](sources/ramp-introducing-glass.md): "one single agent" with pre-built connectivity (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): new agents are "profiles" (prompt, skills, extensions, sandbox policy, model defaults) on one substrate: "a new bundle, not ... a new platform" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify Just Showed the Agent Stack](sources/adaptordie-shopify-river-agent-stack.md): "Pi is the engine room. River is the shop floor interface" (commentator's inference) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): one Kai harness over 1,000+ skills and tools; a no-code builder that produced 4,000+ micro-agents was replaced because of duplicated, uneven, hard-to-maintain agents (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How Stripe Built Kai on Deep Agents (LangChain)](sources/langchain-how-stripe-built-kai-deep-agents.md): skills gate tools via allowedTools (two-pass); foundational skills pinned; frontier-model quality degrades past ~150 skills with the system prompt (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): ~2,000 skills: ~50 used heavily daily, 100-150 by sub-orgs, many by 2-3 people; telemetry pipeline decides what to promote or move out of the general context (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot, end-to-end coding agents - Part 2](sources/stripe-minions-part-2.md): 'Toolshed' internal MCP server with nearly 500 tools but a small curated subset per agent; blueprints mix deterministic nodes with agent nodes (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Don't Build Multi-Agents](sources/cognition-dont-build-multi-agents.md): first-party: parallel sub-agents make conflicting implicit decisions; share full traces, prefer a single-threaded agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Skills specification](sources/agentskills-specification.md): progressive disclosure keeps many skills cheap. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Equipping agents with Agent Skills](sources/anthropic-engineering-equipping-agents-agent-skills.md): general agent plus loadable expertise. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [SkillsBench](sources/arxiv-skillsbench.md): 2-3 skills best; 4+ gives smaller gains (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AGENTS.md outperforms skills](sources/vercel-agents-md-outperforms-skills.md): counter-evidence: on-demand skills unreliable for always-needed reference knowledge (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Extend Claude with skills](sources/anthropic-claude-code-skills-docs.md): context: fork delegates to subagents. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Custom subagents in Claude Code](sources/anthropic-claude-code-subagents-docs.md): skills preloaded into subagents (up to 32). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex vs Claude Code multi-agent](sources/danielvaughan-codex-vs-claude-code-multi-agent.md): subagent topologies differ (anecdote). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Best practices for Claude Code](sources/anthropic-claude-code-best-practices.md): first-party: one general harness spans exploration (vague prompts) to unattended runs (claude -p, hooks, skills); skills for repeatable workflows (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Equipping agents with Agent Skills](sources/anthropic-engineering-equipping-agents-agent-skills.md): first-party: skills proposed instead of fragmented custom agents per use case (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How we built our multi-agent research system](sources/anthropic-multi-agent-research-system.md): first-party: multi-agent fits breadth-first research, not shared-context coding; about 15x tokens (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Choose a design pattern for your agentic AI system](sources/google-cloud-choose-design-pattern-agentic-ai.md): vendor: start with a single agent; go multi-agent when tool count or distinct responsibilities cause failures (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cowork and plugins for teams across the enterprise](sources/claude-cowork-plugins-enterprise.md): "Plugins turn Claude into specialized agents for every role and department": one agent specialised per role by plugin, not separate agents (intro). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How a $2 billion venture fund made Claude Cowork its shared firm infrastructure](sources/claude-customers-airtree-cowork.md): board prep, company-insights and board-summary skills chain in one tool; a meeting-record step "acts like an analyst agent" updating the prep doc (Q&A, "Walk us through a workflow"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Vercel built an ecosystem on the open skills standard](sources/claude-customers-vercel-skills-ecosystem.md): d0, the internal data-science agent, runs on ~100 skills; descriptive names ("aggregating product metrics month over month") let Opus 4.8 route intent; no collisions yet, though Qu expects them (d0 answers). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop](sources/claude-fold-subagents-into-main-loop.md): "a single agent with skills frequently outperformed both the one-prompt-for-everything design and the subagent design on quality, and often at a lower cost and latency per task" (intro). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A complete guide to building skills for Claude](sources/claude-guide-building-skills.md): composability principle (Claude loads multiple skills at once; a skill must not assume it is alone) and the warning to review if more than 20-50 skills are enabled at once, with "skill packs" suggested (Fundamentals; Patterns... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Deploying Claude across your organization: How Anthropic uses Cowork](sources/claude-guide-deploying-cowork-across-org.md): PMs stack productivity, data, sales and product plugins in one session rather than using one PM plugin (ch. 6, "Product management"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agent harness design: 3 patterns for harnessing Claude's intelligence](sources/claude-harness-design-three-patterns.md): skills as progressively disclosed context (frontmatter preloaded, body read on demand) rather than hand-crafted task prompts; subagents used when Claude decides to fork a fresh context (Pattern 2, "Let Claude manage its own... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [New in Claude Managed Agents: dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration](sources/claude-managed-agents-dreaming-outcomes.md): counterpoint: multiagent orchestration delegates to specialists with their own model, prompt and tools when there is "too much work for a single agent to do well" (§Multiagent orchestration). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Skills explained: How Skills compares to prompts, Projects, MCP, and subagents](sources/claude-skills-explained.md): "Skills vs. subagents": put shared expertise in a skill any agent can load rather than baking it into individual subagents; subagents can use skills. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Why Semantic Data Layers matter](sources/departmentofproduct-semantic-data-layers.md): Anthropic pairs a thin "router" knowledge skill (semantic layer first, then domain files) with an analyst-workflow skill that ends in adversarial review. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Multi Agent Architecture explained](sources/departmentofproduct-multi-agent-architecture.md): treats a single agent as fit only for simple cases, the opposite of Cognition's later view (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical Agent Skills for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-practical-agent-skills.md): gstack and Every's compound-engineering are skill families that act "like a small virtual team" in one harness. Each stage writes a file the next stage reads (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Claude Cowork as a Competitive Intelligence System](sources/departmentofproduct-cowork-competitive-intelligence.md): one Cowork session chains browser research, then xlsx/pptx/docx skills, then the PM plugin's /stakeholder-update for Slack (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Spec-driven development at Notion | Ryan Nystrom](sources/howiai-notion-ryan-nystrom-spec-driven.md): Notion rebuilt its agent harness around skills and progressive disclosure after system-prompt bloat (32:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte](sources/lenny-podcast-roman-ugarte-grok-bot.md): users should never need to know what a skill is; skills created in the background (37:52) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of ChatGPT ... | Tibo Sottiaux](sources/lenny-podcast-sottiaux-chatgpt-dots.md): "loops, graphs" are a passing phase; one smart agent that learns goals and preferences; his own agent teams expand at the frontier then shrink when a bigger model "can just do all of it" (2:31, 3:19) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Claude Code (Boris Cherny)](sources/lenny-podcast-boris-cherny-after-coding.md): "the same Claude agent running everywhere" across terminal, desktop, mobile, Slack (1:10:21) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: ... AI agents and data integrity ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-agents-data-integrity.md): recommends one always-on data agent everyone calls over many agents that each need current semantics; alternative is an MCP server plus shared rules and skills (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why most AI products fail: Lessons from 50+ AI deployments](sources/lenny-podcast-reganti-badam-ai-deployments.md): supervisor plus sub-agents works; functional peer-to-peer multi-agent designs are "misunderstood" (1:01:34) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Skills explained](sources/howiai-claire-vo-claude-skills-explained.md): skills invoked by inference from context with no magic word (pasting a changelog triggered the newsletter skill) (20:15) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Not all AI agents are created equal](sources/lenny-newsletter-three-agent-categories.md): "A single orchestrator agent ... is usually simpler and more effective until true cross-team coordination becomes unavoidable"; multi-agent used by "fewer than 5% to 10%" of teams (consultant estimate) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Marily Nika: new PM toolkit](sources/howiai-marily-nika-pm-toolkit.md): "tool hopping" across five specialised apps with copy-paste hand-offs, which she expects a single tool to replace (9:32, 38:41) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Webinar Q&A: How Fin 3x'd R&D output in 16 months](sources/ideas-fin-webinar-qa-3x-rd-output.md): Claude Code is the single primary tool with "hundreds of skills"; Codex used only in review/approval; open tool policy dropped (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## skill-standards: Skill standards
(Section created by research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy; please refine.)
- [AI steering experiments (Stripe)](sources/stripe-ai-steering-experiments.md): modular, progressively disclosed skills beat a monolithic skill by ~10% on Stripe's eval suite and used fewer tokens (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)

- [Agent Skills specification (agentskills.io)](sources/agentskills-specification.md): six frontmatter fields (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools); SKILL.md + scripts/references/assets; ~100-token metadata, <5000-token body; no spec for triggering, versioning or sandboxing (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills](sources/anthropic-engineering-equipping-agents-agent-skills.md): origin of the format (2025-10-16); progressive disclosure, bundled scripts, "build skills from evaluations" (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Extend Claude with skills (Claude Code docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-skills-docs.md): skills and commands merged; `context: fork` runs a skill as a subagent (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Build skills (ChatGPT and Codex docs)](sources/openai-codex-skills-docs.md): Codex follows the open standard; 2% context budget for the skill list; "prefer instructions over scripts" (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AGENTS.md](sources/agentsmd-agents-md.md): schema-free repo instruction file, nearest file wins; 60k+ repos claimed (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Linux Foundation: Agentic AI Foundation](sources/linuxfoundation-agentic-ai-foundation.md): MCP, goose and AGENTS.md under neutral governance since 2025-12-09; SKILL.md governance not confirmed (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AGENTS.md outperforms skills in our agent evals](sources/vercel-agents-md-outperforms-skills.md): skill never invoked in 56% of cases; 53% baseline = 53% default skill; 79% with instruction; 100% AGENTS.md index (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [SkillsBench](sources/arxiv-skillsbench.md): curated skills +16.2pp avg but 16 of 84 tasks worse; self-generated -1.3pp; 2-3 skills best (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Evaluating AGENTS.md](sources/arxiv-evaluating-agents-md.md): context files reduced success and raised cost 20%+ (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Skills Open Standard: portable SKILL.md](sources/danielvaughan-agent-skills-open-standard-portable.md): no backward-compatibility guarantees or formal versioning (anecdote). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [About agent skills (GitHub Copilot docs)](sources/github-copilot-agent-skills-docs.md): Copilot reads .github/.claude/.agents skills; org-level skills not covered (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Gemini CLI and OpenCode skills support](sources/gemini-cli-and-opencode-skills-support.md): same SKILL.md; unknown frontmatter ignored (first-party via search summaries). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [How Blank Metal, a lean professional services firm, runs on Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-blank-metal-cowork.md): anything packaged as a reusable skill "gets shared across the org"; internal skills target friction points (first answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Brainlabs gave 1k+ marketers at its media agency an AI coworker with Claude Cowork and skills](sources/claude-customers-brainlabs-cowork-skills.md): an org-wide skills guideline, a designated owner who reviews and approves every change, and a Claude "skills auditor" that flags duplication, overlapping instructions and token inefficiency; the analytics API is used to see... - [How Miro's champions run their week with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-miro-champions.md): before a skill rolls out team-wide it gets a quality pass: does it cite sources, respect data boundaries, conflict with another skill; every factual claim must link to its source (Hostetler, "keep quality and trust high").
