- [How Vercel built an ecosystem on the open skills standard](sources/claude-customers-vercel-skills-ecosystem.md): skills.sh built on the open Skills spec; a Cloudflare-proposed `/.well-known/skills` URL-discovery convention was adopted into the `npx skills` installer and "move[d] up the official spec progression" (open standard answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop](sources/claude-fold-subagents-into-main-loop.md): per-team DRIs own skills, ship them with evals; /skill-creator and /skill-doctor audit, deduplicate and prune by cost and usage (section "Skills"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A complete guide to building skills for Claude](sources/claude-guide-building-skills.md): skill = folder with required `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter `name` + `description` under 1024 chars) plus optional `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`; Agent Skills published as an open standard "like MCP" (Fundamentals;... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Marketplace: plugins and connectors, products and agents, and service partners](sources/claude-marketplace.md): builders publish connectors or plugins using MCP and Agent Skills, described as "open standards pioneered by Anthropic" ("For builders and partners"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building agents that reach production systems with MCP](sources/claude-mcp-production-patterns.md): skills teach procedure, MCP gives access; data plugin for Cowork = 10 skills + 8 MCP servers (section "Pairing MCP servers with skills"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Improving skill-creator: Test, measure, and refine Agent Skills](sources/claude-skill-creator-evals.md): two kinds of skill: capability uplift vs encoded preference (e.g. NDA review against set criteria, weekly updates drafted from several MCPs) ("Two kinds of skills"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Skills explained: How Skills compares to prompts, Projects, MCP, and subagents](sources/claude-skills-explained.md): skills are folders of instructions, scripts and resources with progressive disclosure: metadata about 100 tokens, full instructions under 5k tokens, bundled files only as needed ("What are Skills?"). - [Building verification loops in Claude Code with skills](sources/claude-verification-loops-skills.md): example SKILL.md with `name`, `description` (stating when to use) and `allowed-tools` frontmatter; embedding only works on skills you control, so plugin-managed skills are wrapped by chaining instead ("Embedded"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude](sources/claude-warp-self-improving-agents.md): skills as plain files with progressive disclosure and bundled scripts; tips: principles not rules, explain the why, keep skills small (section "How to write self-improving skills"). (research-claude-resources-articles)

- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): a tool is something an agent calls; a skill is something it reads (Webflow skills for Codex and ChatGPT) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use Claude Routines at work - a Guide for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-routines-for-product-teams.md): process in SKILL.md and voice in a separate brand file, reused by every routine that writes customer-facing text (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical Agent Skills for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-practical-agent-skills.md): recaps SKILL.md as three layers (a header for selection, the instructions, and files loaded only when needed). Skills load automatically, with no explicit call (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [A designer's guide to Cursor (Elizabeth Lin)](sources/howiai-elizabeth-lin-designers-guide-cursor.md): Cursor Rules to carry setup and taste between prototyping sessions (show notes) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## skill-supply-chain-security: Skill supply chain security
Third-party skills and plugins carry malware, prompt-injection and credential risks; whether a private marketplace with review is needed.
- [Plugin security and trust](sources/anthropic-claude-code-plugin-security.md): plugin hooks/monitors/MCP run outside the sandbox with user privileges (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [ToxicSkills (Snyk)](sources/snyk-toxicskills-study.md): 3,984 skills: 36.82% any issue, 13.4% critical, 76 malicious (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [MalSkills](sources/arxiv-malskills.md): 400 confirmed malicious of 150,108 skills across 7 registries (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [ClawHavoc](sources/thehackernews-clawhavoc-341-malicious-skills.md): 341 of 2,857 ClawHub skills malicious (independent reporting). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CSA: agent context poisoning](sources/csa-skill-md-context-poisoning.md): scanners miss natural-language payloads; hidden Unicode tags (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent skills at enterprise scale](sources/paypal-agent-skills-at-enterprise-scale.md): fail-closed validation + human review. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vercel skills](sources/vercel-skills-sh-open-skills-ecosystem.md): public directory scanned by Snyk. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Customize Claude Code with mods in TypeScript](sources/claude-code-mods.md): mods "aren't sandboxed" and run with Claude Code's access; install only from trusted sources (opening). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Stripe deploys Claude Code to 1,370 engineers with zero-configuration enterprise rollout](sources/claude-customers-stripe-claude-code-rollout.md): random JavaScript packages on corporate laptops were unacceptable; the signed binary bypassed the npm dependency chain ("Claude Code enables zero-friction adoption"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Marketplace: plugins and connectors, products and agents, and service partners](sources/claude-marketplace.md): no listing review, signing, permissions or admin allow-listing is described; the absence is the finding. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Practical Agent Skills for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-practical-agent-skills.md): a popular PM newsletter offers one download bundling skills from 10 repos, one of them a collection of 1,000+ skills, with no warning about review, pinning or scanning (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Community Wisdom: Vibe coding as a team sport](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-vibe-coding-team-sport.md): supply-chain attacks are "a huge risk right now when everyone is building software on their desktop"; vet dependencies, store credentials to limit exposure (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Guillermo Rauch: v0 Git workflow](sources/howiai-guillermo-rauch-v0-git-workflow.md): star ratings added so users can tell vetted skills; skills as prompt-injection vector (9:08, 10:26) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): install skills only from the official bundle or known developers; read SKILL.md first (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## skills-marketplace: A versioned skills marketplace with hidden Git
Skills as markdown in a Git repo, reviewed like code, with the VCS hidden from non-engineers behind publish. A concrete mechanism for sharing agent know-how.
- [How We Built Glass: Vibe Coding a Product Used by 700 People](sources/x-shanebuchan-how-we-built-glass.md): Dojo publish = branch + PR + review behind the scenes (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): Dojo plus the Sensei recommender (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): Agent Studio: domain owners build, test and monitor skills, custom Kai agents and tool selections, with usage and quality signals per asset, organised in 'areas' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): skill-creator turns a session into a skill; publish private or to an area; IDE-like draft editor; automatic improvement suggestions to authors (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Emily Glassberg Sands on Latent Space](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): pre-Kai GoLLM 'presets' (saved, shared prompts): hundreds created overnight (Oct 2025) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Plugin manifest reference](sources/anthropic-claude-code-plugins-reference.md): plugin = unit of distribution; version pinning, dependencies, userConfig. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Manage plugins for your organization](sources/anthropic-claude-code-plugins-org-management.md): org marketplace via managed settings, allow/block lists, release channels, analytics (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Sync your organization's plugins](sources/anthropic-claude-org-plugin-sync.md): private Git repo synced to claude.ai, Cowork and Claude Code (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

## spec-becomes-prototype-and-evals: The spec is replaced by prototype plus evals
Some teams swap the PRD for a problem statement, a working prototype and evals.
- [AI didn't write our SDK. It changed how we built it.](sources/stripe-ai-didnt-write-our-sdk.md): a two-day prototype moved a scope decision weeks earlier; agents draft specs reviewed as GitHub issues before implementation (~20 lint rules) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Protodash (How I AI, Owen Williams)](sources/howiai-stripe-protodash-owen-williams.md): engineers worked from a designer's prototype PR: 'just use the prototype as the source of truth' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [A conversation with Seth Hain about Epic's internal AI adoption](sources/claude-customers-epic-internal-adoption.md): the prototype went "beyond slides or written documentation" as the way to show what was wanted. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How League went all in on Claude in a regulated industry](sources/claude-customers-league.md): R&D runs on "bets" where a small team spends 2-3 weeks and returns a working prototype for the market; customer pitches use working demo agents instead of Figma or slides (Q&A final answer; case study "Half the cycle time"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Datadog built a "universal machine tool" for Claude Code](sources/claude-datadog-universal-machine-tool.md): "instead of producing application code, agents produce specifications"; the kernel verifies and deploys the system the spec describes, so there is no drift (§Temper). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): interactive click-through prototypes built by handing Claude assets and saying "make it work"; each artifact has a shareable link like a doc ("Giving Claude an HTML playground"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Design now stays on brand for daily work](sources/claude-design-on-brand.md): `/design-sync` pulls the design system so designs start from real components; a design hands off to Claude Code, which continues from the work rather than a screenshot; code can be turned into a live prototype ("Move between... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A field guide to Claude Fable 5: Finding your unknowns](sources/claude-fable-finding-unknowns.md): unknown knowns are found by throwaway HTML prototypes with fake data before wiring anything ("Brainstorms and prototypes"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Product management on the AI exponential](sources/claude-pm-on-the-ai-exponential.md): team replaced documentation-first with prototype-first; stand-ups replaced by demos; pro-tip to send a written spec to Claude Code and see if it builds it; Noah's plugins spec produced a near-production prototype that anchored... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Running an AI-native engineering org](sources/claude-running-ai-native-engineering-org.md): planning shifted "away from design docs toward discussions in PRs or prototypes"; few product reviews; prototype, put internal users on it, act on feedback (Planning). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Improving skill-creator: Test, measure, and refine Agent Skills](sources/claude-skill-creator-evals.md): "Looking ahead": a SKILL.md is an implementation plan; evals already describe the "what", and that description may eventually be the skill. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): the PRD is an intermediate step the agent writes; the screens are what goes to stakeholders (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [AI's third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers](sources/lenny-podcast-tara-seshan-persistent-coworkers.md): OpenAI's Codex/Work product lead: "mocks not docs, or prototypes not docs"; a long doc is no longer a signal of rigour; she still writes docs privately to think (55:04-56:37) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): 60-80% of what Anthropic's growth team ships has no PRD; "PRDs are just outdated"; he prototypes to articulate ideas (51:29) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Advanced evals: How to find (and fix) hidden AI failures in your product](sources/lenny-newsletter-advanced-evals-error-discovery.md): Lenny: guests argue "evals are the new PRDs"; nearly half of 25 PM openings he shared ask for eval-writing experience (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Why AI evals are the hottest new skill (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-hamel-shreya-evals.md): "evals are the new PRDs" (Lenny), qualified by Shankar: expectations surface only after reviewing data; PRDs remain but "it's going to change" (1:00:56-1:02:28) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Gumroad CEO's playbook to 40x his team's productivity (How I AI)](sources/howiai-gumroad-sahil-lavingia-v0-devin.md): v0 iteration "was kind of clarifying my spec"; final prompt pasted into Devin as the handoff (12:19-13:05) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

(research-claude-resources-articles)

- [Why LinkedIn is turning PMs into AI-powered "full stack builders"](sources/lenny-podcast-tomer-cohen-full-stack-builder.md): trust agent lists "vulnerabilities, what harm vectors" a spec introduces, grounded in LinkedIn-specific trust know-how (19:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Zapier's EA built an army of AI interns](sources/howiai-zapier-ea-cortney-hickey.md): a document review system checks drafts against the CEO's expectations "before formal reviews" (24:03, show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Shape Up (Ryan Singer)](sources/lenny-podcast-ryan-singer-shape-up.md): the "grumpy old plumber" engineer opens the code during shaping; a one-step fintech onboarding change had three bank-specific branches, found before green-light rather than in week four (50:42) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [25 proven tactics to accelerate AI adoption](sources/lenny-newsletter-25-ai-adoption-tactics.md): Ramp PMs "give any product spec to these personas and get instant feedback on what they're missing" (section 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic teams use Claude Code](sources/anthropic-how-teams-use-claude-code.md): product design maps error states and logic flows with Claude Code to find edge cases early; 'saves hours' later, unquantified. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## status-update-agents: Status updates and 'ask the org' Q&A as an agent job
Drafting weekly updates and answering launch/status questions from org context removes PM note-taking and follow-up work.

## svpg-four-risks: SVPG's four risks and role ownership

## synthetic-users-limits: Synthetic users and AI personas: limits
AI-simulated research participants are optimistic, shallow and uncritical; supplement, never replace, real users.
- [How to build a Persona Feature Tester with Claude Code and ElevenLabs](sources/departmentofproduct-persona-feature-tester.md): personas billed as "grounded in real world data" but built from mock data that Cowork generated; no check against real users (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Strategy Thought Partner](sources/departmentofproduct-strategy-thought-partner.md): the base app runs features past "data-grounded" synthetic personas, including voice calls, with no validation discussed (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): Askable reportedly builds a queryable model from real interviews to answer hypothetical market questions, presented with no caveat (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Advanced evals: How to find (and fix) hidden AI failures in your product](sources/lenny-newsletter-advanced-evals-error-discovery.md): synthetic queries from dimensions, one call per scenario for diversity; "synthetic data cannot replace real data" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Five proven prompt engineering techniques](sources/lenny-newsletter-prompt-engineering-techniques.md): 2024 PM guide recommends generating personas and "potential customer feedback" when lacking real user data, with no validity caveat (Tactic 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Cowork 101](sources/howiai-jj-englert-cowork-101.md): "sub-advisory board" of three persona sub-agents with fresh context reviews drafts; host suggests every PRD reviewed by simulated boss, eng partner, customer; no evidence of fidelity (30:04, 31:55) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [An AI state of the union (Simon Willison)](sources/lenny-podcast-simon-willison-state-of-ai.md): choosing among three cheap prototypes: "I don't have a confident answer"; AI-simulated users not "credible" vs a real person on Zoom (22:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [ChatGPT agent mode: the little helper (Michal Peled, HoneyBook)](sources/howiai-honeybook-michal-peled-personas.md): five research-derived custom-GPT personas used internally; claimed to represent "thousands of potential customers", never validated against real behaviour (38:40) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Marily Nika: new PM toolkit](sources/howiai-marily-nika-pm-toolkit.md): pro and against agents "debate at least 20 times" to derive the minimum feature set; not validated against real users (8:02) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [25 proven tactics to accelerate AI adoption](sources/lenny-newsletter-25-ai-adoption-tactics.md): Ramp AI personas loaded with user research review any spec for gaps; no accuracy or limits discussed (section 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Synthetic Replacements for Human Survey Data? The Perils of Large Language Models (Bisbee et al.)](sources/bisbee-synthetic-replacements-survey-data.md): persona-prompted LLM respondents show reduced variance and different regression estimates vs real respondents. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Synthetic Users: If, When, and How to Use AI-Generated 'Research'](sources/nngroup-synthetic-users.md): optimism bias, no priorities, uncritical concept approval; supplement but never replace real users. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence](sources/stanford-cheng-sycophantic-ai-science-2026.md): users rated sycophantic answers higher and trusted them more (2,405 participants; abstract via search) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## tacit-knowledge-capture: Capturing tacit knowledge from people for agents
How know-how that lives in people's heads (how the business works, which data to trust, design and architectural judgment) gets written down, verified and kept current so agents can use it: by passive mining of work exhaust, by experts curating docs, rules and skills, by interview-style elicitation, or by write-back from finished work. Bears on Geoff's hypothesis that a context-creation agent is needed.
- [How can we help everyone become a 10x engineer? (Stripe Sessions 2024)](sources/stripe-sessions-2024-10x-engineer-panel.md): Trailhead makes owners verify docs or they 'drift away and get archived'; the docs complaint dropped steeply in the next engineering survey (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): a 2013 Stripe engineer: once 'no one has all of the state in their heads anymore' Stripe wrote documents, then robots, and now AI 'can ingest all of this documentation that we'd written' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Protodash (How I AI, Owen Williams)](sources/howiai-stripe-protodash-owen-williams.md): a design manager encoded design-system judgment as agent rules over 18 months: 'I feel insane writing these rules, but ... once you've got them, it works' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [AI didn't write our SDK. It changed how we built it.](sources/stripe-ai-didnt-write-our-sdk.md): repo-local docs 'written for AI consumption' (principles, boundaries, anti-patterns) raised agent output and cut onboarding for humans (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Inside Stripe's Engineering Culture: Part 2](sources/pragmaticengineer-inside-stripe-engineering-culture-part-2.md): CEO- and CTO-led internal writing culture; 'vastly more people consume the writing than produce it' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Investing in Internal Documentation (First Round, David Nunez)](sources/firstround-nunez-internal-documentation.md): knowledge 'trapped in an early hire's head'; internal docs lose to external docs and to the to-do list unless built into career expectations (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's payment method factory](sources/stripe-payment-method-factory.md): planning agent interviews the engineer for context and writes it to a shared knowledge base; learning and decision logs feed prompt updates (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Latent Space, Emily Sands](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): canonical-dataset docs written by domain owners ('brute-forcing it with humans'); Sands did not yet trust an LLM to write them (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Agentic memory in Copilot](sources/github-blog-agentic-memory-copilot.md): write-back with verification: agents store memories with code citations, re-checked on read; A/B merge rate 83% to 90% (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [InterviewBot: LLM-led interviews](sources/arxiv-interviewbot-mllm-led-interviews.md): against interview agents as-is: LLM interviewers are 'acknowledgment-heavy but probe-light', 4.9% deepening probes in 428 turns (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Anthropic Interviewer](sources/anthropic-interviewer-launch.md): 1,250 AI-led interviews, 97.6% satisfied: scalable and liked, but it captures attitudes, not expertise (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Knowledge elicitation automation with LLMs](sources/swj-knowledge-elicitation-automation-llms.md): AI interviews were more efficient, but AI-built ontologies missed data and hallucinated (independent, weak) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Generative AI and the SECI model](sources/arxiv-uchihira-genai-seci-model.md): GenAI work on tacit knowledge is still 'fragmentary'; most GenAI KM handles explicit knowledge (independent position paper) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Scaling expertise with generative AI](sources/tandf-osullivan-scaling-expertise-genai.md): governance that needs persistent state can't be done by prompting alone; GenAI drifts and flatters (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Knowledge activation with curated skills](sources/arxiv-yahoo-knowledge-activation-skills.md): 87 curated skills saved 2.6 h/week; contribution barriers, authoring cost and unmeasured staleness (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [AI-generated table documentation](sources/databricks-ai-generated-table-documentation.md): agent drafts, owner accepts or edits: '>80%' of metadata updates AI-assisted (vendor claim) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Generative AI at Work](sources/nber-brynjolfsson-generative-ai-at-work.md): an assistant trained on top performers' work exhaust raised productivity 14% overall, 34% for novices, about 0 for experts (independent, causal) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [LLMs reduce public knowledge sharing](sources/pnas-nexus-llms-reduce-public-knowledge-sharing.md): Stack Overflow posting fell ~25% within six months of ChatGPT: people stop writing knowledge down once they can ask an AI (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Knowledge hiding meta-analysis](sources/ebr-knowledge-hiding-meta-analysis.md): 131 studies, 47,348 people: knowledge hiding is distinct from (uncorrelated with) sharing, so easier sharing won't fix it (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Copilot and works councils (Microsoft Inside Track)](sources/microsoft-insidetrack-copilot-works-councils.md): works councils objected to features that rank or monitor employees; staged rollout (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Resolution extraction from Slack vs tickets](sources/neurips-2025-resolution-extraction-slack-vs-tickets.md): knowledge mined from Slack is more relevant but noisier; needs high-precision filtering (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Expertise estimation from Slack](sources/arxiv-watanabe-expertise-estimation-slack.md): 'who knows what' inferred from 27k Slack messages had a best error of 21 points out of 100 (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Encoding Your Domain Expert (Spotify Vedder)](sources/spotify-engineering-vedder-context-layer.md): experts own clusters of datasets, vetted question-SQL pairs and docs; curators rejected 87.5% of examples auto-generated from query history as noise; clusters carry a health score (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Intercom Fin NPI](sources/intercom-fin-npi-agent-readiness.md): a feature counts as shipped only when the support agent can answer about it; a 'what we built' doc plus meeting notes go to an agent that drafts and tests content (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Uber Agentic Pods (CTO post)](sources/x-praveen-uber-agentic-pods.md): engineers shadow domain experts for two days before building, because workflows can't be automated 'by looking at process diagrams or documentation' (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Internal AI tools for non-engineers (DoP PDF)](sources/departmentofproduct-internal-ai-tools-for-non-engineers.md): a 15-company table; three rows (Spotify, Intercom, Uber) are capture mechanisms (independent summary) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How Brainlabs gave 1k+ marketers at its media agency an AI coworker with Claude Cowork and skills](sources/claude-customers-brainlabs-cowork-skills.md): an SEO audit skill "refined across thousands of iterations" on a context layer from a decade of agency work, so audit quality no longer depends on which strategist runs it (sections "An authoring layer", "The outcome"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Carvana turns Slack alerts into production fixes with Claude Tag](sources/claude-customers-carvana-claude-tag.md): release-baseline comparison logic kept as a skill in the team repo with runbooks, so senior engineers' knowledge is version-controlled (alert section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Deploying Claude across your organization: How Anthropic uses Cowork](sources/claude-guide-deploying-cowork-across-org.md): skills turn "tribal knowledge" into organizational infrastructure; the Legal plugin was built in an afternoon from existing memos, risk frameworks and policy docs (ch. 2 "Scale"; ch. 6 "Legal"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How healthcare organizations use Claude Tag](sources/claude-tag-healthcare-human-agent-teams.md): Medallion's undocumented payer rules move from a few domain experts into a channel where Tag answers from past expert responses and tags an expert when not confident, whose answer then informs future ones (Medallion section). - [Building verification loops in Claude Code with skills](sources/claude-verification-loops-skills.md): "write down everything that you find yourself doing every time", then encode it as a skill; skill-creator can interview the user to draft it ("Writing verification loops"; "Make it a skill"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Why Semantic Data Layers matter](sources/departmentofproduct-semantic-data-layers.md): LLM-written metric definitions failed at Anthropic; the rule became "AI drafts, a named human owns the definition". (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Community Wisdom: Evaluating startup equity ... MCPs vs. CLIs ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-knowledge-graph-mcp-cli.md): knowledge captured as a by-product of workflows (including logs of accepted vs corrected outputs) rather than a separate documentation task (Thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya](sources/lenny-podcast-anish-acharya-company-loops.md): Kavak's per-customer agent calls a human when stuck; the human coaches it and the traces are captured so "the next time it shouldn't have to call you" (18:50, second-hand) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [I gave Claude Code our entire codebase | Al Chen](sources/howiai-galileo-al-chen-codebase-context.md): "customer quirks" Confluence page per enterprise customer feeds a `/dpl` command; decisions in meetings and hallway talk stay unqueryable (13:17, 22:01) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Zapier's CEO shares his personal AI stack](sources/howiai-zapier-wade-foster-ai-stack.md): a recorder prompt over a year of meetings extracts the "unspoken company culture handbook", which then feeds hiring rubrics (7:31-10:35) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Product manager is an unfair role. So work unfairly.](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-unfair-role.md): dictation transfers PM head-context to LLMs; "product scrapbooking" database of evidence by swim lane (sections 5-6) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers (Elizabeth Stone)](sources/lenny-podcast-elizabeth-stone-netflix-systems-thinkers.md): knowledge once held by "experts who were here for 20 years and saw every experiment" is now queryable by any function (9:52) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Using AI to accelerate a team's velocity](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-team-velocity.md): async structured prompts to stakeholders before an offsite, AI finds "patterns and contradictions"; 3 days became 1.5 (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How custom GPTs can make you a better manager | Hilary Gridley](sources/howiai-whoop-gridley-custom-gpts.md): leader reverse-engineers her decision criteria into rubrics and gives the team GPTs that review like her (show notes; 02:42-21:23) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why most AI products fail: Lessons from 50+ AI deployments](sources/lenny-podcast-reganti-badam-ai-deployments.md): human support agents know a 2019 category node is dead; agents need that undocumented context (52:46) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The design process is dead: Jenny Wen](sources/lenny-podcast-jenny-wen-design-process-dead.md): Cowork over a folder of years of personal and interview notes drafted a rubric for assessing design craft (1:14:28) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to become a supermanager with AI](sources/lenny-newsletter-hilary-gridley-supermanager.md): reverse-engineer a manager's standard from before/after examples into a prompt; "if you're good at teaching people ... you're also extremely well suited to teaching a robot" (Strategy 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Braintrust uses AI agents, evals, and CI](sources/howiai-braintrust-ankur-goyal-evals.md): a designer's taste turned into a repeatable scoring function so quality scales beyond one person (chapter 32:09; show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: speeding up discovery in a big org](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-discovery-big-org.md): decisions, constraints and the "why" live with people and leave with them; capture them durably (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Engineers are becoming sorcerers (Sherwin Wu, OpenAI)](sources/lenny-podcast-sherwin-wu-openai-codex.md): agent failures are "usually a problem with context"; the fix is to encode tribal knowledge into the repo via .md files, skills and code structure; a no-escape-hatch 100% Codex team surfaces these gaps (12:44-14:16) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Top Contributors Summer 2026 (product engineers pilot)](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-product-engineers-pilot.md): the curator asks what is lost when a leader's judgment is distributed through an AI operating system rather than conversation (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Building without clear PM requirements](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-building-without-pm-requirements.md): 2-month experiment pairing 5 engineers with Support/Success/Ops SMEs and a vision doc: fast prototypes, but SMEs stuck on "fix this specific issue" (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## task-context-isolation: Isolation by task context, not only by user permission
Limiting what a session may combine based on the task (e.g. never two customers' data in one analysis), even when the user could access each separately. Matters for trust/privacy defaults of shared or discoverable sessions.
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): "you shouldn't combine data from two unrelated customer contexts in a single analysis"; the boundary is "what should this task be allowed to view given this context?" (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): tool policies stop sensitive HR data being written to a Stripe-wide doc without banning tools (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How Stripe Built a new Internal AI Knowledge Platform (Department of Product)](sources/departmentofproduct-stripe-kai.md): analogous combination guardrails (two candidates, two patients, performance plus pay) that must be enforced at infrastructure or session level, not by skill owners (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How League went all in on Claude in a regulated industry](sources/claude-customers-league.md): patient data is kept in a separate environment Claude has no access to; agents had strict limits while controls were put in place (case study, "The solution"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building agents that reach production systems with MCP](sources/claude-mcp-production-patterns.md): tool search cuts tool-definition tokens 85%+; programmatic tool calling about 37% fewer tokens on complex workflows (section "Making MCP clients more context-efficient"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Multi-agent coordination patterns: Five approaches and when to use them](sources/claude-multi-agent-coordination-patterns.md): recommends "context-centric decomposition" (split by what context each agent needs, not by type of work); Claude Code subagents each run in their own context window and return distilled findings (Pattern 2; "Choosing and... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Skills explained: How Skills compares to prompts, Projects, MCP, and subagents](sources/claude-skills-explained.md): subagents have their own context window, system prompt and tool permissions; example read-only code-reviewer subagent (Read, Grep, Glob, no Write/Edit). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](sources/claude-steering-claude-code.md): subagents run in a fresh context and return only their final message; they can nest up to five levels and dynamic workflows orchestrate tens to hundreds of background agents (Subagents). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The coming AI security crisis | Sander Schulhoff](sources/lenny-podcast-sander-schulhoff-ai-security.md): CAMEL grants only the permissions a request needs (read-only for a summary), blocking injected sends; fails when one request combines reading untrusted data with sending (1:04:24-1:07:28) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How OpenAI uses ChatGPT Sites (Kath Korevec)](sources/howiai-openai-korevec-chatgpt-sites.md): the same site shows team-specific content depending on which Slack channels the viewer comes from (8:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [5 OpenClaw agents run my home (Jesse Genet)](sources/howiai-jesse-genet-openclaw-agents.md): each role agent on its own Mac Mini with data partitioned by machine (show notes, 18:19) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): isolated machine; anyone who can message the bot can instruct it, so no group chats; injection via email and web (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to turn your AI into a world-class designer](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-world-class-designer.md): critic invoked "in a fresh context, with just the screenshot, not the code ... or earlier iterations/critiques" because the builder "isn't objective" (Technique 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-claire-vo-openclaw.md): each agent gets "his own quiet room" with only its lane's context (44:18) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## vendor-claims-vs-independent-evidence: Vendor claims dominate; independent evidence is rare
Most evidence on PM agents is vendor marketing or self-reported; controlled or independent evaluations are almost absent. Weigh sources accordingly.
- [River threads jump to 121,804 (Dealroom)](sources/dealroom-river-threads-121804.md): thread volume alone does not prove productivity or quality; no independent impact measure (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify: Building River (ZenML)](sources/zenml-llmops-shopify-river-durable-infrastructure.md): no models, cost, error rates or baselines disclosed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Building a Public AI Agent Workspace (ZenML)](sources/zenml-llmops-shopify-river-public-workspace.md): security and permission model "aren't described"; the 23% unmerged are not discussed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Inside Shopify's software factory (Port)](sources/port-software-factories-shopify.md): "1 in 8" has no definition of "coauthored"; best detail comes from press and VC interviews, not the blog (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's River shows why agent context costs more (Magica)](sources/magica-shopify-river-agent-context-cost.md): no like-for-like comparison against private agents; migration and Aquifer cost undisclosed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [AI SLOPCAST #9](sources/oleg-guru-ai-slopcast-shopify-river-lehrwerkstatt.md): only positive metrics; review load on seniors unreported (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lutke: River Now Writes Half (Podcast Alpha)](sources/podcastalpha-tobi-lutke-river-half-of-prs.md): "founder-stated, not audited"; headline overstates Tobi's "up to about 50%... created out of conversations" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How to Make AI Work Visible (MindStudio)](sources/mindstudio-make-ai-work-visible-shopify-river.md): loose restatement used as a product pitch (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Stripe Got 83% of Staff Using One AI Agent. Don't Copy Its Sales Numbers.](sources/aifounders-stripe-kai-dont-copy-sales-numbers.md): independent critique: Kai's +39% deals compares the same sellers' Kai and non-Kai weeks; early adopters are the best sellers; cause open (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Sharadh Krishnamurthy LinkedIn Kai launch post](sources/linkedin-sharadhk-kai-launch-post.md): Kai usage stated as 80% weekly / 20,000+ sessions a day (LinkedIn), 83% (blog), 86%+ (podcast), '>60k sessions' (LangChain): inconsistent bases (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Eight trends defining how software gets built in 2026](sources/claude-2026-agentic-coding-trends.md): every "In practice" box is a customer claim (TELUS 500,000 hours, Fountain 50% faster screening, Rakuten 7-hour run); no method given (all chapters). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The 2026 State of AI Agents Report](sources/claude-2026-state-of-ai-agents.md): survey commissioned and published by Anthropic; customer case results (Novo Nordisk, L'Oreal, eSentire etc.) are customer claims, unaudited (ch. 5). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Measure Claude Code's impact with contribution metrics](sources/claude-code-contribution-metrics.md): Anthropic reports a 67% increase in PRs merged per engineer per day internally and 70-90% of code written with Claude Code assistance, method not given ("How we're shipping at Anthropic"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Atlassian builds AI agents teams can trust with Claude and Google Cloud](sources/claude-customers-atlassian-trusted-agents.md): 5 million+ agent executions per month and "millions" of Rovo Chat users are vendor figures; no quality or trust metrics despite trust being the headline. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Gumroad's customer support team ships code with Claude](sources/claude-customers-gumroad-support-ships-code.md): "300% increase" is defined as "shipping 4 commits in the time it took to ship 1", a throughput proxy, not an outcome measure (Driving impressive business results). (research-claude-resources-articles)

## work-structure-spectrum: Work structure spectrum (unstructured exploration to task-specific workflow)
Whether a piece of work wants a flexible general harness or a constrained task-specific agent or workflow depends on a handful of properties (step predictability, verifiability, repeatability, error cost, audit need, tacit context), and most real systems are hybrids. Tests Geoff's hypothesis; see tasks/research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy/track-6-work-structure-fit.md.
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): coding work is uniform enough for one agent architecture; knowledge work needs different tools, data, outputs and definitions of done per task (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Production-grade AI agents for financial compliance: Lessons from Stripe](sources/aws-stripe-compliance-agents.md): compliance review decomposed into a DAG of bite-sized, quality-tested sub-questions; the review tool, not an LLM, orchestrates (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's payment method factory](sources/stripe-payment-method-factory.md): 'although an LLM can orchestrate a workflow, predictable coordination is better implemented in code' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Building effective agents](sources/anthropic-building-effective-agents.md): first-party: workflows (predefined paths) for well-defined tasks, agents for open-ended ones; start simple (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How to think about agent frameworks](sources/langchain-how-to-think-about-agent-frameworks.md): vendor: a spectrum of "how agentic", production systems mix both (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Choose a design pattern for your agentic AI system](sources/google-cloud-choose-design-pattern-agentic-ai.md): vendor: decision table from task traits to pattern; structured single-call work needs no agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Best practices for Claude Code](sources/anthropic-claude-code-best-practices.md): first-party: structure is added on demand inside one harness; exploratory tasks may skip planning (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot coding agents](sources/stripe-minions-one-shot-coding-agents.md): first-party: deterministic nodes wrapped around an agentic core for repeatable engineering work (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Orchestrating AI Code Review at scale](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): first-party: standardised review as coordinator plus narrow specialists, risk-tiered (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Measuring Agents in Production](sources/arxiv-measuring-agents-in-production.md): independent: deployed agents are short-horizon and human-checked (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Future of Work with AI Agents](sources/arxiv-future-of-work-with-ai-agents.md): independent: Human Agency Scale H1-H5 as a worker-desire axis (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [METR early-2025 developer RCT](sources/metr-early-2025-experienced-developer-rct.md): independent: tacit-context, high-standard work saw slowdown with a general assistant (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Anthropic Economic Index, January 2026](sources/anthropic-economic-index-2026-01.md): first-party: Claude.ai 52% augmentation; API about 75% automation (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ask HN: non-coding workflows](sources/hn-ask-claude-code-non-coding-workflows.md): anecdote: unstructured personal knowledge work runs in a general coding harness with folder structure (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Boris Cherny summary (Traces)](sources/traces-boris-cherny-light-cone-summary.md): second-hand counter-evidence: model-compensating structure is temporary (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Introducing dynamic workflows](sources/claude-code-dynamic-workflows.md): structure is generated per task by the model rather than predefined; a customer quote places it "between firing off a single subagent and building out a full agent team" (intro; quotes). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How people are using Claude Cowork](sources/claude-how-people-use-cowork.md): the top categories are connective, cross-role work (assembling scattered updates, onboarding checklists, reconciling spreadsheets, decks) rather than a role's core judgement work ("How knowledge workers are using AI"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): Stripe Minions blueprints and GitHub Copilot's mandatory CodeQL and secret scanning as "mix AI steps with fixed rules" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Perplexity's new Computer...](sources/departmentofproduct-perplexity-computer.md): outcome-first planning with sub-agents, plus persistent background workers on triggers that run "indefinitely" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Identify Opportunities for AI Automation](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-automation-opportunities.md): scores each task 1-3 on safety, volume and verifiability, giving three outcomes: automate now, AI assistant, or not ready. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Agentic Workflows Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agentic-workflows-explained.md): deterministic automation vs non-deterministic agentic workflow as the first mental model, with a seven-part anatomy. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use /loops, /goals and other Powerful Slash Commands as a Non-Engineer](sources/departmentofproduct-loops-goals-slash-commands.md): steps of structure inside one harness: a prompt, then a goal (a stated "done" condition), then a loop that calls a reusable command file (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Claude Cowork as a Competitive Intelligence System](sources/departmentofproduct-cowork-competitive-intelligence.md): a user-defined phrase ("Run the intel workflow") reruns the whole chain, adding structure on demand inside a general agent (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Strategy Thought Partner](sources/departmentofproduct-strategy-thought-partner.md): product frameworks supply the structure. A recommender picks 3, then the chosen framework scripts a step-by-step sparring conversation (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How we restructured Airtable's entire org for AI | Howie Liu](sources/lenny-podcast-howie-liu-airtable-reorg.md): reorg into a "fast thinking" AI Platform group shipping near-weekly and a "slow thinking" group for deliberate infrastructure bets (21:38) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why every company now needs to think and operate like a lab team | Josh Woodward](sources/lenny-podcast-josh-woodward-labs-team.md): Labs stages encoded as zero-to-one, one-to-ten, ten-to-100, with different goals and people; 50-100 day milestones (46:25) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of ChatGPT ... | Tibo Sottiaux](sources/lenny-podcast-sottiaux-chatgpt-dots.md): one primary Dot first; later role-specific Dots for work big enough to fill an agent (e.g. monitoring Twitter) (10:55) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: prototypes and release comms](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-prototypes-release-comms.md): "script the stable stuff and creative stuff in the slash command" for a weekly release-notes job (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What a harness is and how to build one with Claude Agent SDK](sources/howiai-claire-vo-agent-sdk-harness.md): custom harness reserved for "any repetitive, structured workflow" (bug triage), general harness for the rest (show notes) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Not all AI agents are created equal](sources/lenny-newsletter-three-agent-categories.md): three types with fit tests: deterministic flow (<15-20 branches, 60-70% of opportunities), reasoning agent (25-30%), multi-agent; Claude Code is layered: ReAct loop plus deterministic hooks plus isolated sub-agents (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How top PMs increase their leverage with AI](sources/lenny-newsletter-pm-leverage-ladders.md): three ladders (personal, product, systems) of three rungs; "Not every task ... demands that you move up to the highest rung" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Felix Rieseberg (Cowork)](sources/howiai-felix-rieseberg-cowork.md): "go one abstraction layer up": stop entering data, have the agent find it, then ask how the system keeps itself current (15:45-18:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How this PM uses MCPs to automate (How I AI)](sources/howiai-zapier-reid-robinson-mcp-pm-workflows.md): agentic instructions vs deterministic Zap for the same CRM job; slow (7-minute) lookups go in deterministic workflows because MCP calls "can't take that long" (15:26-17:02) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What is a Jira space (formerly project)](sources/atlassian-jira-space-definition.md): team-managed (each team controls its own config) vs company-managed (admin-standardised) is a built-in structured-vs-flexible dial. (user-story-mapping)
- [What is a Confluence space](sources/atlassian-confluence-space-definition.md): a space is a loose knowledge container (knowledge base, launch or campaign space) with no enforced artifact types. (user-story-mapping)
- [What is an idea (Jira Product Discovery docs)](sources/atlassian-jira-product-discovery-ideas.md): connection fields (Premium) link ideas without imposing a fixed hierarchy. (user-story-mapping)
- [Working with databases (Notion API docs)](sources/notion-api-databases-data-sources.md): databases give typed structure, pages give free-form body, in the same object. (user-story-mapping)
- [Projects (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-projects.md): strong opinionated structure (one issue in one project; lead team sets statuses). (user-story-mapping)
- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-initiatives.md): initiative > project > issue, with team-led sub-initiatives rolling up to company goals. (user-story-mapping)
- [Add features to your hierarchy (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-product-hierarchy.md): Hierarchy: Product > Component > Feature > Subfeature. Features can be imported from spreadsheet, Jira or Zapier. (user-story-mapping)
- [About Projects (GitHub Docs)](sources/github-docs-about-projects.md): items are issues, PRs or draft issues with up to 50 custom fields; table, board and roadmap views. (user-story-mapping)
